modules.title: Charge balancing for polynomials
modules.doc:
A polynomial invariant under a phase rotation of charged variables has only charge-balanced terms.

## i. Overview

If the variables of a polynomial carry charges under a phase (here a single element `c` of infinite
order), then invariance under the simultaneous phase rotation `Xᵢ ↦ c^{wᵢ} Xᵢ` forces every
monomial to be *charge balanced* (net charge zero). This is the algebraic content of the statement
that a gauge invariant potential, restricted to a slice on which the gauge torus acts diagonally,
can only contain charge-balanced monomials.

## ii. Key results

- `MvPolynomial.coeff_aeval_diag` : rescaling each variable `Xᵢ` by a constant `d i` multiplies the
  coefficient of a monomial by the corresponding product of the `d i`.
- `MvPolynomial.coeff_eq_zero_of_charge_ne_zero` : charge balancing, a polynomial invariant under
  the phase rotation has vanishing coefficients on monomials of nonzero net charge.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Rescaling the variables
- B. Charge balancing

## iv. References

* None.

## B. Charge balancing

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.coeff_aeval_diag
declarations.doc:
Rescaling each variable `Xᵢ` by a constant `d i` multiplies the coefficient of the monomial `m`
by `∏ᵢ (d i) ^ (m i)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma coeff_aeval_diag {σ R : Type*} [CommRing R] (d : σ → R) (f : MvPolynomial σ R)
    (m : σ →₀ ℕ) :
    (aeval (fun i => C (d i) * X i) f).coeff m = (m.prod fun i k => d i ^ k) * f.coeff m

declarations.name: MvPolynomial.coeff_eq_zero_of_charge_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
**Charge balancing.** If each variable `Xᵢ` carries an integer charge `w i`, `c` is a phase of
infinite order, and the polynomial `f` is invariant under the charge rotation
`Xᵢ ↦ c^{wᵢ} Xᵢ`, then every monomial with nonzero net charge has vanishing coefficient.

modules.title: The effective potential of the two Higgs doublet model
modules.doc:
Effective potentials of the 2HDM, their gauge invariance, and their maximum mass dimension.

## i. Overview

An *effective potential* of the two Higgs doublet model is a real-valued function
`V : TwoHiggsDoublet → ℝ` of the field configuration. This file introduces the two physical
properties of such a potential used when expressing it through the gauge-invariant bilinears:

* `IsInvariant V` — invariance under the global gauge group, and
* `HasMaxMassDimLE V n` — being a polynomial in the field components of mass dimension `≤ n`.

## ii. Key results

* `EffectivePotential` — the type of effective potentials.
* `IsInvariant` — gauge invariance of a potential.
* `HasMaxMassDimLE` — being a bounded-degree polynomial in the field components.
* `HasMaxMassDimLE.exists_comp_linear_poly` — a polynomial potential, restricted along any
  real-linear parametrisation of configurations, is a polynomial in the parameters.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The effective potential and its gauge invariance
- B. Maximum mass dimension

## iv. References

* None.

## B. Maximum mass dimension

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential
declarations.doc: A general potential of the Higgs field.
declarations.statement: abbrev EffectivePotential : Type

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.IsInvariant
declarations.doc:
The proposition that the general potential is invariant under
the global action of the gauge group.
declarations.statement: def IsInvariant (V : EffectivePotential) : Prop

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.HasMaxMassDimLE
declarations.doc:
The proposition that the potential `V` has a maximum mass dimension
less then or equal to `n` - also implying it is a polynomial.
declarations.statement: def HasMaxMassDimLE (V : EffectivePotential) (n : ℕ) : Prop

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.HasMaxMassDimLE.exists_comp_linear_poly
declarations.doc:
A polynomial potential, restricted along any real-linear parametrisation `L` of field
configurations, is a genuine polynomial in the parameters. This is the bookkeeping that lets the
potential be evaluated on the field components of a gauge slice.
declarations.statement:
lemma HasMaxMassDimLE.exists_comp_linear_poly {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ}
    (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (L : (ι → ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] TwoHiggsDoublet) :
    ∃ P : MvPolynomial ι ℝ, ∀ a : ι → ℝ, V (L a) = P.eval a

modules.title: The gauge slice and the hypercharges of the doublet components
modules.doc:
The gauge slice of 2HDM configurations and the gauge-torus phases acting on it.

## i. Overview

After using `SU(2)` to align the first doublet with the second axis, a configuration lies on the
*gauge slice* `sliceHiggs z w₀ w₁ = ⟨(0, z), (w₁, w₀)⟩`. The gauge torus acts on the
three surviving components `z = Φ1₁`, `w₀ = Φ2₁`, `w₁ = Φ2₀` by their hypercharges:

* the Cartan phase `gaugeCartan ā` multiplies the components `z, w₀` along `Φ1` by `a` (and
  conjugates the would-be charged component of `Φ1`, which vanishes here), giving
  `(z, w₀, w₁) ↦ (a z, a w₀, ā w₁)`;
* the residual electromagnetic `U(1)` (`electromagnetismU1 c`) multiplies the charged component
  `w₁` by `c⁶`, giving `(z, w₀, w₁) ↦ (z, w₀, c⁶ w₁)`.

These two phase rotations are the source of the charge balancing of the effective potential.

## ii. Key results

- `TwoHiggsDoublet.sliceHiggs` : the gauge slice configuration `⟨(0, z), (w₁, w₀)⟩`.
- `TwoHiggsDoublet.sliceR` : the slice as a real-linear map from six real field parameters.
- `TwoHiggsDoublet.gaugeCartan_smul_sliceHiggs` : the hypercharge action of the Cartan phase.
- `TwoHiggsDoublet.electromagnetismU1_smul_sliceHiggs` : the hypercharge action of the residual
  electromagnetic `U(1)`.
- `TwoHiggsDoublet.gaugeCartan_smul_sliceR` : the Cartan phase rotates the real parameters.
- `TwoHiggsDoublet.electromagnetismU1_smul_sliceR` : the residual `U(1)` rotates only the
  perpendicular parameter pair.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The slice configuration
- B. Hypercharge action on the slice
- C. Gauge action on the real parameters

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The slice configuration
## B. Hypercharge action on the slice
## C. Gauge action on the real parameters

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.sliceHiggs
declarations.doc:
The gauge slice configuration `⟨(0, z), (w₁, w₀)⟩`. It specialises to `repHiggs`
when the components take their real "canonical frame" values.
declarations.statement: def sliceHiggs (z w0 w1 : ℂ) : TwoHiggsDoublet

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.sliceHiggs_Φ1
declarations.statement: lemma sliceHiggs_Φ1 (z w0 w1 : ℂ) : (sliceHiggs z w0 w1).Φ1 = !₂[0, z]

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.sliceHiggs_Φ2
declarations.statement: lemma sliceHiggs_Φ2 (z w0 w1 : ℂ) : (sliceHiggs z w0 w1).Φ2 = !₂[w1, w0]

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.real_smul_fst
declarations.statement: lemma real_smul_fst (c : ℝ) (H : TwoHiggsDoublet) : (c • H).Φ1 = c • H.Φ1

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.real_smul_snd
declarations.statement: lemma real_smul_snd (c : ℝ) (H : TwoHiggsDoublet) : (c • H).Φ2 = c • H.Φ2

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.sliceR
declarations.doc:
The slice as a real-linear map from the six real field parameters
`(Re Φ1₁, Im Φ1₁, Re Φ2₁, Im Φ2₁, Re Φ2₀, Im Φ2₀)`.
declarations.statement: def sliceR : (Fin 6 → ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] TwoHiggsDoublet

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.sliceR_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma sliceR_apply (a : Fin 6 → ℝ) :
    sliceR a = sliceHiggs (↑(a 0) + Complex.I * ↑(a 1)) (↑(a 2) + Complex.I * ↑(a 3))
      (↑(a 4) + Complex.I * ↑(a 5))

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.repHiggs_eq_sliceHiggs
declarations.doc: The representative family is the real slice.
declarations.statement:
lemma repHiggs_eq_sliceHiggs (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    repHiggs X = sliceHiggs (X 0) ((X 1 : ℂ) + Complex.I * (X 2 : ℂ)) (X 3)

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.gaugeCartan_smul_sliceHiggs
declarations.doc:
Hypercharge action of the Cartan phase `diag(ā, a)` on the slice: it multiplies the components
along `Φ1` by `a` and the charged component by `ā`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeCartan_smul_sliceHiggs (a : unitary ℂ) (z w0 w1 : ℂ) :
    GaugeGroupI.gaugeCartan (star a) • sliceHiggs z w0 w1
      = sliceHiggs ((a : ℂ) * z) ((a : ℂ) * w0) ((star a : ℂ) * w1)

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.electromagnetismU1_smul_sliceHiggs
declarations.doc:
Hypercharge action of the residual electromagnetic `U(1)` on the slice: it multiplies the
charged component by `c⁶` and leaves the components along `Φ1` fixed.
declarations.statement:
lemma electromagnetismU1_smul_sliceHiggs (c : unitary ℂ) (z w0 w1 : ℂ) :
    GaugeGroupI.electromagnetismU1 c • sliceHiggs z w0 w1
      = sliceHiggs z w0 ((c : ℂ) ^ 6 * w1)

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.cartanRotParam
declarations.doc:
The Cartan hypercharge phase `u`, transported to a rotation of the six real field parameters:
it phases the first-component pairs by `u` and the perpendicular pair by `ū`.
declarations.statement: def cartanRotParam (u : unitary ℂ) (a : Fin 6 → ℝ) : Fin 6 → ℝ

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.gaugeCartan_smul_sliceR
declarations.doc: Acting by the Cartan phase on a slice configuration is the same as rotating its parameters.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeCartan_smul_sliceR (u : unitary ℂ) (a : Fin 6 → ℝ) :
    GaugeGroupI.gaugeCartan (star u) • sliceR a = sliceR (cartanRotParam u a)

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.resRotParam
declarations.doc: The residual `U(1)` phase `c`, transported to a rotation of the perpendicular parameter pair.
declarations.statement: def resRotParam (c : unitary ℂ) (a : Fin 6 → ℝ) : Fin 6 → ℝ

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.electromagnetismU1_smul_sliceR
declarations.doc: Acting by the residual `U(1)` on a slice configuration rotates only the perpendicular pair.
declarations.statement:
lemma electromagnetismU1_smul_sliceR (c : unitary ℂ) (a : Fin 6 → ℝ) :
    GaugeGroupI.electromagnetismU1 c • sliceR a = sliceR (resRotParam c a)

modules.title: The gauge torus acting on Higgs vectors
modules.doc:
The SU(2) Cartan element diag(a, ā), which with the electromagnetic U(1) realises the gauge torus.

## i. Overview

The maximal torus of the gauge group acting on a Higgs doublet is the group of diagonal phase
rotations `diag(a, b)` of the two components. We realise it using

* the `SU(2)` Cartan element `diag(a, ā)` (constructed here as `gaugeCartan`), and
* the electromagnetic `U(1)` `electromagnetismU1`, whose action is `diag(μ, 1)`.

Together these realise an arbitrary diagonal phase `diag(a, b)`, which is the symmetry underlying
the charge-balancing ("Condition A") of the effective potential on the orbit representatives.

## ii. Key results

- `StandardModel.GaugeGroupI.gaugeCartan` : the Cartan `SU(2)` gauge element `diag(a, ā)`.
- `StandardModel.GaugeGroupI.gaugeCartan_smul_eq` : it acts on a Higgs vector as `diag(a, ā)`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Cartan gauge element

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The Cartan gauge element

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeGroupI.gaugeCartan
declarations.doc: The Cartan `SU(2)` gauge element `diag(a, ā)`, for `a` a phase.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gaugeCartan (a : unitary ℂ) : GaugeGroupI

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeGroupI.gaugeCartan_toU1
declarations.statement: lemma gaugeCartan_toU1 (a : unitary ℂ) : (gaugeCartan a).toU1 = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeGroupI.gaugeCartan_toSU2_coe
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeCartan_toSU2_coe (a : unitary ℂ) :
    ((gaugeCartan a).toSU2 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) = !![(a : ℂ), 0; 0, (star a : ℂ)]

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeGroupI.gaugeCartan_smul_eq
declarations.doc: The Cartan element acts as the diagonal matrix `diag(a, ā)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeCartan_smul_eq (a : unitary ℂ) (φ : HiggsVec) :
    HiggsVec.repGaugeGroupI (gaugeCartan a) φ =
      WithLp.toLp 2 (!![(a : ℂ), 0; 0, (star a : ℂ)] *ᵥ φ.ofLp)

modules.title: The two Higgs doublet potential as a polynomial in the gauge invariants
modules.doc:
Every gauge-invariant polynomial 2HDM potential is a polynomial in the four Gram bilinears.

## i. Overview

In the *bilinear formalism* of the two Higgs doublet model (hep-ph/0605184
[ref: arxiv_hep_ph_0605184]) the four gauge-invariant bilinears — the Gram vector `gramVector`
— describe the gauge orbits of the configuration space. This file proves the corresponding
statement for the potential: every
gauge-invariant polynomial effective potential is a polynomial in these four gauge-invariant
bilinears.

The proof gauge-fixes the potential to the polynomial family of orbit representatives `repHiggs X`
and runs the following physical pipeline:

1. **Charge balancing.** Invariance under the gauge torus forces the potential, written in
   hypercharge eigen-coordinates, to be supported only on hypercharge-neutral monomials.
2. **Generation.** Every neutral monomial is a product of the five neutral gauge-invariant
   quadratic bilinears, so the potential is a polynomial in them.
3. **Clearing the norms.** A power of `‖Φ1‖²` (resp. `‖Φ2‖²`, via the doublet swap) times the
   potential is a genuine polynomial in the Gram vector.
4. **Coprimality.** `‖Φ1‖²` and `‖Φ2‖²` are coprime in the (algebraically independent) Gram ring,
   which removes these factors and yields the Gram polynomial.

Mathematically the result is the first fundamental theorem of invariant theory for `SU(2)`
acting on two doublets in `ℂ²`.

## ii. Key results

* `exists_polynomial_repHiggs_sliceBilinear` — on gauge representatives, the potential is a
  polynomial in the five real gauge-invariant bilinears.
* `exists_normSq_Φ1_clearing`, `exists_normSq_Φ2_clearing` — a power of `‖Φ1‖²` (resp. `‖Φ2‖²`)
  times the potential is a polynomial in the Gram vector.
* `exists_polynomial_on_repHiggs` — the potential on representatives is a polynomial in the Gram
  vector.
* `effectivePotential_is_polynomial_gramVector` — a gauge-invariant polynomial potential is a
  polynomial in the four gauge-invariant bilinears.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Gauge-torus invariance of the potential on the slice
- B. Hypercharge eigen-coordinates and charge balancing
- C. Generation by the neutral gauge-invariant bilinears
- D. The potential on representatives as a polynomial in the bilinears
- E. Clearing the `‖Φ1‖²` and `‖Φ2‖²` factors
- F. Independence and coprimality of the Gram invariants
- G. The gauge-invariant potential as a polynomial in the Gram vector

## iv. References

* The bilinear formalism: https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/0605184. [ref: arxiv_hep_ph_0605184]

sections.text:
## A. Gauge-torus invariance of the potential on the slice

Invariance of the potential under the gauge torus forces the slice polynomial `P` to be invariant
under the hypercharge rotations of its variables: the Cartan rotation `cartanSubst` and the residual
`U(1)` rotation `residualSubst`.

## B. Hypercharge eigen-coordinates and charge balancing

Changing to hypercharge eigen-coordinates `z, z̄, w₀, w̄₀, w₁, w̄₁` diagonalises the gauge-torus
rotation into a scaling by the hypercharges `cartanCharge` (Cartan) and `hyperCharge` (residual).
Feeding an infinite-order phase into the invariance from part A shows that every monomial of the
potential carrying nonzero hypercharge has vanishing coefficient.

## C. Generation by the neutral gauge-invariant bilinears

The hypercharge-neutral monomials of `Qslice P` are exactly the products of the five neutral
quadratic bilinears `z z̄, w₀ w̄₀, z w̄₀, z̄ w₀, w₁ w̄₁` — the gauge invariants.
This is the (abelian)generation step: combined Cartan- and residual-neutrality of a
monomial forces it to be a product of
these five, because every charged variable carries a unit Cartan charge and the residual charges
come in an exact `±1` pair.

## D. The potential on representatives as a polynomial in the bilinears

Evaluating at the hypercharge eigen-point of a representative `repHiggs X`, and descending from the
complex value back to its real part, turns the generation result of part C into the statement that
the value `V (repHiggs X)` is a polynomial in the five real gauge-invariant bilinears
`‖Φ1‖², Re⟪⟫, Im⟪⟫, |Φ2₁|², |Φ2₀|²`.

## E. Clearing the `‖Φ1‖²` and `‖Φ2‖²` factors

Part D expresses the value as a polynomial in the bilinears, but two of them — `|Φ2₀|²`
  and `|Φ2₁|²`
— are not directly Gram polynomials. Multiplying by a power of `‖Φ1‖²` clears these; the
doublet swap of `SwapDoublet` then gives the mirror statement with `‖Φ2‖²`.

## F. Independence and coprimality of the Gram invariants

The four Gram invariants are algebraically independent (`gramPoly_injective`), and the two linear
combinations `‖Φ1‖² = (g₀+g₃)/2` and `‖Φ2‖² = (g₀-g₃)/2` are coprime in the Gram ring
(`uPow_dvd`). Together these let the `‖Φ1‖²` and `‖Φ2‖²` factors be cancelled.

## G. The gauge-invariant potential as a polynomial in the Gram vector

Every configuration is gauge equivalent to a representative `repHiggs X`
(`exists_smul_eq_repHiggs`) whose Gram vector is polynomial in the parameters
(`gramVector_repHiggs_*`). Combining the two norm clearings of part E with the coprimality of part F
removes the `‖Φ1‖²`/`‖Φ2‖²` factors and produces the Gram polynomial on representatives
(`exists_polynomial_on_repHiggs`); gauge invariance then transports it to all configurations.

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.eval_aeval_comp
declarations.doc: Pushing an evaluation through an `aeval` substitution.
declarations.statement:
lemma eval_aeval_comp {R : Type*} [CommRing R] {κ ι : Type*} (x : ι → R)
    (f : κ → MvPolynomial ι R) (G : MvPolynomial κ R) :
    eval x (aeval f G) = eval (fun i => eval x (f i)) G

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.cartanSubst
declarations.doc:
The Cartan hypercharge rotation of the slice parameters, as a substitution of the polynomial
variables.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def cartanSubst (u : unitary ℂ) : Fin 6 → MvPolynomial (Fin 6) ℝ

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.eval_cartanSubst
declarations.statement:
lemma eval_cartanSubst (u : unitary ℂ) (a : Fin 6 → ℝ) :
    (fun k => MvPolynomial.eval a (cartanSubst u k)) = cartanRotParam u a

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.aeval_cartanSubst_eq
declarations.doc:
Gauge (Cartan) invariance of the potential forces the slice polynomial to be invariant under the
hypercharge rotation of its variables.
declarations.statement:
lemma aeval_cartanSubst_eq {V : EffectivePotential} (hI : IsInvariant V)
    {P : MvPolynomial (Fin 6) ℝ} (hP : ∀ a, V (sliceR a) = P.eval a) (u : unitary ℂ) :
    aeval (cartanSubst u) P = P

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.residualSubst
declarations.doc: The residual `U(1)` rotation of the perpendicular parameter, as a substitution.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def residualSubst (c : unitary ℂ) : Fin 6 → MvPolynomial (Fin 6) ℝ

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.eval_residualSubst
declarations.statement:
lemma eval_residualSubst (c : unitary ℂ) (a : Fin 6 → ℝ) :
    (fun k => MvPolynomial.eval a (residualSubst c k)) = resRotParam c a

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.aeval_residualSubst_eq
declarations.doc:
Gauge (residual `U(1)`) invariance forces the slice polynomial to be invariant under the
perpendicular rotation of its variables.
declarations.statement:
lemma aeval_residualSubst_eq {V : EffectivePotential} (hI : IsInvariant V)
    {P : MvPolynomial (Fin 6) ℝ} (hP : ∀ a, V (sliceR a) = P.eval a) (c : unitary ℂ) :
    aeval (residualSubst c) P = P

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.hyperchargeEigen
declarations.doc:
Change to hypercharge eigen-coordinates: `aₖ` in terms of `z, z̄, w₀, w̄₀, w₁, w̄₁`
(indices `0..5`). This diagonalises the gauge-torus rotation into a scaling.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def hyperchargeEigen : Fin 6 → MvPolynomial (Fin 6) ℂ

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.diagCartan
declarations.doc: The Cartan hypercharge, diagonal in eigen-coordinates: charges `(1,-1,1,-1,-1,1)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def diagCartan (u : unitary ℂ) : Fin 6 → MvPolynomial (Fin 6) ℂ

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.diagRes
declarations.doc: The residual `U(1)`, diagonal in eigen-coordinates: only the perpendicular pair is charged.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def diagRes (c : unitary ℂ) : Fin 6 → MvPolynomial (Fin 6) ℂ

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.bind₁_diagCartan_hyperchargeEigen
declarations.doc:
Conjugation identity: the diagonal Cartan scaling, pulled back through the eigen-coordinate
change, is the (complexified) Cartan rotation substitution.
declarations.statement:
lemma bind₁_diagCartan_hyperchargeEigen (u : unitary ℂ) (k : Fin 6) :
    bind₁ (diagCartan u) (hyperchargeEigen k)
      = bind₁ hyperchargeEigen (map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ) (cartanSubst u k))

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.bind₁_diagRes_hyperchargeEigen
declarations.doc: Conjugation identity for the residual `U(1)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma bind₁_diagRes_hyperchargeEigen (c : unitary ℂ) (k : Fin 6) :
    bind₁ (diagRes c) (hyperchargeEigen k)
      = bind₁ hyperchargeEigen (map (algebraMap ℝ ℂ) (residualSubst c k))

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.cartanCharge
declarations.doc: The Cartan hypercharges of `z, z̄, w₀, w̄₀, w₁, w̄₁`.
declarations.statement: def cartanCharge : Fin 6 → ℤ

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.hyperCharge
declarations.doc: The residual-`U(1)` hypercharges (only the perpendicular pair is charged).
declarations.statement: def hyperCharge : Fin 6 → ℤ

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.Qslice
declarations.doc: The slice potential, complexified and written in hypercharge eigen-coordinates.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def Qslice (P : MvPolynomial (Fin 6) ℝ) : MvPolynomial (Fin 6) ℂ

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.diagCartan_eq
declarations.doc: The Cartan diagonal in the charge form consumed by the charge-balancing engine.
declarations.statement:
lemma diagCartan_eq (u : unitary ℂ) :
    diagCartan u = fun i => C ((u : ℂ) ^ (cartanCharge i)) * X i

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.diagRes_eq
declarations.doc: The residual diagonal in the charge form consumed by the engine.
declarations.statement:
lemma diagRes_eq (c : unitary ℂ) :
    diagRes c = fun i => C (((c : ℂ) ^ 6) ^ (hyperCharge i)) * X i

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.bind₁_diagCartan_Qslice
declarations.doc:
In eigen-coordinates, the Cartan hypercharge acts by the diagonal scaling, and the slice
potential is invariant under it.
declarations.statement:
lemma bind₁_diagCartan_Qslice {V : EffectivePotential} (hI : IsInvariant V)
    {P : MvPolynomial (Fin 6) ℝ} (hP : ∀ a, V (sliceR a) = P.eval a) (u : unitary ℂ) :
    bind₁ (diagCartan u) (Qslice P) = Qslice P

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.bind₁_diagRes_Qslice
declarations.doc: Likewise for the residual `U(1)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma bind₁_diagRes_Qslice {V : EffectivePotential} (hI : IsInvariant V)
    {P : MvPolynomial (Fin 6) ℝ} (hP : ∀ a, V (sliceR a) = P.eval a) (c : unitary ℂ) :
    bind₁ (diagRes c) (Qslice P) = Qslice P

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.exists_infiniteOrder_unitary
declarations.doc: There is a gauge phase of infinite order (`exp i`), needed to run charge balancing.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_infiniteOrder_unitary :
    ∃ ω : unitary ℂ, ∀ n : ℤ, (ω : ℂ) ^ n = 1 → n = 0

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.coeff_Qslice_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
**Hypercharge balancing.** Every monomial of the slice potential `Qslice P` (in eigen-
coordinates) that carries nonzero Cartan or residual hypercharge has vanishing coefficient.
declarations.statement:
lemma coeff_Qslice_eq_zero {V : EffectivePotential} (hI : IsInvariant V)
    {P : MvPolynomial (Fin 6) ℝ} (hP : ∀ a, V (sliceR a) = P.eval a) (m : Fin 6 →₀ ℕ)
    (hm : (∑ i ∈ m.support, (m i : ℤ) * cartanCharge i ≠ 0) ∨
          (∑ i ∈ m.support, (m i : ℤ) * hyperCharge i ≠ 0)) :
    (Qslice P).coeff m = 0

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.neutralBilinear
declarations.doc:
The five hypercharge-neutral quadratic bilinears in eigen-coordinates:
`z z̄`, `w₀ w̄₀`, `z w̄₀`, `z̄ w₀`, `w₁ w̄₁`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def neutralBilinear : Fin 5 → MvPolynomial (Fin 6) ℂ

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.charge_univ_eq_support
declarations.doc: The charge of a monomial, summed over the whole index set, equals the sum over its support.
declarations.statement:
lemma charge_univ_eq_support (w : Fin 6 → ℤ) (m : Fin 6 →₀ ℕ) :
    ∑ i, (m i : ℤ) * w i = ∑ i ∈ m.support, (m i : ℤ) * w i

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.chargeSum_add
declarations.doc: A charge sum is additive in the monomial.
declarations.statement:
lemma chargeSum_add (w : Fin 6 → ℤ) (a b : Fin 6 →₀ ℕ) :
    ∑ k, ((a + b) k : ℤ) * w k = (∑ k, (a k : ℤ) * w k) + ∑ k, (b k : ℤ) * w k

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.chargeSum_single
declarations.doc: The charge sum of a single generator is the charge of that variable.
declarations.statement:
lemma chargeSum_single (w : Fin 6 → ℤ) (i : Fin 6) :
    ∑ k, ((Finsupp.single i (1 : ℕ)) k : ℤ) * w k = w i

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.monomial_mem_adjoin_neutralBilinear
declarations.doc: **Generation.** Every hypercharge-neutral monomial is a product of the five bilinears.
declarations.statement:
lemma monomial_mem_adjoin_neutralBilinear (m : Fin 6 →₀ ℕ)
    (hA : ∑ i, (m i : ℤ) * cartanCharge i = 0) (hB : ∑ i, (m i : ℤ) * hyperCharge i = 0) :
    monomial m (1 : ℂ) ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℂ (Set.range neutralBilinear)

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.Qslice_mem_adjoin_neutralBilinear
declarations.doc:
The slice potential lies in the subalgebra generated by the five bilinears: every monomial that
survives is hypercharge-neutral, hence a product of the bilinears.
declarations.statement:
lemma Qslice_mem_adjoin_neutralBilinear {V : EffectivePotential} (hI : IsInvariant V)
    {P : MvPolynomial (Fin 6) ℝ} (hP : ∀ a, V (sliceR a) = P.eval a) :
    Qslice P ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℂ (Set.range neutralBilinear)

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.exists_aeval_neutralBilinear
declarations.doc:
Consequently the complexified slice potential is `aeval neutralBilinear G` for some polynomial
`G` in the five bilinears.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_aeval_neutralBilinear {V : EffectivePotential} (hI : IsInvariant V)
    {P : MvPolynomial (Fin 6) ℝ} (hP : ∀ a, V (sliceR a) = P.eval a) :
    ∃ G : MvPolynomial (Fin 5) ℂ, aeval neutralBilinear G = Qslice P

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.aRep
declarations.doc: The slice parameters realising `repHiggs X` as a point of the slice family.
declarations.statement: def aRep (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) : Fin 6 → ℝ

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.repHiggs_eq_sliceR
declarations.statement: lemma repHiggs_eq_sliceR (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) : repHiggs X = sliceR (aRep X)

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.eigenPoint
declarations.doc:
The hypercharge eigen-point `(z, z̄, w₀, w̄₀, w₁, w̄₁)` of `repHiggs X`: here `z = X₀` is real,
`w₀ = X₁ + i X₂` and `w₁ = X₃` is real.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def eigenPoint (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) : Fin 6 → ℂ

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.aeval_hyperchargeEigen_eigenPoint
declarations.doc:
The eigen-coordinate change sends the eigen-point of `repHiggs X` back to its
slice parameters.
declarations.statement:
lemma aeval_hyperchargeEigen_eigenPoint (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) (k : Fin 6) :
    aeval (eigenPoint X) (hyperchargeEigen k) = algebraMap ℝ ℂ (aRep X k)

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.eval_Qslice_eigenPoint
declarations.doc:
The complexified slice potential, evaluated at the eigen-point of `repHiggs X`, returns the real
value `V (repHiggs X)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma eval_Qslice_eigenPoint (P : MvPolynomial (Fin 6) ℝ) (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    eval (eigenPoint X) (Qslice P) = algebraMap ℝ ℂ (P.eval (aRep X))

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.realPart
declarations.doc: The real part of a complex polynomial, taken coefficient-wise.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def realPart (H : MvPolynomial (Fin 5) ℂ) : MvPolynomial (Fin 5) ℝ

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.realPart_coeff
declarations.statement:
lemma realPart_coeff (H : MvPolynomial (Fin 5) ℂ) (m : Fin 5 →₀ ℕ) :
    (realPart H).coeff m = (H.coeff m).re

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.realPart_C
declarations.statement: lemma realPart_C (a : ℂ) : realPart (C a) = C a.re

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.realPart_add
declarations.statement:
lemma realPart_add (p q : MvPolynomial (Fin 5) ℂ) :
    realPart (p + q) = realPart p + realPart q

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.realPart_mul_X
declarations.statement:
lemma realPart_mul_X (p : MvPolynomial (Fin 5) ℂ) (i : Fin 5) :
    realPart (p * X i) = realPart p * X i

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.realPart_eval
declarations.doc:
Evaluating a complex polynomial at a real point and taking the real part is the same as
evaluating its real part.
declarations.statement:
lemma realPart_eval (H : MvPolynomial (Fin 5) ℂ) (y : Fin 5 → ℝ) :
    (eval (fun j => (↑(y j) : ℂ)) H).re = (realPart H).eval y

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.sliceBilinear
declarations.doc:
The five real gauge-invariant bilinears, evaluated at `repHiggs X`:
`‖Φ1‖², Re⟪⟫, Im⟪⟫, |Φ2₁|², |Φ2₀|²`.
declarations.statement: def sliceBilinear (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) : Fin 5 → ℝ

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.transf
declarations.doc:
The complex substitution expressing each bilinear, at the eigen-point, through the real
generators (the off-diagonal pair `z w̄₀, z̄ w₀` mix `Re⟪⟫` and `Im⟪⟫`).
declarations.statement: noncomputable def transf : Fin 5 → MvPolynomial (Fin 5) ℂ

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.neutralBilinear_eval_eigenPoint
declarations.doc:
The bilinears at the eigen-point of `repHiggs X` are the real generators,
read through `transf`.
declarations.statement:
lemma neutralBilinear_eval_eigenPoint (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) (i : Fin 5) :
    eval (eigenPoint X) (neutralBilinear i)
      = eval (fun j => (↑(sliceBilinear X j) : ℂ)) (transf i)

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.exists_polynomial_repHiggs_sliceBilinear
declarations.doc:
**The potential on representatives, in the bilinears.** A gauge-invariant polynomial potential,
on the representative family, is a polynomial in the five real gauge-invariant bilinears
`‖Φ1‖², Re⟪⟫, Im⟪⟫, |Φ2₁|², |Φ2₀|²`.

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.sliceBilinearPoly
declarations.doc: The five bilinear generators, as polynomials in the four representative parameters.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def sliceBilinearPoly : Fin 5 → MvPolynomial (Fin 4) ℝ

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.gramPoly
declarations.doc: The four Gram components, as polynomials in the four representative parameters.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gramPoly : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 → MvPolynomial (Fin 4) ℝ

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.sliceBilinearPoly_eval
declarations.statement:
lemma sliceBilinearPoly_eval (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) (i : Fin 5) :
    (sliceBilinearPoly i).eval X = sliceBilinear X i

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.gramPoly_eval
declarations.statement:
lemma gramPoly_eval (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (gramPoly μ).eval X = (repHiggs X).gramVector μ

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.exists_clearing_mem
declarations.doc:
Some power of `‖Φ1‖² = X₀²` times the value polynomial lies in the Gram
subalgebra: multiplying by `X₀²` pairs each `X₁²+X₂²` into `(X₀X₁)²+(X₀X₂)²` and each `X₃²` into
the determinant `X₀²X₃²`, both of which are Gram polynomials.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_clearing_mem (p : MvPolynomial (Fin 5) ℝ) :
    ∃ N : ℕ, (X 0) ^ (2 * N) * aeval sliceBilinearPoly p ∈
      Algebra.adjoin ℝ (Set.range gramPoly)

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.exists_gram_clearing
declarations.doc:
**Denominator clearing.** For the value polynomial `p`, some power of `‖Φ1‖² = X₀²`
times `p ∘ sliceBilinear` is a polynomial in the Gram vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_gram_clearing (p : MvPolynomial (Fin 5) ℝ) :
    ∃ (A : MvPolynomial (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ℝ) (N : ℕ), ∀ X : Fin 4 → ℝ,
      (X 0) ^ (2 * N) * p.eval (sliceBilinear X) = A.eval ((repHiggs X).gramVector)

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.exists_normSq_Φ1_clearing
declarations.doc:
**`‖Φ1‖²`-clearing, on all configurations.** A power of `‖Φ1‖²` times a gauge-invariant
polynomial potential is, everywhere, a polynomial in the Gram vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_normSq_Φ1_clearing {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ}
    (hI : IsInvariant V) (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n) :
    ∃ (A : MvPolynomial (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ℝ) (N : ℕ), ∀ φ : TwoHiggsDoublet,
      (‖φ.Φ1‖ ^ 2) ^ N * V φ = A.eval φ.gramVector

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.swapSubst
declarations.doc:
The Gram-vector substitution induced by swapping the doublets (sign flip on the imaginary and
difference components).
declarations.statement: noncomputable def swapSubst : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → MvPolynomial (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ℝ

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.exists_normSq_Φ2_clearing
declarations.doc:
**`‖Φ2‖²`-clearing, on all configurations.** A power of `‖Φ2‖²` times a gauge-invariant
polynomial potential is, everywhere, a polynomial in the Gram vector. Obtained from
`exists_normSq_Φ1_clearing` for the doublet-swapped potential.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_normSq_Φ2_clearing {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ}
    (hI : IsInvariant V) (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n) :
    ∃ (B : MvPolynomial (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ℝ) (M : ℕ), ∀ φ : TwoHiggsDoublet,
      (‖φ.Φ2‖ ^ 2) ^ M * V φ = B.eval φ.gramVector

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.gramPoly_injective
declarations.doc: The four Gram invariants are algebraically independent: the Gram substitution is injective.
declarations.statement:
lemma gramPoly_injective :
    Function.Injective
      (aeval gramPoly : MvPolynomial (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ℝ → MvPolynomial (Fin 4) ℝ)

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.uPow_dvd
declarations.doc:
`‖Φ1‖²` and `‖Φ2‖²`, as the distinct linear forms `(g₀±g₃)/2` of the Gram ring, are coprime:
if `‖Φ1‖²ᴺ · B = ‖Φ2‖²ᴹ · A` then `‖Φ1‖²ᴺ ∣ A`.
declarations.statement:
lemma uPow_dvd {N M : ℕ} {A B : MvPolynomial (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ℝ}
    (hAB : (C (1 / 2) * (X (Sum.inl 0) + X (Sum.inr 2))) ^ N * B
       = (C (1 / 2) * (X (Sum.inl 0) - X (Sum.inr 2))) ^ M * A) :
    (C (1 / 2) * (X (Sum.inl 0) + X (Sum.inr 2))) ^ N ∣ A

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.exists_polynomial_on_repHiggs
declarations.doc:
**On representatives.** A gauge-invariant polynomial potential, restricted to the polynomial
family of orbit representatives `repHiggs X`, is a polynomial in the Gram components of that
family. Proved by the doublet-swap argument: clearing the `‖Φ1‖²` factor (aligning `Φ1`) and the
`‖Φ2‖²` factor (aligning `Φ2`, via the gauge-commuting swap), then using that `‖Φ1‖²` and `‖Φ2‖²`
are coprime in the Gram ring.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_polynomial_on_repHiggs {V : EffectivePotential} {n : ℕ}
    (hI : IsInvariant V) (h : HasMaxMassDimLE V n) :
    ∃ p : MvPolynomial (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ℝ,
      ∀ X : Fin 4 → ℝ, V (repHiggs X) = p.eval (repHiggs X).gramVector

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.effectivePotential_is_polynomial_gramVector
declarations.doc:
**The two Higgs doublet potential in the bilinear formalism.** A gauge-invariant polynomial
effective potential of maximum mass dimension `n` is a polynomial in the four gauge-invariant
bilinears — the entries of the Gram vector.

modules.title: The Module structure on the two Higgs doublet model
modules.doc:
The complex vector space (module) structure on two Higgs doublet configurations.

## i. Overview

Configurations of the two Higgs doublet model are pairs of Higgs vectors `(Φ1, Φ2)`. This file
defines addition, zero, negation and complex scalar multiplication componentwise, and assembles
them into an additive commutative group and a `ℂ`-module structure on `TwoHiggsDoublet`.

## ii. Key results

- `AddCommGroup TwoHiggsDoublet` : the additive commutative group structure (an instance).
- `Module ℂ TwoHiggsDoublet` : the `ℂ`-module structure (an instance).

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The structure of a module

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.statement: instance : Add TwoHiggsDoublet

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.add_fst
declarations.statement: lemma add_fst (H1 H2 : TwoHiggsDoublet) : (H1 + H2).Φ1 = H1.Φ1 + H2.Φ1

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.add_snd
declarations.statement: lemma add_snd (H1 H2 : TwoHiggsDoublet) : (H1 + H2).Φ2 = H1.Φ2 + H2.Φ2
instance : Zero TwoHiggsDoublet

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.zero_fst
declarations.statement: lemma zero_fst : (0 : TwoHiggsDoublet).Φ1 = 0

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.zero_snd
declarations.statement: lemma zero_snd : (0 : TwoHiggsDoublet).Φ2 = 0
instance : SMul ℂ TwoHiggsDoublet

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.smul_fst
declarations.statement: lemma smul_fst (c : ℂ) (H : TwoHiggsDoublet) : (c • H).Φ1 = c • H.Φ1

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.smul_snd
declarations.statement: lemma smul_snd (c : ℂ) (H : TwoHiggsDoublet) : (c • H).Φ2 = c • H.Φ2

modules.title: A polynomial family of orbit representatives for the two Higgs doublet model
modules.doc:
Every 2HDM gauge orbit meets a four-parameter family whose Gram vector is polynomial.

## i. Overview

Every gauge orbit of the two Higgs doublet model meets the four–real–parameter family

`repHiggs X = ⟨(0, X₀), (X₃, X₁ + i X₂)⟩`.

The crucial feature of this family (compared with the normalised representatives of
`gaugeGroupI_exists_fst_eq_snd_eq`) is that it is a *polynomial* family: the Gram vector of
`repHiggs X` is a polynomial in `X`, with no square roots. Consequently the value of a gauge
invariant potential on any field configuration is `V (repHiggs X)` for a suitable `X`, and the
question of whether `V` is a polynomial in the Gram vector reduces to the purely algebraic question
of whether `V ∘ repHiggs` lies in the subring generated by the (polynomial) Gram components of the
representative family.

## ii. Key results

- `TwoHiggsDoublet.repHiggs` : the four-parameter family of representatives.
- `TwoHiggsDoublet.gramVector_repHiggs_inl`, `TwoHiggsDoublet.gramVector_repHiggs_inr0`,
  `TwoHiggsDoublet.gramVector_repHiggs_inr1`, `TwoHiggsDoublet.gramVector_repHiggs_inr2` : the
  components of the Gram vector of `repHiggs X` as polynomials in `X`.
- `TwoHiggsDoublet.exists_smul_eq_repHiggs` : every configuration is gauge equivalent to a
  representative.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The representative family
- B. The Gram vector of a representative
- C. Every configuration is gauge equivalent to a representative

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The representative family

## B. The Gram vector of a representative

The Gram vector of `repHiggs X` is an explicit polynomial in the four real parameters `X`.
## C. Every configuration is gauge equivalent to a representative

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.repHiggs
declarations.doc:
A four–real–parameter polynomial family of representatives for the gauge orbits: the first
doublet is `(0, X₀)` and the second is `(X₃, X₁ + i X₂)`.
declarations.statement: def repHiggs (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) : TwoHiggsDoublet

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.repHiggs_Φ1
declarations.statement: lemma repHiggs_Φ1 (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) : (repHiggs X).Φ1 = !₂[0, (X 0 : ℂ)]

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.repHiggs_Φ2
declarations.statement:
lemma repHiggs_Φ2 (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    (repHiggs X).Φ2 = !₂[(X 3 : ℂ), (X 1 : ℂ) + Complex.I * (X 2 : ℂ)]

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.normSq_repHiggs_Φ1
declarations.statement: lemma normSq_repHiggs_Φ1 (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) : ‖(repHiggs X).Φ1‖ ^ 2 = X 0 ^ 2

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.normSq_repHiggs_Φ2
declarations.statement:
lemma normSq_repHiggs_Φ2 (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    ‖(repHiggs X).Φ2‖ ^ 2 = X 1 ^ 2 + X 2 ^ 2 + X 3 ^ 2

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.inner_repHiggs
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_repHiggs (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    ⟪(repHiggs X).Φ1, (repHiggs X).Φ2⟫_ℂ = (X 0 : ℂ) * ((X 1 : ℂ) + Complex.I * (X 2 : ℂ))

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.gramVector_repHiggs_inl
declarations.statement:
lemma gramVector_repHiggs_inl (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    (repHiggs X).gramVector (Sum.inl 0) = X 0 ^ 2 + (X 1 ^ 2 + X 2 ^ 2 + X 3 ^ 2)

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.gramVector_repHiggs_inr0
declarations.statement:
lemma gramVector_repHiggs_inr0 (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    (repHiggs X).gramVector (Sum.inr 0) = 2 * X 0 * X 1

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.gramVector_repHiggs_inr1
declarations.statement:
lemma gramVector_repHiggs_inr1 (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    (repHiggs X).gramVector (Sum.inr 1) = 2 * X 0 * X 2

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.gramVector_repHiggs_inr2
declarations.statement:
lemma gramVector_repHiggs_inr2 (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) :
    (repHiggs X).gramVector (Sum.inr 2) = X 0 ^ 2 - (X 1 ^ 2 + X 2 ^ 2 + X 3 ^ 2)

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.exists_smul_eq_repHiggs
declarations.doc:
Every field configuration is in the gauge orbit of a representative `repHiggs X`. This is the
key fact that lets a gauge invariant potential be evaluated on the polynomial family.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_smul_eq_repHiggs (φ : TwoHiggsDoublet) :
    ∃ (X : Fin 4 → ℝ) (g : GaugeGroupI), g • φ = repHiggs X

modules.title: Swapping the two Higgs doublets
modules.doc:
The doublet swap Φ1 ↔ Φ2 commutes with gauge action, preserving invariance and mass dimension.

## i. Overview

Exchanging the two doublets `Φ1 ↔ Φ2` is an `ℝ`-linear map `swapDoublet` that commutes with the
gauge action. It therefore preserves gauge invariance and the maximum mass dimension, while turning
the alignment of `Φ1` into the alignment of `Φ2`. This is precisely the symmetry used to clear the
`‖Φ2‖²` factor when writing the potential through the gauge invariants, mirroring the `‖Φ1‖²`
clearing.

## ii. Key results

* `swapDoublet` — the doublet exchange, as an `ℝ`-linear map.
* `swapDoublet_smul` — it commutes with the gauge action.
* `gramVector_swapDoublet_*` — its effect on the Gram vector (a sign flip on the imaginary and
  difference components).
* `IsInvariant.comp_swapDoublet`, `HasMaxMassDimLE.comp_swapDoublet` — it preserves gauge invariance
  and bounded mass dimension.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The doublet-swap map and its components
- B. Commutation with the gauge action
- C. The action on the Gram vector
- D. Effect on gauge invariance and mass dimension

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.swapDoublet
declarations.doc:
Swapping the two doublets, as an `ℝ`-linear map. It commutes with the gauge action, so it sends
gauge-invariant polynomial potentials to gauge-invariant polynomial potentials, but turns the
alignment of `Φ1` into the alignment of `Φ2`.
declarations.statement: def swapDoublet : TwoHiggsDoublet →ₗ[ℝ] TwoHiggsDoublet

declarations.name: TwoHiggsDoublet.EffectivePotential.swapDoublet_Φ1

modules.title: The jet algebras of quantum electrodynamics
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

This file contains *all the definitions* of the jet-algebra formulation of
quantum electrodynamics: the jet algebras of the photon and of the Dirac
electron, their tensor product — the QED jet algebra — the data of a gauge
transformation as seen by jets, the gauge actions on all three algebras, and
the evaluation of the photon jet algebra on an honest electromagnetic
potential.

The *fields* of QED (the jet coordinates, the field strength, the γ matrices
and the covariant derivatives) are defined on top of these algebras in
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Fields`, and the Lagrangian in
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Lagrangian`. All
theorems about them are proved in the definition-free files
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.FermionStatistics`, `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.FieldStrength`,
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.GammaMatrices`, `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.GaugeInvariance` and
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Evaluation`.

The design choices:

* The photon jet algebra is the free commutative algebra on formal symbols
  `∂_s A_μ`, one for every multiset `s` of spacetime directions and every
  Lorentz index `μ`, built directly on the electromagnetic potential of
  `Physlib.Electromagnetism`.  It deliberately does *not* use
  `Physlib.Particles.StandardModel.GaugeBosons.BBoson`: the `B` boson is the
  gauge boson of `U(1)_Y` before electroweak symmetry breaking, the photon is
  the mixed combination `A = cos θ_W B + sin θ_W W³`, and the two are not the
  same field.  Building directly on `ElectromagneticPotential` also avoids
  inheriting the Standard Model charge normalisation `6Y`, which has no
  meaning for `U(1)_em`.

* The electron jet algebra is the free *exterior* algebra on formal symbols
  `∂_s ψ_α`, `∂_s ψ̄_α` with `α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2` a Dirac index in the chiral
  representation; the exterior product implements fermionic statistics.  A
  faithful QED matter sector needs a *Dirac* electron — equivalently two Weyl
  spinors of the same chirality with charges `±1` — which is what makes the
  dimension-three mass term `m ψ̄ ψ` possible; a single Weyl fermion admits no
  such term.

* A gauge transformation is recorded by its jets: the derivative jets
  `∂_s χ` of the real gauge function together with the derivative jets
  `∂_s (exp (I e χ))` of its unitary phase, related by the formal Leibniz
  identity `∂_μ u = I e (∂_μ χ) u`.  The action on the photon coordinates is
  the affine shift `∂_s A_μ ↦ ∂_s A_μ + ∂_s ∂_μ χ`, and on the electron
  coordinates the Leibniz expansion of `∂_s (ū ψ)` over
  `Multiset.antidiagonal s`, whose multiplicities are exactly the multinomial
  coefficients of the Leibniz rule.

This construction mirrors `Physlib.Particles.LeptonGaugeSector`, where the
analogous algebra for a single charged Weyl fermion is built from
representation-theoretic data.

## ii. Key results

- `Photon.JetGenerators`, `Photon.JetAlgebra`, `Photon.JetAlgebra.coord` :
  the photon jet coordinates `∂_s A_μ` and their polynomial algebra.
- `Photon.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction` : the affine gauge action on the photon jet
  algebra.
- `Photon.JetAlgebra.evalPotential` : the evaluation of the photon jet
  algebra on an electromagnetic potential.
- `GaugeJet` : the jets of a `U(1)_em` gauge transformation with coupling `e`.
- `Electron.JetGenerators`, `Electron.JetAlgebra` : the electron jet
  coordinates `∂_s ψ_α`, `∂_s ψ̄_α` and their exterior algebra.
- `Electron.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction` : the Leibniz gauge action on the
  electron jet algebra.
- `JetAlgebra` : the QED jet algebra, the tensor product of the complexified
  photon jet algebra with the electron jet algebra.
- `JetAlgebra.gaugeAction` : the gauge action on the QED jet algebra.
- `JetAlgebra.lorentzAction` : the Lorentz action on the QED jet algebra,
  through the covering map `Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup` on the photon factor
  and the Dirac spinor representation `Electron.JetAlgebra.spinorRep` on the
  electron factor.
- `JetAlgebra.massScale` : the mass-weight scaling on the QED jet algebra.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. 0. Transport of derivative indices along a Lorentz transformation
- B. The jet algebra of the photon
  - B.1. The jet coordinates
  - B.2. The gauge action on the photon jet algebra
  - B.3. Iterated derivatives indexed by a multiset
  - B.4. Evaluation on a potential
  - B.5. The Lorentz action on the photon jet algebra
  - B.6. The mass-weight scaling on the photon jet algebra
  - B.7. The formal total derivative on the photon jet algebra
- C. The gauge jet of a `U(1)_em` transformation
  - C.1. Low-order consequences of the Leibniz identity
  - C.2. The commutative monoid of gauge jets
- D. The jet algebra of the electron
  - D.1. The jet coordinates
  - D.2. The gauge action on the electron jet algebra
  - D.3. The action on the low-order jet coordinates
  - D.4. The Lorentz action on the electron jet algebra
  - D.5. The mass-weight scaling on the electron jet algebra
  - D.6. The formal total derivative on the electron jet algebra
- E. The jet algebra of QED
  - E.1. Pure tensors and their arithmetic
  - E.2. The inclusions of the two factors
  - E.3. The gauge action on the QED jet algebra
  - E.4. The Lorentz action on the QED jet algebra
  - E.5. The mass-weight scaling on the QED jet algebra
  - E.6. The formal total derivative on the QED jet algebra

## iv. References

The concrete electromagnetic side is
`Physlib/Electromagnetism/Kinematics/GaugeTransformation.lean` and
`Physlib/Electromagnetism/Dynamics/KineticTerm.lean`.

sections.text:
## A. 0. Transport of derivative indices along a Lorentz transformation

A jet coordinate carries a multiset of derivative indices, each of which
transforms with `Λ⁻¹` under a Lorentz transformation (the chain rule for
`x ↦ Λ⁻¹ x`).  To sum over the transformed indices without summing over
functions on a multiset, the transport recurses along the *canonical sorted
list* of the multiset, threading the chosen indices through a continuation.

## B. The jet algebra of the photon

### B.1. The jet coordinates

A jet coordinate is a formal symbol `∂_s A_μ`, where `s` is a *multiset* of
spacetime directions: for a smooth potential the partial derivatives commute,
so only the number of times each direction occurs matters.  The jet algebra is
the algebra of real polynomials in these symbols.

### B.2. The gauge action on the photon jet algebra

A `U(1)_em` gauge transformation sends `A_μ ↦ A_μ + ∂_μ χ`, hence on jet
coordinates `∂_s A_μ ↦ ∂_s A_μ + ∂_s ∂_μ χ`.  All that the photon jet algebra
sees of the gauge function `χ` is the family of its symmetrised derivatives at
the base point, which is what `GaugeJet` records; the shift of `∂_s A_μ` is
then the value of that family at `s + {μ}`.

### B.3. Iterated derivatives indexed by a multiset

To evaluate a jet coordinate on a potential we must differentiate along a
multiset of directions, so we must choose an order; we choose the canonical
one, sorting `s` through `Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 ≃ Fin 4`.  For a `C^∞` potential the
choice is immaterial, by Clairaut's theorem (`SpaceTime.deriv_commute`).

### B.4. Evaluation on a potential

`ElectromagneticPotential` stores the contravariant components `A^μ`, whereas
a gauge potential carries a lower index, so the jet coordinate `∂_s A_μ`
evaluates to the `s`-th derivative of `A_μ = η_{μμ} A^μ`.

### B.5. The Lorentz action on the photon jet algebra

Under a Lorentz transformation the potential transforms as a covector field,
`A'(x) = (Λ⁻¹)ᵀ A (Λ⁻¹ x)`, so every lower index of the jet coordinate
`∂_s A_μ` — the index `μ` and each derivative index in `s` — is summed
against a row of `Λ⁻¹`.
### B.6. The mass-weight scaling on the photon jet algebra
### B.7. The formal total derivative on the photon jet algebra

## C. The gauge jet of a `U(1)_em` transformation

A gauge transformation with gauge function `χ` acts on the photon by
`A_μ ↦ A_μ + ∂_μ χ` and on a field of charge `q` by `ψ ↦ exp (I q e χ) ψ`.
All that the jet algebras see of `χ` are its derivative jets `c s = ∂_s χ`,
and all they see of the phase are the derivative jets
`u s = ∂_s (exp (I e χ))`.  The two families are not independent:
differentiating the exponential gives `∂_μ u = I e (∂_μ χ) u`, whose `s`-th
derivative is a Leibniz sum over the splittings of `s`.
`Multiset.antidiagonal` counts each splitting with its multiplicity, which is
exactly the multinomial weight of the Leibniz rule.

### C.1. Low-order consequences of the Leibniz identity

The QED Lagrangian only involves jet coordinates of derivative order at most
one, so its gauge invariance only uses the Leibniz identity at order zero,
together with unitarity at the base point.

### C.2. The commutative monoid of gauge jets

Gauge jets compose: the gauge functions add and the phases convolve by the
Leibniz rule.  Closure of the two axioms under this product is a consistency
check on the axiomatisation of `GaugeJet`.

## D. The jet algebra of the electron

### D.1. The jet coordinates

A jet coordinate is a formal symbol `∂_s ψ_α` or `∂_s ψ̄_α`, where `s` is a
*multiset* of spacetime directions (partial derivatives of a smooth field
commute) and `α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2` is a Dirac spinor index in the chiral
representation: `Sum.inl` indexes the left-handed and `Sum.inr` the
right-handed Weyl component.

### D.2. The gauge action on the electron jet algebra

A gauge transformation sends the electron (charge `-1`) to `ū ψ` and its
conjugate to `u ψ̄`, where `u = exp (I e χ)`.  On jet coordinates this is the
Leibniz expansion

`∂_s ψ_α ↦ ∑_{x + y = s} (∂_x ū) (∂_y ψ_α)`,

the sum running over `Multiset.antidiagonal s`, whose multiplicities are the
multinomial coefficients of the Leibniz rule.  The action is linear on the jet
component space and extends functorially to an algebra map of the exterior
algebra.

### D.3. The action on the low-order jet coordinates

The QED Lagrangian involves only the jet coordinates of derivative order at
most one, for which the antidiagonal sums are short: `antidiagonal 0` is the
single splitting `(0, 0)`, and `antidiagonal {μ}` the two splittings
`(0, {μ})` and `({μ}, 0)`.

### D.4. The Lorentz action on the electron jet algebra

Under `M : SL(2,ℂ)` the Dirac spinor transforms in the chiral basis by the
block-diagonal matrix `S(M) = ((M, 0), (0, (M†)⁻¹))`, its conjugate by the
entrywise conjugate of `S(M)`, and every derivative index by `Λ(M)⁻¹`, where
`Λ(M)` is the image of `M` under the covering map
`Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup`.
### D.5. The mass-weight scaling on the electron jet algebra

### D.6. The formal total derivative on the electron jet algebra

The total derivative extends from the jet coordinates to the whole exterior
algebra as an *even* derivation, `∂_ρ (x y) = (∂_ρ x) y + x (∂_ρ y)` with no
Koszul signs.  It is constructed by lifting `ι x ↦ (ι x, ι (∂_ρ x))` to an
algebra homomorphism into the trivial square-zero extension of the jet
algebra, following
`Physlib.Particles.StandardModel.Fermions.LeptonSinglet.JetAlgebra.JetDeriv`.
## E. The jet algebra of QED
### E.1. Pure tensors and their arithmetic
### E.2. The inclusions of the two factors

### E.3. The gauge action on the QED jet algebra

A gauge jet acts on the photon factor by the affine shift
`∂_s A_μ ↦ ∂_s A_μ + ∂_s ∂_μ χ`, complexified, and on the electron factor by
the Leibniz expansion of `∂_s (ū ψ)` and `∂_s (u ψ̄)`; the action on the full
jet algebra is the tensor product of the two, an algebra map.

### E.4. The Lorentz action on the QED jet algebra

An `M : SL(2,ℂ)` acts on the photon factor through its image `Λ(M)` in the
Lorentz group, complexified, and on the electron factor through the spinor
representation; the action on the full jet algebra is the tensor product of
the two.
