declarations.name: QED.indexList
declarations.doc:
The canonical sorted list of a multiset of spacetime directions, sorted
through `Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 ≃ Fin 4`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def indexList (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)

declarations.name: QED.indexList_zero
declarations.statement: lemma indexList_zero : indexList 0 = []

declarations.name: QED.indexList_singleton
declarations.statement: lemma indexList_singleton (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : indexList {μ} = [μ]

declarations.name: QED.mem_indexList
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_indexList {t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)} {a : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3} :
    a ∈ indexList t ↔ a ∈ t

declarations.name: QED.indexList_length
declarations.statement:
lemma indexList_length (t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    (indexList t).length = Multiset.card t

declarations.name: QED.classRep
declarations.doc:
The canonical representative of a nonempty multiset of spacetime
directions: the head of its canonical sorted list.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def classRep (t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3

declarations.name: QED.classRep_mem
declarations.statement: lemma classRep_mem {t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)} (ht : t ≠ 0) : classRep t ∈ t

declarations.name: QED.derivSum
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz transport of a family indexed by derivative multisets along a
list of derivative directions: each direction in the list is summed against
a row of `Λ⁻¹`, and the chosen directions accumulate in the multiset
argument of the continuation `k`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivSum {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module ℝ M]
    (Λ : LorentzGroup 3) :
    List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M) → M

declarations.name: QED.derivSum_nil
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSum_nil {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module ℝ M]
    (Λ : LorentzGroup 3) (k : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M) :
    derivSum Λ [] k = k 0

declarations.name: QED.derivSum_cons
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSum_cons {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module ℝ M]
    (Λ : LorentzGroup 3) (σ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (l : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (k : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M) :
    derivSum Λ (σ :: l) k =
      ∑ τ, (Λ⁻¹).1 τ σ • derivSum Λ l fun t => k (t + {τ})

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetGenerators
declarations.doc:
The jet coordinates of the electromagnetic potential: the symbol `∂_s A_μ`,
the `s`-th derivative of the `μ`-th covariant component.
declarations.statement:
inductive JetGenerators where
  /-- The jet coordinate `∂_s A_μ`. -/
  | dA (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : JetGenerators
  deriving DecidableEq

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetGenerators.massWeight
declarations.doc:
The mass weight (twice the mass dimension) of a photon jet coordinate:
the potential has mass dimension one and each derivative adds one.
declarations.statement: def JetGenerators.massWeight : JetGenerators → ℕ

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetGenerators.indexClass
declarations.doc:
The symmetrized-index class of a photon jet coordinate: under a gauge
transformation `∂_s A_μ` shifts by `∂_s ∂_μ χ`, which depends only on the
multiset `s + {μ}`.  Coordinates in a common class shift together.
declarations.statement: def JetGenerators.indexClass : JetGenerators → Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetGenerators.classProj
declarations.doc:
The canonical jet coordinate of a symmetrized-index class: the coordinate
whose Lorentz index is the canonical representative of the class.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def JetGenerators.classProj (j : JetGenerators) : JetGenerators

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra
declarations.doc: The jet algebra of the photon: real polynomials in the jet coordinates.
declarations.statement: abbrev JetAlgebra : Type

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.coord
declarations.doc: The jet coordinate `∂_s A_μ` as an element of the jet algebra.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def coord (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.GaugeJet
declarations.doc:
A photon gauge jet: the family `s ↦ ∂_s χ` of symmetrised derivatives of a
gauge function at the base point.  This is all the photon jet algebra sees of
a gauge transformation.
declarations.statement: abbrev GaugeJet : Type

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction
declarations.doc:
The gauge action on the photon jet algebra: the algebra map determined by
`∂_s A_μ ↦ ∂_s A_μ + ∂_s ∂_μ χ`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gaugeAction (c : GaugeJet) : JetAlgebra →ₐ[ℝ] JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_coord
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_coord (c : GaugeJet) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    gaugeAction c (coord s μ) = coord s μ + MvPolynomial.C (c (s + {μ}))

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_C
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_C (c : GaugeJet) (r : ℝ) :
    gaugeAction c (MvPolynomial.C r) = MvPolynomial.C r

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.derivMultiset
declarations.doc:
The iterated partial derivative `∂_s f` along a multiset `s` of spacetime
directions, taken in the canonical order obtained by sorting `s`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivMultiset (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (f : SpaceTime 3 → ℝ) :
    SpaceTime 3 → ℝ

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.derivMultiset_zero
declarations.statement: lemma derivMultiset_zero (f : SpaceTime 3 → ℝ) : derivMultiset 0 f = f

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.derivMultiset_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma derivMultiset_singleton (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (f : SpaceTime 3 → ℝ) :
    derivMultiset {μ} f = ∂_ μ f

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.coPotential
declarations.doc: The covariant components `A_μ = η_{μμ} A^μ` of an electromagnetic potential.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def coPotential (A : ElectromagneticPotential 3) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    SpaceTime 3 → ℝ

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.evalPotential
declarations.doc:
The evaluation of the photon jet algebra at an electromagnetic potential `A`:
the algebra map sending the formal jet coordinate `∂_s A_μ` to the honest
function `∂_s A_μ` on spacetime.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def evalPotential (A : ElectromagneticPotential 3) :
    JetAlgebra →ₐ[ℝ] (SpaceTime 3 → ℝ)

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.evalPotential_coord
declarations.statement:
lemma evalPotential_coord (A : ElectromagneticPotential 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    evalPotential A (coord s μ) = derivMultiset s (coPotential A μ)

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on the photon jet algebra: the algebra map transporting
every lower index of `∂_s A_μ` with `Λ⁻¹`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def lorentzAction (Λ : LorentzGroup 3) : JetAlgebra →ₐ[ℝ] JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_coord
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_coord (Λ : LorentzGroup 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    lorentzAction Λ (coord s μ) =
      derivSum Λ (indexList s) fun t => ∑ ν, (Λ⁻¹).1 ν μ • coord t ν

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_coord_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_coord_zero (Λ : LorentzGroup 3) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    lorentzAction Λ (coord 0 μ) = ∑ ν, (Λ⁻¹).1 ν μ • coord 0 ν

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_coord_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_coord_singleton (Λ : LorentzGroup 3) (σ μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    lorentzAction Λ (coord {σ} μ) =
      ∑ τ, ∑ ν, ((Λ⁻¹).1 τ σ * (Λ⁻¹).1 ν μ) • coord {τ} ν

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.massScale
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight scaling on the photon jet algebra: the algebra map
multiplying each jet coordinate by `c` to the power of its mass weight.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def massScale (c : ℝ) : JetAlgebra →ₐ[ℝ] JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.massScale_coord
declarations.statement:
lemma massScale_coord (c : ℝ) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    massScale c (coord s μ) = c ^ (2 + 2 * Multiset.card s) • coord s μ

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv
declarations.doc:
The formal total spacetime derivative on the photon jet algebra in the
direction `ρ`: the derivation appending the derivative index,
`∂_s A_μ ↦ ∂_{s + {ρ}} A_μ`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def jetDeriv (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : JetAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv_coord
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_coord (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    jetDeriv ρ (coord s μ) = coord (s + {ρ}) μ

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv_one
declarations.statement: lemma jetDeriv_one (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : jetDeriv ρ (1 : JetAlgebra) = 0

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv_mul
declarations.doc: The total derivative is a derivation on the photon jet algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_mul (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x y : JetAlgebra) :
    jetDeriv ρ (x * y) = jetDeriv ρ x * y + x * jetDeriv ρ y

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv_baseChange_mul
declarations.doc: The Leibniz rule for the complexified total derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_baseChange_mul (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x y : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] JetAlgebra) :
    LinearMap.baseChange ℂ (jetDeriv ρ) (x * y) =
      LinearMap.baseChange ℂ (jetDeriv ρ) x * y +
        x * LinearMap.baseChange ℂ (jetDeriv ρ) y

declarations.name: QED.sum_map_antidiagonal_ite
declarations.doc:
Summing an indicator supported on the splittings `(0, t)` over the
antidiagonal of `t` picks out `f t`: the splitting `(0, t)` occurs exactly
once in `Multiset.antidiagonal t`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_map_antidiagonal_ite {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M]
    (t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (f : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M) :
    ((t.antidiagonal).map fun p => if p.1 = 0 then f p.2 else 0).sum = f t

declarations.name: QED.phaseAct
declarations.doc:
The Leibniz convolution of a phase family against a module-valued family
of jets, over the antidiagonal of the derivative multiset: the formal
expansion `∂_s (u ⬝ f) = ∑_{x + y = s} (∂_x u) (∂_y f)`, with the
multiplicities of `Multiset.antidiagonal` supplying the multinomial
weights.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def phaseAct {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] [Module ℂ M]
    (u : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ) (f : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M) :
    Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M

declarations.name: QED.phaseAct_zero_arg
declarations.statement: lemma phaseAct_zero_arg : phaseAct u f 0 = u 0 • f 0

declarations.name: QED.phaseAct_eq_sum
declarations.doc:
The convolution as a literal antidiagonal sum of products, for
scalar-valued families.
declarations.statement:
lemma phaseAct_eq_sum (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    phaseAct u v s = (s.antidiagonal.map fun p => u p.1 * v p.2).sum

declarations.name: QED.phaseAct_add_singleton
declarations.doc:
The Leibniz rule of the convolution: differentiating a convolution
differentiates one factor at a time.
declarations.statement:
lemma phaseAct_add_singleton (a : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    phaseAct u f (s + {a}) =
      phaseAct u (fun t => f (t + {a})) s +
        phaseAct (fun t => u (t + {a})) f s

declarations.name: QED.phaseAct_add_left
declarations.statement:
lemma phaseAct_add_left (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    phaseAct (fun t => u₁ t + u₂ t) f s = phaseAct u₁ f s + phaseAct u₂ f s

declarations.name: QED.phaseAct_add_right
declarations.statement:
lemma phaseAct_add_right (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    phaseAct u (fun t => f t + g t) s = phaseAct u f s + phaseAct u g s

declarations.name: QED.phaseAct_smul_left
declarations.statement:
lemma phaseAct_smul_left (c : ℂ) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    phaseAct (fun t => c * u t) f s = c • phaseAct u f s

declarations.name: QED.phaseAct_smul_right
declarations.statement:
lemma phaseAct_smul_right (c : ℂ) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    phaseAct u (fun t => c • f t) s = c • phaseAct u f s

declarations.name: QED.phaseAct_assoc
declarations.doc:
Associativity of the convolution: acting by `u` after `v` is acting by
the convolution `u ⋆ v`.
declarations.statement:
lemma phaseAct_assoc (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    phaseAct u (phaseAct v f) s = phaseAct (phaseAct u v) f s

declarations.name: QED.phaseAct_comm
declarations.doc: Commutativity of the scalar convolution.
declarations.statement:
lemma phaseAct_comm (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    phaseAct u v s = phaseAct v u s

declarations.name: QED.map_phaseAct
declarations.doc: A linear map passes through the convolution.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_phaseAct {N : Type*} [AddCommMonoid N] [Module ℂ N] (L : M →ₗ[ℂ] N)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    L (phaseAct u f s) = phaseAct u (fun t => L (f t)) s

declarations.name: QED.phaseAct_indicator
declarations.doc:
The convolution against the indicator of the empty multiset is the
identity: the splitting `(0, t)` occurs exactly once in the
antidiagonal.
declarations.statement:
lemma phaseAct_indicator (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    phaseAct (fun t => if t = 0 then 1 else 0) f s = f s

declarations.name: QED.star_phaseAct
declarations.doc: The star of a convolution is the convolution of the stars.
declarations.statement:
lemma star_phaseAct (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    star (phaseAct u v s) =
      phaseAct (fun t => star (u t)) (fun t => star (v t)) s

declarations.name: QED.GaugeJet
declarations.doc:
The jets of a `U(1)_em` gauge transformation with coupling `e`: the
derivative jets `χjet s = ∂_s χ` of the real gauge function and
`phase s = ∂_s (exp (I e χ))` of its unitary phase at the base point,
subject to the two identities every honest gauge function satisfies:
the phase has unit norm at the base point, and its derivatives obey the
formal Leibniz expansion of `∂_μ (exp (I e χ)) = I e (∂_μ χ) exp (I e χ)`.
declarations.statement:
structure GaugeJet (e : ℝ) where
  /-- The derivative jets `∂_s χ` of the gauge function. -/
  χjet : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℝ
  /-- The derivative jets `∂_s (exp (I e χ))` of the unitary phase. -/
  phase : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ
  /-- The phase is unitary at the base point. -/
  phase_zero_unitary : phase 0 * star (phase 0) = 1
  /-- The formal Leibniz identity `∂_s ∂_μ u = I e ∂_s ((∂_μ χ) u)`. -/
  phase_deriv : ∀ (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
    phase (s + {μ}) = Complex.I * e *
      ((s.antidiagonal.map fun p => (χjet (p.1 + {μ}) : ℂ) * phase p.2).sum)

declarations.name: QED.GaugeJet.star_phase_zero_unitary
declarations.statement: lemma star_phase_zero_unitary : star (g.phase 0) * g.phase 0 = 1

declarations.name: QED.GaugeJet.phase_singleton
declarations.doc:
The first derivative of the phase: the `s = 0` case of the Leibniz
identity, `∂_μ u = I e (∂_μ χ) u` at the base point.
declarations.statement:
lemma phase_singleton (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    g.phase {μ} = Complex.I * e * (g.χjet {μ} * g.phase 0)

declarations.name: QED.GaugeJet.star_phase_singleton
declarations.doc:
The first derivative of the conjugate phase,
`∂_μ ū = -I e (∂_μ χ) ū` at the base point.
declarations.statement:
lemma star_phase_singleton (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    star (g.phase {μ}) = -(Complex.I * e * (g.χjet {μ} * star (g.phase 0)))

declarations.name: QED.GaugeJet.trivial
declarations.doc: The trivial gauge jet: the jets of the constant gauge function `χ = 0`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def trivial (e : ℝ) : GaugeJet e

declarations.name: QED.GaugeJet.ext
declarations.statement:
lemma ext {g₁ g₂ : GaugeJet e} (h1 : g₁.χjet = g₂.χjet)
    (h2 : g₁.phase = g₂.phase) : g₁ = g₂

declarations.doc:
The composite of two gauge jets: the gauge functions add and the phases
convolve by the Leibniz rule.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance : Mul (GaugeJet e)

declarations.name: QED.GaugeJet.mul_χjet
declarations.statement: lemma mul_χjet (g₁ g₂ : GaugeJet e) : (g₁ * g₂).χjet = g₁.χjet + g₂.χjet

declarations.name: QED.GaugeJet.mul_phase
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_phase (g₁ g₂ : GaugeJet e) :
    (g₁ * g₂).phase = phaseAct g₁.phase g₂.phase
noncomputable instance : One (GaugeJet e)

declarations.name: QED.GaugeJet.one_χjet
declarations.statement: lemma one_χjet : (1 : GaugeJet e).χjet = 0

declarations.name: QED.GaugeJet.one_phase
declarations.statement:
lemma one_phase :
    (1 : GaugeJet e).phase = fun s => if s = 0 then (1 : ℂ) else 0

declarations.doc:
**The gauge jets form a commutative monoid**: the gauge symmetry data of
QED composes associatively, with the trivial gauge jet as the unit.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance : CommMonoid (GaugeJet e)

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetGenerators
declarations.doc:
The jet coordinates of the Dirac electron: the symbols `∂_s ψ_α` and
`∂_s ψ̄_α`, the `s`-th derivatives of the Dirac components and their
conjugates.  The electron has electric charge `-1`; its conjugate has
charge `+1`.
declarations.statement:
inductive JetGenerators where
  /-- The jet coordinate `∂_s ψ_α` of the electron. -/
  | dψ (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) : JetGenerators
  /-- The jet coordinate `∂_s ψ̄_α` of the conjugate electron. -/
  | dbarψ (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) : JetGenerators
  deriving DecidableEq

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetGenerators.massWeight
declarations.doc:
The mass weight (twice the mass dimension) of an electron jet coordinate:
a fermion has mass dimension `3/2` and each derivative adds one.
declarations.statement: def JetGenerators.massWeight : JetGenerators → ℕ

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetComponentSpace
declarations.doc:
The jet component space of the electron: the free complex module on the
jet coordinates.
declarations.statement: abbrev JetComponentSpace : Type

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The jet algebra of the electron: the exterior algebra on the free module
over the jet coordinates.  The exterior product implements the fermionic
anticommutativity of the electron field.
declarations.statement: abbrev JetAlgebra : Type

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.ofGenerator
declarations.doc:
The jet coordinate `∂_s ψ_α` or `∂_s ψ̄_α` as an element of the jet
algebra.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def ofGenerator (j : JetGenerators) : JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.gaugeActionGenerator
declarations.doc:
The gauge action on a single electron jet coordinate: the Leibniz
expansion of `∂_s (ū ψ_α)` and `∂_s (u ψ̄_α)` over the splittings of `s`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def gaugeActionGenerator {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) :
    JetGenerators → JetComponentSpace

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.gaugeActionCS
declarations.doc:
The gauge action on the jet component space: the linear extension of the
Leibniz expansion on the jet coordinates.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def gaugeActionCS {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) :
    JetComponentSpace →ₗ[ℂ] JetComponentSpace

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.gaugeActionCS_single
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeActionCS_single {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) (j : JetGenerators) :
    gaugeActionCS g (Finsupp.single j 1) = gaugeActionGenerator g j

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction
declarations.doc:
The gauge action on the electron jet algebra: the algebra map induced by
the Leibniz expansion on the jet coordinates.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def gaugeAction {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) :
    JetAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_ofGenerator_dψ
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_ofGenerator_dψ {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e)
    (t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    gaugeAction g (ofGenerator (.dψ t α)) =
      (t.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        star (g.phase p.1) • ofGenerator (.dψ p.2 α)).sum

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_ofGenerator_dbarψ
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_ofGenerator_dbarψ {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e)
    (t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    gaugeAction g (ofGenerator (.dbarψ t α)) =
      (t.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        g.phase p.1 • ofGenerator (.dbarψ p.2 α)).sum

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.antidiagonal_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma antidiagonal_singleton (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ({μ} : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)).antidiagonal = {(0, {μ}), ({μ}, 0)}

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_ofGenerator_dψ_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_ofGenerator_dψ_zero {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    gaugeAction g (ofGenerator (.dψ 0 α)) =
      star (g.phase 0) • ofGenerator (.dψ 0 α)

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_ofGenerator_dbarψ_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_ofGenerator_dbarψ_zero {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    gaugeAction g (ofGenerator (.dbarψ 0 α)) =
      g.phase 0 • ofGenerator (.dbarψ 0 α)

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_ofGenerator_dψ_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_ofGenerator_dψ_singleton {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e)
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    gaugeAction g (ofGenerator (.dψ {μ} α)) =
      star (g.phase 0) • ofGenerator (.dψ {μ} α) +
        star (g.phase {μ}) • ofGenerator (.dψ 0 α)

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_ofGenerator_dbarψ_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_ofGenerator_dbarψ_singleton {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e)
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    gaugeAction g (ofGenerator (.dbarψ {μ} α)) =
      g.phase 0 • ofGenerator (.dbarψ {μ} α) +
        g.phase {μ} • ofGenerator (.dbarψ 0 α)

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.spinorRep
declarations.doc:
The Dirac spinor representation of `SL(2,ℂ)` in the chiral basis: the two
Weyl components transform in the two conjugate-dual fundamental
representations, `S(M) = ((M, 0), (0, (M†)⁻¹))`, the assignment being fixed
by the conventions of `Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spinorRep (M : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    Matrix (Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) (Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) ℂ

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.lorentzActionGenerator
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on a single electron jet coordinate: the spinor index
is rotated by the spinor representation (its conjugate for `∂_s ψ̄`) and the
derivative indices are transported with `Λ(M)⁻¹`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def lorentzActionGenerator (M : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    JetGenerators → JetComponentSpace

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.lorentzActionCS
declarations.doc: The Lorentz action on the jet component space.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def lorentzActionCS (M : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    JetComponentSpace →ₗ[ℂ] JetComponentSpace

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.lorentzActionCS_single
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzActionCS_single (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (j : JetGenerators) :
    lorentzActionCS M (Finsupp.single j 1) = lorentzActionGenerator M j

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on the electron jet algebra: the algebra map induced by
the action on the jet coordinates.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def lorentzAction (M : SL(2,ℂ)) : JetAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_ofGenerator_dψ_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_ofGenerator_dψ_zero (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    lorentzAction M (ofGenerator (.dψ 0 α)) =
      ∑ β, spinorRep M α β • ofGenerator (.dψ 0 β)

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_ofGenerator_dbarψ_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_ofGenerator_dbarψ_zero (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    lorentzAction M (ofGenerator (.dbarψ 0 α)) =
      ∑ β, star (spinorRep M α β) • ofGenerator (.dbarψ 0 β)

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_ofGenerator_dψ_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_ofGenerator_dψ_singleton (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (σ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    lorentzAction M (ofGenerator (.dψ {σ} α)) =
      ∑ τ, ∑ β, ((((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup M)⁻¹).1 τ σ : ℝ) • spinorRep M α β) •
        ofGenerator (.dψ {τ} β)

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_ofGenerator_dbarψ_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_ofGenerator_dbarψ_singleton (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (σ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    lorentzAction M (ofGenerator (.dbarψ {σ} α)) =
      ∑ τ, ∑ β, ((((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup M)⁻¹).1 τ σ : ℝ) •
          star (spinorRep M α β)) • ofGenerator (.dbarψ {τ} β)

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.massScaleCS
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight scaling on the jet component space: the diagonal map
multiplying each jet coordinate by `c` to the power of its mass weight.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def massScaleCS (c : ℝ) : JetComponentSpace →ₗ[ℂ] JetComponentSpace

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.massScale
declarations.doc: The mass-weight scaling on the electron jet algebra.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def massScale (c : ℝ) : JetAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.massScale_ofGenerator
declarations.statement:
lemma massScale_ofGenerator (c : ℝ) (j : JetGenerators) :
    massScale c (ofGenerator j) = (c : ℂ) ^ j.massWeight • ofGenerator j

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetGenerators.shift
declarations.doc: The jet coordinate with one further derivative in the direction `ρ`.
declarations.statement: def JetGenerators.shift (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : JetGenerators → JetGenerators

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.jetDerivCS
declarations.doc:
The total derivative on the jet component space: the shift of the
derivative multi-index.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetDerivCS (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    JetComponentSpace →ₗ[ℂ] JetComponentSpace

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.jetDerivCS_single
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDerivCS_single (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (j : JetGenerators) :
    jetDerivCS ρ (Finsupp.single j 1) =
      Finsupp.single (JetGenerators.shift ρ j) 1

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.jetDerivGen
declarations.doc:
The generator map of the total derivative into the trivial square-zero
extension of the jet algebra: `ι x ↦ (ι x, ι (∂_ρ x))`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetDerivGen (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    JetComponentSpace →ₗ[ℂ] TrivSqZeroExt JetAlgebra JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.jetDerivGen_fst
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDerivGen_fst (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : JetComponentSpace) :
    (jetDerivGen ρ x).fst = ExteriorAlgebra.ι ℂ x

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.jetDerivGen_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDerivGen_snd (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : JetComponentSpace) :
    (jetDerivGen ρ x).snd = ExteriorAlgebra.ι ℂ (jetDerivCS ρ x)

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.jetDerivGen_mul_self
declarations.doc:
The generator map squares to zero: degree-one elements of the exterior
algebra anticommute.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDerivGen_mul_self (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : JetComponentSpace) :
    jetDerivGen ρ x * jetDerivGen ρ x = 0

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.jetDerivHom
declarations.doc:
The lift of the total derivative to the trivial square-zero extension of
the jet algebra: the algebra homomorphism `x ↦ (x, ∂_ρ x)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetDerivHom (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    JetAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] TrivSqZeroExt JetAlgebra JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.jetDerivHom_ι
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDerivHom_ι (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : JetComponentSpace) :
    jetDerivHom ρ (ExteriorAlgebra.ι ℂ x) = jetDerivGen ρ x

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.jetDerivHom_fst
declarations.doc: The first component of the square-zero lift is the identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDerivHom_fst (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : JetAlgebra) :
    (jetDerivHom ρ x).fst = x

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv
declarations.doc:
The formal total spacetime derivative on the electron jet algebra in the
direction `ρ`: the even derivation extending the shift
`∂_s ψ_α ↦ ∂_{s + {ρ}} ψ_α` of the jet coordinates.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def jetDeriv (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : JetAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_apply (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : JetAlgebra) :
    jetDeriv ρ x = (jetDerivHom ρ x).snd

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv_ι
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_ι (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : JetComponentSpace) :
    jetDeriv ρ (ExteriorAlgebra.ι ℂ x) =
      ExteriorAlgebra.ι ℂ (jetDerivCS ρ x)

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv_ofGenerator
declarations.doc:
The total derivative appends the derivative index to each jet
coordinate.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_ofGenerator (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (j : JetGenerators) :
    jetDeriv ρ (ofGenerator j) = ofGenerator (JetGenerators.shift ρ j)

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv_one
declarations.statement: lemma jetDeriv_one (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : jetDeriv ρ (1 : JetAlgebra) = 0

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv_mul
declarations.doc:
The total derivative is an even derivation: the Leibniz rule holds on the
electron jet algebra with no Koszul signs.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_mul (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x y : JetAlgebra) :
    jetDeriv ρ (x * y) = jetDeriv ρ x * y + x * jetDeriv ρ y

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The jet algebra of quantum electrodynamics: the tensor product of the
complexified photon jet algebra with the electron jet algebra.

This is a `def` rather than an `abbrev`, and its algebraic structure is fixed
by the single `Ring` and `Algebra` instances below, so that every algebraic
class projects from one root.  On the bare tensor product `One`, `Mul`,
`Zero`, `Add`, `SMul` and `Module` are instead supplied by standalone
`TensorProduct.*` instances rather than as projections of the semiring; those
are definitionally the projections, but not syntactically, so a generic lemma
whose type argument is not pinned by an explicit argument (such as `one_pow`)
cannot be unified against a goal.  Rooting the structure here keeps the
generic algebraic lemmas usable.
declarations.statement: def JetAlgebra : Type
noncomputable instance : Ring JetAlgebra
noncomputable instance : Algebra ℂ JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.tmul
declarations.doc:
A pure tensor, as an element of the jet algebra.

Writing `a ⊗ₜ[ℂ] b` builds an element of the *underlying* tensor product,
which is only definitionally an element of `JetAlgebra`.  A goal mixing such
a term with the jet algebra's own operations is then not type-correct at
`instances` transparency, and no rewrite can fire on it.  This constructor
keeps pure tensors typed at `JetAlgebra`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tmul (a : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra) (b : Electron.JetAlgebra) :
    JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.tmul_eq
declarations.doc:
`tmul` is the pure tensor of the underlying tensor product; use this to
move between the jet algebra and lemmas stated for the tensor product.
declarations.statement:
lemma tmul_eq (a : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra) (b : Electron.JetAlgebra) :
    a ⊗ⱼ b = a ⊗ₜ[ℂ] b

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.one_eq_tmul
declarations.statement: lemma one_eq_tmul : (1 : JetAlgebra) = (1 : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra) ⊗ⱼ 1

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.tmul_mul_tmul
declarations.doc:
Multiplication of pure tensors. `Algebra.TensorProduct.tmul_mul_tmul` does
not rewrite here, even though it is definitionally the same statement.
declarations.statement:
lemma tmul_mul_tmul (a₁ a₂ : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra)
    (b₁ b₂ : Electron.JetAlgebra) :
    (a₁ ⊗ⱼ b₁) * (a₂ ⊗ⱼ b₂) = (a₁ * a₂) ⊗ⱼ (b₁ * b₂)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.zero_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma zero_tmul (b : Electron.JetAlgebra) :
    (0 : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra) ⊗ⱼ b = 0

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.tmul_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma tmul_zero (a : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra) :
    a ⊗ⱼ (0 : Electron.JetAlgebra) = 0

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.add_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma add_tmul (a₁ a₂ : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra) (b : Electron.JetAlgebra) :
    (a₁ + a₂) ⊗ⱼ b = a₁ ⊗ⱼ b + a₂ ⊗ⱼ b

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.tmul_add
declarations.statement:
lemma tmul_add (a : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra) (b₁ b₂ : Electron.JetAlgebra) :
    a ⊗ⱼ (b₁ + b₂) = a ⊗ⱼ b₁ + a ⊗ⱼ b₂

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.sub_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma sub_tmul (a₁ a₂ : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra) (b : Electron.JetAlgebra) :
    (a₁ - a₂) ⊗ⱼ b = a₁ ⊗ⱼ b - a₂ ⊗ⱼ b

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.tmul_sub
declarations.statement:
lemma tmul_sub (a : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra) (b₁ b₂ : Electron.JetAlgebra) :
    a ⊗ⱼ (b₁ - b₂) = a ⊗ⱼ b₁ - a ⊗ⱼ b₂

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.neg_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma neg_tmul (a : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra) (b : Electron.JetAlgebra) :
    (-a) ⊗ⱼ b = -(a ⊗ⱼ b)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.tmul_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma tmul_neg (a : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra) (b : Electron.JetAlgebra) :
    a ⊗ⱼ (-b) = -(a ⊗ⱼ b)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.tmul_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma tmul_sum {ι : Type*} (a : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra) (s : Finset ι)
    (f : ι → Electron.JetAlgebra) : a ⊗ⱼ (∑ i ∈ s, f i) = ∑ i ∈ s, a ⊗ⱼ f i

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.sum_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_tmul {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra)
    (b : Electron.JetAlgebra) : (∑ i ∈ s, f i) ⊗ⱼ b = ∑ i ∈ s, f i ⊗ⱼ b

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.tmul_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma tmul_smul (r : ℂ) (a : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra) (b : Electron.JetAlgebra) :
    a ⊗ⱼ (r • b) = r • (a ⊗ⱼ b)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.smul_tmul'
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_tmul' (r : ℂ) (a : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra) (b : Electron.JetAlgebra) :
    (r • a) ⊗ⱼ b = r • (a ⊗ⱼ b)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.real_smul_tmul
declarations.doc: An `ℝ`-scalar on the photon factor is a `ℂ`-scalar of the jet algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma real_smul_tmul (r : ℝ) (a : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra)
    (b : Electron.JetAlgebra) :
    (r • a) ⊗ⱼ b = (r : ℂ) • (a ⊗ⱼ b)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.tmul_C_eq_smul_one
declarations.doc: A constant of the photon factor is a scalar of the jet algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma tmul_C_eq_smul_one (r : ℝ) :
    ((1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] (MvPolynomial.C r : Photon.JetAlgebra)) ⊗ⱼ
        (1 : Electron.JetAlgebra) = (r : ℂ) • (1 : JetAlgebra)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.induction_on
declarations.doc:
Induction on the jet algebra, stated for `JetAlgebra` itself.  Using
`TensorProduct.inductionOn` directly leaves the sum and the pure tensors in
the goals carrying the tensor product's structure rather than the jet
algebra's, which makes those goals unrewritable.
declarations.statement:
lemma induction_on {motive : JetAlgebra → Prop} (x : JetAlgebra)
    (tmul : ∀ (a : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra) (b : Electron.JetAlgebra),
      motive (a ⊗ⱼ b))
    (add : ∀ x y : JetAlgebra, motive x → motive y → motive (x + y)) : motive x

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.inclA
declarations.doc: The photon factor included into the QED jet algebra.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev inclA : (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra) →ₐ[ℂ] JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.inclE
declarations.doc: The electron factor included into the QED jet algebra.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev inclE : Electron.JetAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.inclA_apply
declarations.statement: lemma inclA_apply (a : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra) : inclA a = a ⊗ⱼ 1

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.inclE_apply
declarations.statement: lemma inclE_apply (b : Electron.JetAlgebra) : inclE b = 1 ⊗ⱼ b

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeActionPhoton
declarations.doc:
The gauge action on the complexified photon jet algebra: the
complexification of the affine action `∂_s A_μ ↦ ∂_s A_μ + ∂_s ∂_μ χ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def gaugeActionPhoton (c : Photon.JetAlgebra.GaugeJet) :
    (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra) →ₐ[ℂ] ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeActionPhoton_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeActionPhoton_tmul (c : Photon.JetAlgebra.GaugeJet) (x : ℂ)
    (p : Photon.JetAlgebra) :
    gaugeActionPhoton c (x ⊗ₜ[ℝ] p) = x ⊗ₜ[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction c p

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction
declarations.doc:
The gauge action on the QED jet algebra: the tensor product of the affine
action on the photon factor with the Leibniz phase rotation on the electron
factor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def gaugeAction {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) :
    JetAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_tmul {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) (a : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra)
    (b : Electron.JetAlgebra) :
    gaugeAction g (a ⊗ⱼ b) =
      gaugeActionPhoton g.χjet a ⊗ⱼ Electron.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction g b

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.lorentzActionPhoton
declarations.doc: The Lorentz action on the complexified photon jet algebra.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def lorentzActionPhoton (Λ : LorentzGroup 3) :
    (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra) →ₐ[ℂ] ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.lorentzActionPhoton_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzActionPhoton_tmul (Λ : LorentzGroup 3) (x : ℂ) (p : Photon.JetAlgebra) :
    lorentzActionPhoton Λ (x ⊗ₜ[ℝ] p) = x ⊗ₜ[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction Λ p

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on the QED jet algebra: the tensor product of the
photon action through the covering map with the electron spinor action.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def lorentzAction (M : SL(2,ℂ)) : JetAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzAction_tmul (M : SL(2,ℂ)) (a : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra)
    (b : Electron.JetAlgebra) :
    lorentzAction M (a ⊗ⱼ b) =
      lorentzActionPhoton (Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup M) a ⊗ⱼ
        Electron.JetAlgebra.lorentzAction M b

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.massScalePhoton
declarations.doc: The mass-weight scaling on the complexified photon jet algebra.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def massScalePhoton (c : ℝ) :
    (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra) →ₐ[ℂ] ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.massScalePhoton_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma massScalePhoton_tmul (c : ℝ) (x : ℂ) (p : Photon.JetAlgebra) :
    massScalePhoton c (x ⊗ₜ[ℝ] p) = x ⊗ₜ[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra.massScale c p

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.massScale
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight scaling on the QED jet algebra: the algebra map
multiplying each jet coordinate by `c` to the power of its mass weight,
i.e. `c` squared to the power of its mass dimension.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def massScale (c : ℝ) : JetAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.massScale_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma massScale_tmul (c : ℝ) (a : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra)
    (b : Electron.JetAlgebra) :
    massScale c (a ⊗ⱼ b) =
      massScalePhoton c a ⊗ⱼ Electron.JetAlgebra.massScale c b

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv
declarations.doc:
The formal total spacetime derivative on the QED jet algebra in the
direction `ρ`: the Leibniz extension of the total derivatives of the photon
and electron factors.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def jetDeriv (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : JetAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] JetAlgebra

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_tmul (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Photon.JetAlgebra)
    (b : Electron.JetAlgebra) :
    jetDeriv ρ (a ⊗ⱼ b) =
      (LinearMap.baseChange ℂ (Photon.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv ρ) a) ⊗ⱼ b +
        a ⊗ⱼ Electron.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv ρ b

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv_one
declarations.statement: lemma jetDeriv_one (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : jetDeriv ρ (1 : JetAlgebra) = 0

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.jetDeriv_mul
declarations.doc:
The total derivative is an even derivation on the QED jet algebra: the
Leibniz rule holds with no Koszul signs.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_mul (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x y : JetAlgebra) :
    jetDeriv ρ (x * y) = jetDeriv ρ x * y + x * jetDeriv ρ y

modules.title: The current coupling of quantum electrodynamics
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The interaction of QED is *minimal coupling to the Dirac current*: expanding
the covariant derivative inside the Dirac kinetic term,

`i ψ̄ γ^μ D_μ ψ = i ψ̄ γ^μ ∂_μ ψ - e J^μ A_μ`  with  `J^μ = ψ̄ γ^μ ψ`.

This is the jet-algebra counterpart of the current coupling `J^μ A_μ` of
`Physlib.Electromagnetism.Dynamics.Lagrangian`: the photon couples to matter
only through a conserved current contracted with the potential, with the
electron supplying `J^μ = ψ̄ γ^μ ψ`.

The current is gauge invariant (`gaugeAction_diracCurrent`) — the electron
and its conjugate carry opposite charges, so the phases cancel — which is
what makes it a physically meaningful source for the photon.

This file contains no definitions, only theorems about the fields of
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Fields` and the Lagrangian of `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Lagrangian`.

## ii. Key results

- `JetAlgebra.diracKineticTerm_eq_free_add_current` : **minimal coupling** —
  the Dirac kinetic term is the free kinetic term plus `- e J^μ A_μ`.
- `JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_diracCurrent` : the Dirac current is gauge
  invariant.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The minimal-coupling decomposition of the kinetic term
- B. Gauge invariance of the Dirac current
- C. Noether: conservation of the Dirac current on-shell

## iv. References

The current is defined in `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Lagrangian`; the concrete
electromagnetic current coupling is
`Physlib.Electromagnetism.Dynamics.Lagrangian`.

## A. The minimal-coupling decomposition of the kinetic term

The photon coordinates commute with the fermion coordinates
(`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.FermionStatistics`), so the interaction inside the kinetic term
reorganises into the potential times the Dirac current.
## B. Gauge invariance of the Dirac current
## C. Noether: conservation of the Dirac current on-shell

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.A_mul_diracCurrent
declarations.doc:
The photon potential times the Dirac current, written through the fermion
bilinears.
declarations.statement:
lemma A_mul_diracCurrent (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    A 0 μ * diracCurrent μ =
      ∑ α, ∑ β, kineticGamma μ α β • (A 0 μ * (barψ 0 α * ψ 0 β))

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.diracKineticTerm_eq_free_add_current
declarations.doc:
**Minimal coupling**: the Dirac kinetic term with coupling `e` is the free
Dirac kinetic term plus the current coupling `- e J^μ A_μ`.  All of the
interaction of QED is the photon contracted with the Dirac current, the
jet-algebra counterpart of the current coupling of
`Physlib.Electromagnetism.Dynamics`.
declarations.statement:
lemma diracKineticTerm_eq_free_add_current (e : ℝ) :
    diracKineticTerm e = diracKineticTerm 0 +
      (-e : ℂ) • ∑ μ, A 0 μ * diracCurrent μ

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_diracCurrent
declarations.doc:
**The Dirac current is gauge invariant**: the electron and its conjugate
carry opposite charges, so the phases cancel by unitarity.  This is what
makes `J^μ` a physically meaningful source for the photon.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAction_diracCurrent {e : ℝ} (g : GaugeJet e) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    gaugeAction g (diracCurrent μ) = diracCurrent μ

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.current_conservation
declarations.doc:
**Noether's identity for the Dirac current**: the divergence of the
current is a combination of the Dirac-equation elements,
`i ∂_μ J^μ = ψ̄ ⬝ (Dirac eq) + (adjoint Dirac eq) ⬝ ψ`.
On solutions of the Dirac equations the current is conserved,
`∂_μ J^μ = 0` — for every coupling `e` and mass `m`: the gauge interaction
and the mass drop out of the divergence identically.
declarations.statement:
lemma current_conservation (e m : ℝ) :
    Complex.I • ∑ μ, jetDeriv μ (diracCurrent μ) =
      ∑ α, barψ 0 α * diracEquation e m α +
        ∑ β, diracAdjEquation e m β * ψ 0 β

modules.title: Evaluation of the photon jet algebra on a potential
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The theorems tying the formal photon jet algebra of QED to the honest
electromagnetism of `Physlib.Electromagnetism`, through the evaluation map
`Photon.JetAlgebra.evalPotential` of `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Basic`:

* evaluated on any differentiable potential, the formal field strength is the
  field strength of the potential with both indices lowered;
* evaluated on any differentiable potential, the formal Maxwell term
  `F_{μν} F^{μν}` is `-4 μ₀` times `ElectromagneticPotential.kineticTerm`;
* the evaluation is compatible with concrete gauge transformations
  `A ↦ A + ∂χ`, matching the formal gauge invariance of
  `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.GaugeInvariance` on the concrete side.

Only the photon sector evaluates: fermionic jet coordinates would have to be
evaluated on anticommuting (Grassmann-valued) fields, which have no
realisation as honest functions on spacetime.

This file contains no definitions, only theorems.

## ii. Key results

- `Photon.JetAlgebra.evalPotential_fieldStrength_zero` : the formal field
  strength evaluates to the field strength.
- `Photon.JetAlgebra.evalPotential_maxwellTerm` : **the formal Maxwell term
  is the Maxwell Lagrangian**.
- `Photon.JetAlgebra.electricField_eq_evalPotential_fieldStrength`,
  `Photon.JetAlgebra.magneticField_eq_evalPotential_fieldStrength` : the
  time–space and space–space components of the evaluated formal field
  strength are the electric and magnetic fields.
- `Photon.JetAlgebra.evalPotential_neg_quarter_maxwellTerm` : the Maxwell
  part of the QED Lagrangian is `μ₀` times the electromagnetic kinetic term.
- `Photon.JetAlgebra.evalPotential_fieldStrength_gaugeTransform`,
  `Photon.JetAlgebra.evalPotential_maxwellTerm_gaugeTransform` :
  compatibility with concrete gauge transformations.
- `Photon.JetAlgebra.evalPotential_maxwell_homogeneous` : **the homogeneous
  Maxwell equations**, as the evaluation of the formal Bianchi identity.
- `Photon.JetAlgebra.evalPotential_fieldStrength_lorentzAction` :
  compatibility of the formal and concrete Lorentz actions.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Evaluation of the field strength
- B. The Maxwell term is the Maxwell Lagrangian
- C. B'. The electric and magnetic fields from the jet algebra
- D. B''. The Maxwell part of the QED Lagrangian
- E. First-order jets and the homogeneous Maxwell equations
- F. D'. The inhomogeneous Maxwell equations and the action principle
- G. Compatibility with concrete Lorentz transformations
- H. Compatibility with concrete gauge transformations

## iv. References

The evaluation map is defined in `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Basic`; the concrete side is
`Physlib/Electromagnetism/Kinematics/GaugeTransformation.lean` and
`Physlib/Electromagnetism/Dynamics/KineticTerm.lean`.

sections.text: ## A. Evaluation of the field strength
## B. The Maxwell term is the Maxwell Lagrangian

## C. B'. The electric and magnetic fields from the jet algebra

Splitting spacetime into time and space through `toTimeAndSpace`, the
time–space components of the evaluated formal field strength are the electric
field and the space–space components the magnetic field of
`Physlib.Electromagnetism`.
## D. B''. The Maxwell part of the QED Lagrangian

## E. First-order jets and the homogeneous Maxwell equations

Evaluation intertwines the first-order jet of the field strength with the
honest spacetime derivative — for a `C²` potential the sorted iterated
derivative is symmetric by Clairaut's theorem — and hence the formal Bianchi
identity of `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.FieldStrength` evaluates to **the homogeneous
Maxwell equations** in covariant form.

## F. D'. The inhomogeneous Maxwell equations and the action principle

The concrete side (`Physlib.Electromagnetism.Dynamics.IsExtrema`) proves
variationally that a potential extremises the electromagnetic action exactly
when `∂_μ F^{μν} = μ₀ J^ν`.  The left-hand side is the evaluation of the
formal Maxwell operator of `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Fields`, so the action
principle can be read entirely through the jet algebra.

## G. Compatibility with concrete Lorentz transformations

The formal Lorentz action of `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Basic` is matched by the concrete
action `(Λ • A) x = Λ • A (Λ⁻¹ • x)` of `Physlib.Electromagnetism`:
evaluating the field strength on the transformed potential is evaluating the
Lorentz-transformed jet on the original potential at the transformed point.

## H. Compatibility with concrete gauge transformations

The formal gauge invariance of `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.GaugeInvariance` is matched on
the concrete side: the evaluation of the field strength, and hence of the
Maxwell term, is unchanged when the potential is replaced by `A + ∂χ`.

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.deriv_coPotential
declarations.doc:
The derivative of a covariant component.  Differentiability is needed to move
the constant `η_{νν}` through the derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_coPotential (A : ElectromagneticPotential 3) (hA : Differentiable ℝ A)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : SpaceTime 3) :
    ∂_ μ (coPotential A ν) x = η ν ν * ∂_ μ A x ν

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.evalPotential_fieldStrength_zero_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma evalPotential_fieldStrength_zero_apply (A : ElectromagneticPotential 3)
    (hA : Differentiable ℝ A) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : SpaceTime 3) :
    evalPotential A (fieldStrength 0 μ ν) x = η ν ν * ∂_ μ A x ν - η μ μ * ∂_ ν A x μ

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.evalPotential_fieldStrength_zero
declarations.doc:
The formal field strength evaluates to the field strength of the potential
with both indices lowered, `F_{μν} = η_{μμ} η_{νν} F^{μν}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalPotential_fieldStrength_zero (A : ElectromagneticPotential 3)
    (hA : Differentiable ℝ A) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : SpaceTime 3) :
    evalPotential A (fieldStrength 0 μ ν) x =
      η μ μ * η ν ν * toScalar {A.toFieldStrength x | [μ] [ν]}ᵀ

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.evalPotential_maxwellTerm
declarations.doc:
**The formal Maxwell term is the Maxwell Lagrangian.**  Evaluated on any
differentiable electromagnetic potential, the gauge-invariant jet polynomial
`F_{μν} F^{μν}` is `-4 μ₀` times the kinetic term
`- 1/(4 μ₀) F_{μν} F^{μν}` of `Physlib.Electromagnetism`.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalPotential_maxwellTerm (𝓕 : FreeSpace) (A : ElectromagneticPotential 3)
    (hA : Differentiable ℝ A) (x : SpaceTime 3) :
    evalPotential A maxwellTerm x = -(4 * 𝓕.μ₀) * A.kineticTerm 𝓕 x

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.electricField_eq_evalPotential_fieldStrength
declarations.doc:
The electric field is (the speed of light times) the evaluated time–space
components of the formal field strength: `E_i = c ∂_0 A_i - c ∂_i A_0`
with lowered indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma electricField_eq_evalPotential_fieldStrength (c : SpeedOfLight)
    (A : ElectromagneticPotential 3) (hA : Differentiable ℝ A) (t : Time)
    (x : Space) (i : Fin 3) :
    A.electricField c t x i =
      c * evalPotential A (fieldStrength 0 (Sum.inl 0) (Sum.inr i))
        ((toTimeAndSpace c).symm (t, x))

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.magneticField_eq_evalPotential_fieldStrength
declarations.doc:
The magnetic field is the evaluated space–space components of the formal
field strength, `B_i = - F_{(i+1)(i+2)}` with lowered indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma magneticField_eq_evalPotential_fieldStrength (c : SpeedOfLight)
    (A : ElectromagneticPotential 3) (hA : Differentiable ℝ A) (t : Time)
    (x : Space) (i : Fin 3) :
    A.magneticField c t x i =
      - evalPotential A (fieldStrength 0 (Sum.inr (i + 1)) (Sum.inr (i + 2)))
        ((toTimeAndSpace c).symm (t, x))

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.evalPotential_neg_quarter_maxwellTerm
declarations.doc:
The Maxwell part `- 1/4 F_{μν} F^{μν}` of the QED Lagrangian evaluates to
`μ₀` times the electromagnetic kinetic term of
`Physlib.Electromagnetism.Dynamics`: the two Lagrangians agree up to the
choice of units absorbed into the field normalisation.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalPotential_neg_quarter_maxwellTerm (𝓕 : FreeSpace)
    (A : ElectromagneticPotential 3) (hA : Differentiable ℝ A) (x : SpaceTime 3) :
    evalPotential A ((-(1 : ℝ)/4) • maxwellTerm) x = 𝓕.μ₀ * A.kineticTerm 𝓕 x

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.contDiff_coPotential
declarations.statement:
lemma contDiff_coPotential {A : ElectromagneticPotential 3} (hA : ContDiff ℝ 2 A)
    (ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : ContDiff ℝ 2 (coPotential A ν)

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.derivMultiset_pair
declarations.doc:
The iterated derivative along a pair of directions, in either order: for a
`C²` function the canonical sorted order is immaterial by Clairaut's
theorem.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivMultiset_pair (a b : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (f : SpaceTime 3 → ℝ)
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 f) :
    derivMultiset {a, b} f = ∂_ a (∂_ b f)

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.deriv_sub_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_sub_eq {f g : SpaceTime 3 → ℝ} (lam : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) (hg : Differentiable ℝ g) :
    ∂_ lam (f - g) = ∂_ lam f - ∂_ lam g

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.evalPotential_fieldStrength_singleton
declarations.doc:
Evaluation intertwines the first-order jet with the spacetime derivative:
the evaluated `∂_lam F_{μν}` is the derivative of the evaluated `F_{μν}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalPotential_fieldStrength_singleton (A : ElectromagneticPotential 3)
    (hA : ContDiff ℝ 2 A) (lam μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    evalPotential A (fieldStrength {lam} μ ν) =
      ∂_ lam (evalPotential A (fieldStrength 0 μ ν))

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.evalPotential_maxwell_homogeneous
declarations.doc:
**The homogeneous Maxwell equations** in covariant form,
`∂_lam F_{μν} + ∂_μ F_{ν lam} + ∂_ν F_{lam μ} = 0`, as the evaluation of the
formal Bianchi identity of `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.FieldStrength`: Faraday's law and
the absence of magnetic monopoles are its time–space–space and
space–space–space components.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalPotential_maxwell_homogeneous (A : ElectromagneticPotential 3)
    (hA : ContDiff ℝ 2 A) (lam μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ∂_ lam (evalPotential A (fieldStrength 0 μ ν)) +
      ∂_ μ (evalPotential A (fieldStrength 0 ν lam)) +
      ∂_ ν (evalPotential A (fieldStrength 0 lam μ)) = 0

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.deriv_const_mul_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_const_mul_apply (c : ℝ) {f : SpaceTime 3 → ℝ} (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) (x : SpaceTime 3) :
    ∂_ ρ (fun y => c * f y) x = c * ∂_ ρ f x

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.isExtrema_iff_evalPotential_maxwellOperator
declarations.doc:
**The action principle through the jet algebra**: an electromagnetic
potential extremises the Maxwell action with source `J` exactly when the
evaluated formal Maxwell operator equals `μ₀ J` — the inhomogeneous Maxwell
equations `∂_μ F^{μν} = μ₀ J^ν`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isExtrema_iff_evalPotential_maxwellOperator (𝓕 : FreeSpace)
    (A : ElectromagneticPotential 3) (hA : ContDiff ℝ ∞ A)
    (J : LorentzCurrentDensity 3) (hJ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ J) :
    ElectromagneticPotential.IsExtrema 𝓕 A J ↔
      ∀ x ν, evalPotential A (maxwellOperator ν) x = 𝓕.μ₀ * J x ν

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.evalPotential_fieldStrength_lorentzAction
declarations.doc:
**Compatibility of the formal and concrete Lorentz actions**: the
evaluation of the field strength on `Λ • A` at `x` is the evaluation of its
formal Lorentz transform on `A` at `Λ⁻¹ • x`, matching the equivariance
`Physlib.Electromagnetism.Kinematics.FieldStrength.toFieldStrength_equivariant`
on the concrete side.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalPotential_fieldStrength_lorentzAction (Λ : LorentzGroup 3)
    (A : ElectromagneticPotential 3) (hA : Differentiable ℝ A)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : SpaceTime 3) :
    evalPotential (Λ • A) (fieldStrength 0 μ ν) x =
      evalPotential A (lorentzAction Λ (fieldStrength 0 μ ν)) (Λ⁻¹ • x)

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.differentiable_gaugeTransform
QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.evalPotential_fieldStrength_gaugeTransform
declarations.doc:
The evaluated field strength is invariant under the concrete gauge
transformation `A ↦ A + ∂χ`, matching the formal gauge invariance
`Physlib.Particles.QED.GaugeInvariance.Photon.JetAlgebra.gaugeAction_fieldStrength`.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalPotential_fieldStrength_gaugeTransform (A : ElectromagneticPotential 3)
    (χ : SpaceTime 3 → ℝ) (hA : Differentiable ℝ A) (hχ : ContDiff ℝ 2 χ)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : SpaceTime 3) :
    evalPotential (ElectromagneticPotential.gaugeTransform χ A) (fieldStrength 0 μ ν) x =
      evalPotential A (fieldStrength 0 μ ν) x

declarations.name: QED.Photon.JetAlgebra.evalPotential_maxwellTerm_gaugeTransform
declarations.doc: The Maxwell Lagrangian is gauge invariant, as read off from the jet algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalPotential_maxwellTerm_gaugeTransform (A : ElectromagneticPotential 3)
    (χ : SpaceTime 3 → ℝ) (hA : Differentiable ℝ A) (hχ : ContDiff ℝ 2 χ)
    (x : SpaceTime 3) :
    evalPotential (ElectromagneticPotential.gaugeTransform χ A) maxwellTerm x =
      evalPotential A maxwellTerm x

modules.title: Spin-statistics of the QED fields
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The statistics of the fields of QED, as encoded in the QED jet algebra: the
electron jet coordinates anticommute among themselves and square to zero
(fermionic statistics), while the photon jet coordinates commute with
everything (bosonic statistics).

This file contains no definitions, only theorems about the fields of
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Fields`.

## ii. Key results

- `Electron.JetAlgebra.ofGenerator_mul_self`,
  `Electron.JetAlgebra.ofGenerator_anticommute` : fermionic statistics of the
  electron jet coordinates.
- `JetAlgebra.ψ_mul_ψ_anticomm`, `JetAlgebra.ψ_mul_barψ_anticomm`,
  `JetAlgebra.barψ_mul_barψ_anticomm` : the electron coordinates anticommute
  in the QED jet algebra.
- `JetAlgebra.ψ_mul_self`, `JetAlgebra.barψ_mul_self` : Pauli exclusion for
  the jet coordinates.
- `JetAlgebra.A_mul_A_comm`, `JetAlgebra.A_mul_ψ_comm`,
  `JetAlgebra.A_mul_barψ_comm` : the photon coordinates are bosonic.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Fermionic statistics of the electron jet coordinates
- B. Fermionic statistics in the QED jet algebra
- C. Bosonic statistics of the photon jet coordinates

## iv. References

The fields are defined in `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Fields`.

## B. Fermionic statistics in the QED jet algebra
## C. Bosonic statistics of the photon jet coordinates

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.ofGenerator_mul_self
declarations.statement:
lemma ofGenerator_mul_self (j : JetGenerators) :
    ofGenerator j * ofGenerator j = 0

declarations.name: QED.Electron.JetAlgebra.ofGenerator_anticommute
declarations.doc:
The jet coordinates of the electron anticommute: the electron is a
fermion.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofGenerator_anticommute (i j : JetGenerators) :
    ofGenerator i * ofGenerator j = -(ofGenerator j * ofGenerator i)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.ψ_mul_ψ_anticomm
declarations.doc: The electron jet coordinates anticommute.
declarations.statement:
lemma ψ_mul_ψ_anticomm (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (α β : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    ψ s α * ψ t β = -(ψ t β * ψ s α)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.ψ_mul_barψ_anticomm
declarations.doc: The electron and conjugate-electron jet coordinates anticommute.
declarations.statement:
lemma ψ_mul_barψ_anticomm (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (α β : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    ψ s α * barψ t β = -(barψ t β * ψ s α)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.barψ_mul_barψ_anticomm
declarations.doc: The conjugate-electron jet coordinates anticommute.
declarations.statement:
lemma barψ_mul_barψ_anticomm (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (α β : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    barψ s α * barψ t β = -(barψ t β * barψ s α)

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.ψ_mul_self
declarations.doc: Pauli exclusion: an electron jet coordinate squares to zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma ψ_mul_self (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    ψ s α * ψ s α = 0

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.barψ_mul_self
declarations.doc: Pauli exclusion: a conjugate electron jet coordinate squares to zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma barψ_mul_self (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    barψ s α * barψ s α = 0

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.A_mul_A_comm
declarations.doc:
The photon jet coordinates commute among themselves: the photon is a
boson.
declarations.statement:
lemma A_mul_A_comm (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    A s μ * A t ν = A t ν * A s μ

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.A_mul_ψ_comm
declarations.doc: The photon jet coordinates commute with the electron jet coordinates.
declarations.statement:
lemma A_mul_ψ_comm (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    A s μ * ψ t α = ψ t α * A s μ

declarations.name: QED.JetAlgebra.A_mul_barψ_comm
declarations.doc:
The photon jet coordinates commute with the conjugate electron jet
coordinates.
declarations.statement:
lemma A_mul_barψ_comm (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (α : Fin 2 ⊕ Fin 2) :
    A s μ * barψ t α = barψ t α * A s μ

modules.title: The fields of quantum electrodynamics
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The fields of QED, defined on top of the jet algebras of `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Basic`:
the photon and electron jet coordinates as elements of the QED jet algebra,
the field strength, the Maxwell term, the Dirac γ matrices in the chiral
representation, and the covariant derivatives of the electron and its
conjugate.

This file contains only definitions; the theorems about these fields are
proved in `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.FermionStatistics`,
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.FieldStrength`,
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.GammaMatrices`, `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.GaugeInvariance` and
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Evaluation`, and the Lagrangian built from them is defined in
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Lagrangian`.

## ii. Key results

- `Photon.JetAlgebra.fieldStrength`, `Photon.JetAlgebra.maxwellTerm` : the
  field strength and the Maxwell term in the photon jet algebra.
- `JetAlgebra.A`, `JetAlgebra.ψ`, `JetAlgebra.barψ` : the jet coordinates of
  QED.
- `JetAlgebra.fieldStrength`, `JetAlgebra.maxwellTerm` : the field strength
  and the Maxwell term in the QED jet algebra.
- `JetAlgebra.gammaMatrix`, `JetAlgebra.kineticGamma` : the γ matrices in the
  chiral representation and the contraction matrices `γ⁰ γ^μ`.
- `JetAlgebra.covDψ`, `JetAlgebra.covDbarψ` : the covariant derivatives.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The field strength and Maxwell term of the photon
- B. The jet coordinates of QED
- C. The γ matrices in the chiral representation
- D. The covariant derivatives

## iv. References

The jet algebras are defined in `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Basic`; the Lagrangian is
defined in `PhyslibAlpha.Particles.QED.Lagrangian`.

sections.text: ## A. The field strength and Maxwell term of the photon

## B. The jet coordinates of QED

The photon jet coordinate `∂_s A_μ` and the electron jet coordinates
`∂_s ψ_α`, `∂_s ψ̄_α`, as elements of the QED jet algebra, together with the
field strength and the Maxwell term.

## C. The γ matrices in the chiral representation

In the chiral representation `γ^μ = ((0, σ^μ), (σ̄^μ, 0))` with
`σ^μ = (1, σ^i)` and `σ̄^μ = (1, -σ^i)`; since the Minkowski matrix is
diagonal, `σ̄^μ = η_{μμ} σ^μ` with no sum over `μ`.

## D. The covariant derivatives

The electron has electric charge `-1`, so `D_μ ψ = ∂_μ ψ + i e A_μ ψ` and
`D_μ ψ̄ = ∂_μ ψ̄ - i e A_μ ψ̄`, with `e` the electric coupling.
