declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.commute_of_mem_gaugeAlgebra_of_mem_fermionAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The gauge algebra and the fermion algebra commute element-wise: every generator of
the gauge algebra commutes with every generator of the fermion algebra by the
structure fields `h.F_comm_d`, ..., `h.F_comm_bare`, and commutation extends from
generators to the algebras they generate.

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.fermionMassWeight_mul_gaugeMassWeight_le
declarations.doc:
The fermion sector's mass-weight submodules and the gauge sector's mass-weight
submodules commute past each other, in the order needed by
`sectorMassWeight_pair_le`.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionMassWeight_mul_gaugeMassWeight_le (a b : ℕ) :
    h.isFermionSector.massWeightSubmodule a * h.isGaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule b
      ≤ h.isGaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule b * h.isFermionSector.massWeightSubmodule a

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_le
declarations.doc:
**The mixed gauge-fermion sector decomposition.** The weight-`w` piece of the
`{gauge, fermion}` sector lies in the join, over the splittings of `w` into two
non-zero parts, of the products of the gauge and fermion sectors' own mass-weight
submodules.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_le (w : ℕ) :
    h.sectorMassWeight {GeneratorClass.gauge, GeneratorClass.fermion} w
      ≤ ⨆ (p : ℕ × ℕ) (_ : p.1 + p.2 = w) (_ : p.1 ≠ 0) (_ : p.2 ≠ 0),
        h.isGaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule p.1 * h.isFermionSector.massWeightSubmodule p.2

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_eq_bot_of_lt_seven
declarations.doc:
**The mixed gauge-fermion sector vanishes below weight `7`.** A non-zero gauge
weight is at least `4` and a non-zero fermion weight is at least `3`, so no
splitting of a weight below `7` into two non-zero parts can supply both.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_eq_bot_of_lt_seven {w : ℕ} (hw : w < 7) :
    h.sectorMassWeight {GeneratorClass.gauge, GeneratorClass.fermion} w = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_eight
declarations.doc:
**The mixed gauge-fermion sector vanishes at weight `8`.** The only splittings of
`8` into two non-zero parts with a non-zero gauge weight and a non-zero fermion
weight would need the gauge part to be `4` or `6`(with fermion part `4` or `2`), but
the fermion sector vanishes at both `4` and `2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_eight :
    h.sectorMassWeight {GeneratorClass.gauge, GeneratorClass.fermion} 8 = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_seven
declarations.doc:
**The mixed gauge-fermion sector at weight `7`** is exactly the product of the
underived field-strength submodule with the underived fermion submodule: the only
splitting of `7` into a non-zero gauge weight and a non-zero fermion weight that
survives is `4 + 3`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_seven :
    h.sectorMassWeight {GeneratorClass.gauge, GeneratorClass.fermion} 7
      = h.isGaugeSector.derivSubmodule 0 * h.isFermionSector.derivSubmodule 0

modules.title: The gauge-fermion invariants below mass weight nine
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The mixed `{gauge, fermion}` sector is almost empty below weight nine, and what little
there is cannot be invariant. A field-strength tower weighs at least four and a fermion
tower at least three, so the sector vanishes below weight seven; at weight eight the two
splittings that arithmetic allows are `4 + 4` and `6 + 2`, and the fermion sector is
trivial at both four and two, so weight eight vanishes too. That leaves weight seven, the
single product `F ψ` of the underived field strength against the underived fermion towers.

Weight seven is barred from carrying an invariant by the same parity count on spin that
empties the Yukawa sector at weights five and seven. The field strength is of integer spin,
its two covector indices and its derivative slots all mixing by the Lorentz matrix and its
adjoint index not seeing the Lorentz group at all, while a fermion carries one Weyl-spinor
index. The one product at weight seven has exactly one fermion factor, so it is of
half-integer spin; and a half-integer spin carries no Lorentz invariant.

The machinery is the Yukawa sector's: `mul_le_centreEigenspace` multiplies the signs the
two factors carry at the centre of `SL(2,ℂ)`, and
`mem_of_invariant_of_mem_sup_centreEigenspace_neg_one` turns the sign `-1` into the absence
of invariants modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule. Only the left-hand factor changes: the
Higgs sign `+1` is replaced by the gauge one, which is `+1` for the same reason.


The bound is `w < 9` rather than `w < 8`: weight eight is as empty as the weights below
seven, so nothing is gained by stopping short of the first weight the sector can occupy.

## ii. Key results

- `gaugeFermion_le_centreEigenspace` : a field-strength derivative submodule against a fermion one
  is of half-integer spin: `+1` times `-1`
- `mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_seven_sup`
- `mem_of_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_lt_nine_sup`
- `mem_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff` : the
  classification below mass weight nine as an equivalence, in the shape of the gauge- and
  Yukawa-sector statements: an element of `sectorMassWeight {gauge, fermion} w ⊔ S` for `w < 9` is
  fixed by both groups exactly when it is itself an element of `S` fixed by both groups

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Integer field strength against half-integer fermion
- B. Mass weight seven
- C. The classification below mass weight nine

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Integer field strength against half-integer fermion

The signs the two factors carry at the centre are already proved: the field-strength
derivative submodules carry `+1`, every one of their indices being inert there, and the
fermion ones carry `-1`, the Weyl-spinor value index doing the work. The Lorentz action on
`B` is by algebra maps, so the product carries `+1` times `-1`.

## B. Mass weight seven

Weight seven is the single product `F ψ`, the underived field strength against the
underived fermion towers. It has exactly one fermion factor, so section A gives it the sign
`-1`, and a subspace of sign `-1` carries no invariant modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule.

## C. The classification below mass weight nine

The nine weights below nine are now settled: the sector vanishes below weight seven and
again at weight eight, and weight seven is section B. So below weight nine the
gauge-fermion sector supplies no invariant beyond what `S` already carries, and the
equivalences record it in the shape the other sectors carry, so that all of them can be
combined.

No lower bound on the weight is needed. The sector is the two-class sector of the gauge
and fermion generators, so both classes must be present with a non-zero weight and the
sector is already trivial at weight zero; the scalars, which force `0 < w` in the
gauge-sector statement, never appear.

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_seven_sup
declarations.doc:
Mass weight seven carries no Lorentz invariant modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule: a
Lorentz invariant of `sectorMassWeight {gauge, fermion} 7 ⊔ S` lies in `S`. The weight is
the underived field strength against the underived fermion towers, of half-integer
spin.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_seven_sup (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ h.sectorMassWeight {GeneratorClass.gauge, GeneratorClass.fermion} 7 ⊔ S)
    (hL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mem_of_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_lt_nine_sup
declarations.doc:
Below mass weight nine the gauge-fermion sector carries no Lorentz invariant: a
Lorentz invariant of `sectorMassWeight {gauge, fermion} w ⊔ S` for `w < 9` lies in `S`.
Weights below seven and weight eight are trivial submodules, and weight seven is section
B.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_lt_nine_sup (w : ℕ) (hw : w < 9)
    (S : Submodule ℂ B) (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ h.sectorMassWeight {GeneratorClass.gauge, GeneratorClass.fermion} w ⊔ S)
    (hL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mem_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
declarations.doc:
The classification below mass weight nine as an equivalence, in the shape of the gauge-
and Yukawa-sector statements: an element of `sectorMassWeight {gauge, fermion} w ⊔ S` for
`w < 9` is fixed by both groups exactly when it is itself an element of `S` fixed by both
groups. Gauge stability of `S` is not needed, and neither is gauge invariance of `x`: the
forward direction is the boost-weight parity argument, which uses the Lorentz group
alone.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
    (w : ℕ) (hw : w < 9) (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.sectorMassWeight {GeneratorClass.gauge, GeneratorClass.fermion} w ⊔ S
        ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x) ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g y = y)
          ∧ x = y

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mem_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
declarations.doc:
The same classification without the existential: below mass weight nine an element of
`sectorMassWeight {gauge, fermion} w ⊔ S` fixed by both groups is an element of `S` fixed
by both groups, and conversely.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sectorMassWeight_gauge_fermion_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
    (w : ℕ) (hw : w < 9) (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.sectorMassWeight {GeneratorClass.gauge, GeneratorClass.fermion} w ⊔ S
        ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x) ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)
      ↔ (x ∈ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
          ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)

modules.title: The mixed gauge-Higgs sector
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The field-strength towers are bosonic, so they commute with every Higgs tower
(`h.F_comm_H`, `h.F_comm_barH`); consequently the gauge algebra and the Higgs algebra
commute (`commute_of_mem_gaugeAlgebra_of_mem_higgsAlgebra`), and so do their
mass-weight submodules in either order (`higgsMassWeight_mul_gaugeMassWeight_le`).
Feeding this into the abstract two-class bound `sectorMassWeight_pair_le` gives the
mixed `{gauge, higgs}` sector's weight-`w` piece as a join, over the splittings of `w`
into two non-zero parts, of products of the two sectors' own mass-weight submodules
(`sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_le`).

Both a non-zero gauge weight and a non-zero Higgs weight are even, and they are at
least `4` and `2` respectively.  So the mixed sector vanishes below weight `6` and at
every odd weight; at weight `6` it is exactly the underived field strength against the
underived Higgs, and at weight `8` it is bounded by the field strength against the
weight-four Higgs terms together with the once-derived field strength against the
underived Higgs.

## ii. Key results

- `commute_of_mem_gaugeAlgebra_of_mem_higgsAlgebra` : the gauge algebra and the Higgs algebra
  commute element-wise
- `higgsMassWeight_mul_gaugeMassWeight_le` : the Higgs and gauge mass-weight submodules commute past
  each other
- `sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_le` : the mixed gauge-Higgs sector decomposition

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The mixed gauge-Higgs sector

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.doc:

`4 + 2`.

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mul_le_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs
declarations.doc:
A product of a gauge-weight piece and a Higgs-weight piece lands in the mixed
sector of the total weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_le_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs {a b w : ℕ} {X Y : Submodule ℂ B}
    (ha : a ≠ 0) (hb : b ≠ 0) (hab : a + b = w)
    (hX : X ≤ h.isGaugeSector.massWeightSubmodule a)
    (hY : Y ≤ h.isHiggsSector.massWeightSubmodule b) :
    X * Y ≤ h.sectorMassWeight {GeneratorClass.gauge, GeneratorClass.higgs} w

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_eight
declarations.doc:

`4 + 4` and `6 + 2`, giving the field strength against the weight-four Higgs terms
and the once-derived field strength against the underived Higgs.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_eight :
    h.sectorMassWeight {GeneratorClass.gauge, GeneratorClass.higgs} 8
      = h.isGaugeSector.derivSubmodule 0 * h.isHiggsSector.derivSubmodule 1
        ⊔ h.isGaugeSector.derivSubmodule 0 * h.isHiggsSector.derivSubmodule 0
          * h.isHiggsSector.derivSubmodule 0
        ⊔ h.isGaugeSector.derivSubmodule 1 * h.isHiggsSector.derivSubmodule 0

modules.title: The gauge-Higgs invariants below mass weight nine
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The mixed `{gauge, higgs}` sector is small, and none of it is invariant. A field-strength
tower weighs at least four and a Higgs tower at least two, and both weights are even, so
the sector vanishes below weight six and at every odd weight, weight seven included. What
is left is weight six, the underived field strength against the underived Higgs, and
weight eight: that same field strength against the weight-four Higgs terms, together with
the once-derived field strength against the underived Higgs.

None of it can carry an invariant, and the reason is an index count. The Higgs is a Lorentz
scalar, so an underived Higgs symbol has no covector index at all and is fixed by the whole
Lorentz group, while a once-derived one carries a single index, its derivative slot. The
covector indices of these products are therefore those of the field strength — two when it
is underived and three when it is once derived — plus at most one from the Higgs.

Two indices admit exactly one invariant contraction, the metric trace, and it vanishes: the
metric is symmetric in the pair of indices in which `IsGaugeSector.F_antisymm` says the
field strength is antisymmetric. Three indices admit no invariant contraction at all, the
metric tying two and the Levi-Civita symbol four. Weight six and the two-Higgs term of
weight eight are of the first kind and the other two terms of weight eight of the second,
so at no weight below nine does the sector add an invariant to what is already there.

Neither count needs the gauge group, and neither needs a basis of the Higgs. The families
being peeled are indexed by a covector of the gauge algebra together with a piece of Higgs
material, and neither index is finite; section B peels a join over an arbitrary index type
by passing to a finite subset of it, which is all an element of a join ever needs.


The bound is `w < 9` rather than the gauge sector's `w < 8`, weight eight being as empty of
invariants as the weights below it. No lower bound on `w` is needed either: the sector is
the two-class sector of the gauge and Higgs generators, so both classes must be present
with a non-zero weight and the scalars, which force `0 < w` in the gauge-sector statement,
never appear.

## ii. Key results

- `IsLorentzCovariant.mul_fixed` : multiplying a Lorentz tensor family by a Lorentz-inert element
  gives a family of the same rank: the element rides through the transformation law untouched
- `ofComponents_mul_right` : the map of a family multiplied on the right by an element is the map of
  the family, multiplied by that element
- `IsLorentzCovariant.mul_vector` : a rank-two family against a Lorentz vector is a rank-three
  family: the two covector indices of the first factor and the single index of the second make three
- `mem_of_lorentz_invariant_iSup_rankTwo_span` : a Lorentz invariant of a join, over an arbitrary
  index type, of the spans of bi-Lorentz families with vanishing metric traces lies in the stable
  submodule it is taken modulo

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Field strengths against Lorentz-inert material
- B. Peeling a join over an arbitrary index
- C. The underived Higgs is Lorentz inert
- D. Field strengths against Higgs material
- E. Mass weights six and eight
- F. The classification below mass weight nine

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Field strengths against Lorentz-inert material

A family transforming as a Lorentz tensor stays one when multiplied by an element the
Lorentz group fixes, and its metric trace is multiplied by that element too. So a field
strength against an underived Higgs is a tensor of the same two or three indices as the
field strength alone. A once-derived Higgs contributes an index of its own, and a
rank-two family against a Lorentz vector is a rank-three family.

## B. Peeling a join over an arbitrary index

The gauge sector combines the reductions of a join of spans indexed by a finite set, which
is what its twelve directions of the gauge algebra need. Here the families are indexed by a
covector of the gauge algebra together with a piece of Higgs material, and neither index is
finite. Nothing is lost: an element of a join lies in the join over finitely many of the
summands, so `ReducesInvariantsTo.iSup` combines the reductions over the whole join, by
way of `ReducesInvariantsTo.iSup_of_biSup`. The rest of the section collects the
stability and the inertness of products and joins that section E consumes.

## C. The underived Higgs is Lorentz inert

The Higgs is a Lorentz scalar, and an underived symbol has no derivative slot for the
Lorentz matrix to act on, so it is fixed outright — and with it every element of the
submodule the underived symbols span.

## D. Field strengths against Higgs material

Three products have to be classified. An underived field strength against inert material is
a bi-Lorentz family whose metric trace vanishes with the antisymmetry of the field strength;
a once-derived one against inert material is a triple Lorentz family; and an underived one
against a once-derived Higgs is a triple Lorentz family as well, the Higgs supplying the
third index. The last is the only one in which a Higgs index moves at all.

## E. Mass weights six and eight

Weight six is a single product and section D settles it outright. Weight eight is a join of
three, and they are peeled one at a time, the two not yet peeled joining the error term —
which asks that they be Lorentz stable. The gauge and Higgs derivative submodules are, and
so are their products and joins.

## F. The classification below mass weight nine

The nine weights below nine are now settled: the sector vanishes below weight six and at
weight seven, and weights six and eight are section E. So below weight nine the gauge-Higgs
sector supplies no invariant beyond what `S` already carries, and the equivalences record it
in the shape the other sectors carry, so that all of them can be combined.

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsLorentzCovariant.mul_fixed
declarations.doc:
Multiplying a Lorentz tensor family by a Lorentz-inert element gives a family of the
same rank: the element rides through the transformation law untouched.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsLorentzCovariant.mul_fixed {n : ℕ}
    (hmul : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x y : B), repLorentz Λ (x * y) = repLorentz Λ x * repLorentz Λ y)
    {T : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B} (hT : IsLorentzCovariant n B repLorentz (ofComponents T))
    {y : B} (hy : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g y = y) :
    IsLorentzCovariant n B repLorentz (ofComponents fun d => T d * y)

declarations.name: Lorentz.ofComponents_mul_right
declarations.doc:
The map of a family multiplied on the right by an element is the map of the family,
multiplied by that element.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofComponents_mul_right {n : ℕ} (T : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) (y : B)
    (t : ℂT(fun _ : Fin n => Color.up)) :
    ofComponents (fun d => T d * y) t = ofComponents T t * y

declarations.name: Lorentz.IsLorentzCovariant.mul_vector
declarations.doc:
A rank-two family against a Lorentz vector is a rank-three family: the two covector
indices of the first factor and the single index of the second make three.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsLorentzCovariant.mul_vector
    (hmul : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x y : B), repLorentz Λ (x * y) = repLorentz Λ x * repLorentz Λ y)
    {T : (Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B} (hT : IsLorentzCovariant 2 B repLorentz (ofComponents T))
    {U : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B}
    (hU : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), repLorentz g (U μ)
      = ∑ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup g).1 ν μ : ℝ) : ℂ) • U ν) :
    IsLorentzCovariant 3 B repLorentz
      (ofComponents fun d : Fin 3 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 => T ![d 0, d 1] * U (d 2))

declarations.name: StandardModel.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_iSup_rankTwo_span
declarations.doc:
A Lorentz invariant of a join, over an arbitrary index type, of the spans of
bi-Lorentz families with vanishing metric traces lies in the stable submodule it is taken
modulo. Each span reduces to the line through its metric contraction, which is zero; the
reductions combine over every finite set of indices, and so over the whole join.

declarations.name: StandardModel.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_iSup_rankThree_span
declarations.doc:
A Lorentz invariant of a join, over an arbitrary index type, of the spans of triple
Lorentz families lies in the stable submodule it is taken modulo: three covector indices
admit no invariant contraction at all, so each span reduces to `⊥`, and the reductions
combine over every finite set of indices, and so over the whole join.

declarations.name: StandardModel.repLorentz_eq_self_of_mem_mul
declarations.doc: A product of two pointwise Lorentz-inert submodules is pointwise Lorentz inert.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_eq_self_of_mem_mul
    (hmul : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x y : B), repLorentz Λ (x * y) = repLorentz Λ x * repLorentz Λ y)
    {V W : Submodule ℂ B} (hV : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)), ∀ y ∈ V, repLorentz g y = y)
    (hW : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)), ∀ y ∈ W, repLorentz g y = y) (g : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    ∀ y ∈ V * W, repLorentz g y = y

declarations.name: StandardModel.repLorentz_mem_mul_of_stable
declarations.doc: A product of two Lorentz-stable submodules is Lorentz stable.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_mem_mul_of_stable
    (hmul : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x y : B), repLorentz Λ (x * y) = repLorentz Λ x * repLorentz Λ y)
    {V W : Submodule ℂ B} (hV : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)), ∀ y ∈ V, repLorentz g y ∈ V)
    (hW : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)), ∀ y ∈ W, repLorentz g y ∈ W) (g : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    ∀ y ∈ V * W, repLorentz g y ∈ V * W

declarations.name: StandardModel.repLorentz_mem_of_fixed
declarations.doc: A pointwise Lorentz-inert submodule is Lorentz stable.

declarations.name: StandardModel.repLorentz_mem_sup_of_stable
declarations.doc: A join of two Lorentz-stable submodules is Lorentz stable.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_mem_sup_of_stable {V W : Submodule ℂ B}
    (hV : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)), ∀ y ∈ V, repLorentz g y ∈ V)
    (hW : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)), ∀ y ∈ W, repLorentz g y ∈ W) (g : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    ∀ y ∈ V ⊔ W, repLorentz g y ∈ V ⊔ W

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.repLorentz_eq_self_of_mem_higgs_derivSubmodule_zero
declarations.doc:
The underived Higgs and conjugate-Higgs symbols are Lorentz scalars with no derivative
slot to rotate, so every element of the weight-two Higgs submodule is fixed by the whole
Lorentz group.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_eq_self_of_mem_higgs_derivSubmodule_zero (g : SL(2,ℂ)) {y : B}
    (hy : y ∈ h.isHiggsSector.derivSubmodule 0) : repLorentz g y = y

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_derivSubmodule_zero_mul_fixed_sup
declarations.doc:
An underived field strength against Lorentz-inert material carries no Lorentz
invariant modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_derivSubmodule_zero_mul_fixed_sup (C : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hC : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)), ∀ y ∈ C, repLorentz g y = y) (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ h.isGaugeSector.derivSubmodule 0 * C ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_derivSubmodule_one_mul_fixed_sup
declarations.doc:
A once-derived field strength against Lorentz-inert material carries no Lorentz
invariant modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_derivSubmodule_one_mul_fixed_sup (C : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hC : ∀ (g : SL(2,ℂ)), ∀ y ∈ C, repLorentz g y = y) (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ h.isGaugeSector.derivSubmodule 1 * C ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_derivSubmodule_zero_mul_higgs_one_sup
declarations.doc:
An underived field strength against a once-derived Higgs carries no Lorentz invariant
modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule: three covector indices admit no contraction.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_derivSubmodule_zero_mul_higgs_one_sup (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ h.isGaugeSector.derivSubmodule 0 * h.isHiggsSector.derivSubmodule 1 ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_six_sup
declarations.doc:
Mass weight six carries no Lorentz invariant modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule: a
Lorentz invariant of `sectorMassWeight {gauge, higgs} 6 ⊔ S` lies in `S`. The weight is
the underived field strength against the underived Higgs, whose two covector indices are
contracted only by the metric, and that trace vanishes.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_six_sup (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ h.sectorMassWeight {GeneratorClass.gauge, GeneratorClass.higgs} 6 ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_eight_sup
declarations.doc:
Mass weight eight carries no Lorentz invariant modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule: a
Lorentz invariant of `sectorMassWeight {gauge, higgs} 8 ⊔ S` lies in `S`. The three
products making up the weight are peeled off one at a time, the two carrying three
covector indices by the absence of any contraction and the one carrying two by the
vanishing of the metric trace.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_eight_sup (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ h.sectorMassWeight {GeneratorClass.gauge, GeneratorClass.higgs} 8 ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mem_of_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_lt_nine_sup
declarations.doc:
Below mass weight nine the gauge-Higgs sector carries no Lorentz invariant: a Lorentz
invariant of `sectorMassWeight {gauge, higgs} w ⊔ S` for `w < 9` lies in `S`. Weights
below six and weight seven are trivial submodules, and weights six and eight are the two
index counts.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_invariant_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_lt_nine_sup (w : ℕ) (hw : w < 9)
    (S : Submodule ℂ B) (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ h.sectorMassWeight {GeneratorClass.gauge, GeneratorClass.higgs} w ⊔ S)
    (hL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mem_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
declarations.doc:
The classification below mass weight nine as an equivalence, in the shape of the gauge-
and Yukawa-sector statements: an element of `sectorMassWeight {gauge, higgs} w ⊔ S` for
`w < 9` is fixed by both groups exactly when it is itself an element of `S` fixed by both
groups. Gauge stability of `S` is not needed, and neither is gauge invariance of `x`: the
forward direction is the index count, which uses the Lorentz group alone.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
    (w : ℕ) (hw : w < 9) (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.sectorMassWeight {GeneratorClass.gauge, GeneratorClass.higgs} w ⊔ S
        ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x) ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g y = y)
          ∧ x = y

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mem_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
declarations.doc:
The same classification without the existential: below mass weight nine an element of
`sectorMassWeight {gauge, higgs} w ⊔ S` fixed by both groups is an element of `S` fixed by
both groups, and conversely.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sectorMassWeight_gauge_higgs_lt_nine_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
    (w : ℕ) (hw : w < 9) (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.sectorMassWeight {GeneratorClass.gauge, GeneratorClass.higgs} w ⊔ S
        ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x) ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)
      ↔ (x ∈ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
          ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)

modules.title: The covariant generators of the field algebra
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The covariant fields, indexed abstractly: `Generators` names one covariant tower
applied to a member of the dual basis of its value space, and `generatorVal` evaluates
it in the algebra. Only basis indices are stored, so the generators of a given mass
weight form a finite type. The field algebra is generated by these values
(`fieldAlgebra_eq_adjoin_range`), and they supercommute — the weight of a generator is
odd exactly when it is fermionic.

The grading of the algebra by mass weight is in `CovAlgebraRealization.MassWeight`.

## ii. Key results

- `Generators` : the abstract index of a single covariant generator of the field algebra: one of the
  covariant-derivative towers of the field strength, of the Higgs and its conjugate, or of the three
  families of each fermion species and their conjugates, applied to a member of the dual basis of
  its value space
- `generatorVal` : the value in `B` of a covariant generator: the corresponding covariant tower
  applied to the indicated dual basis vector of its value space
- `fieldAlgebra_eq_adjoin_range` : the field algebra is generated by the covariant basis generators

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Derivative collections
- B. Covariant generators
- C. Per-kind minimum weights
- D. The classes realised by a word
- E. Supercommutativity of the generators

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Derivative collections
## B. Covariant generators

## C. Per-kind minimum weights

Each of the three classes of covariant generator carries a minimum mass weight: the
field-strength towers `F` are the heaviest, at weight `2 * (2 + n) ≥ 4`; the Higgs and
conjugate-Higgs towers `H`, `barH` are the lightest, at weight `2 * (1 + n) ≥ 2`; and
the ten families of fermion towers sit in between, at weight `3 + 2 * n ≥ 3`.
## D. The classes realised by a word

## E. Supercommutativity of the generators

The mass weight doubles as the super-grading: the weight of a covariant generator
is odd exactly when the generator is fermionic. Two generators therefore exchange
up to the sign `(-1) ^ (weight * weight)`, and words of generators up to the sign
of the product of their total weights.

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.Generators
declarations.doc:
The abstract index of a single covariant generator of the field algebra: one of
the covariant-derivative towers of the field strength, of the Higgs and its
conjugate, or of the three families of each fermion species and their conjugates,
applied to a member of the dual basis of its value space. Only basis indices are
stored, so for a fixed tower length the generators of a given mass weight form a
finite type. The evaluation in `B` is `generatorVal`.
declarations.statement:
inductive Generators where
  /-- The Higgs tower `∇_l H` applied to a dual basis vector. -/
  | H : (n : ℕ) → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Fin 2 → Generators
  /-- The conjugate-Higgs tower `∇_l H̄` applied to a dual basis vector. -/
  | barH : (n : ℕ) → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Fin 2 → Generators
  /-- The field-strength tower `∇_l F_μν` applied to a dual basis vector. -/
  | F : (n : ℕ) → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) →
      (Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) → Generators
  /-- The fermion tower `∇_l d` of the `i`-th family applied to a dual basis vector. -/
  | d : Fin 3 → (n : ℕ) → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Fin 2 × Fin 3 → Generators
  /-- The fermion tower `∇_l bard` of the `i`-th family applied to a dual basis vector. -/
  | bard : Fin 3 → (n : ℕ) → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Fin 2 × Fin 3 → Generators
  /-- The fermion tower `∇_l u` of the `i`-th family applied to a dual basis vector. -/
  | u : Fin 3 → (n : ℕ) → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Fin 2 × Fin 3 → Generators
  /-- The fermion tower `∇_l baru` of the `i`-th family applied to a dual basis vector. -/
  | baru : Fin 3 → (n : ℕ) → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Fin 2 × Fin 3 → Generators
  /-- The fermion tower `∇_l Q` of the `i`-th family applied to a dual basis vector. -/
  | Q : Fin 3 → (n : ℕ) → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Fin 2 × Fin 3 × Fin 2 → Generators
  /-- The fermion tower `∇_l barQ` of the `i`-th family applied to a dual basis vector. -/
  | barQ : Fin 3 → (n : ℕ) → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Fin 2 × Fin 3 × Fin 2 → Generators
  /-- The fermion tower `∇_l L` of the `i`-th family applied to a dual basis vector. -/
  | L : Fin 3 → (n : ℕ) → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Fin 2 × Fin 2 → Generators
  /-- The fermion tower `∇_l barL` of the `i`-th family applied to a dual basis vector. -/
  | barL : Fin 3 → (n : ℕ) → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Fin 2 × Fin 2 → Generators
  /-- The fermion tower `∇_l e` of the `i`-th family applied to a dual basis vector. -/
  | e : Fin 3 → (n : ℕ) → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Fin 2 → Generators
  /-- The fermion tower `∇_l bare` of the `i`-th family applied to a dual basis vector. -/
  | bare : Fin 3 → (n : ℕ) → (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Fin 2 → Generators

declarations.statement: lemma wordClasses_nil : wordClasses [] = ∅

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.wordClasses_append
declarations.doc: Concatenating words unions the classes they realise.
declarations.statement:
lemma wordClasses_append (gl gl' : List Generators) :
    wordClasses (gl ++ gl') = wordClasses gl ∪ wordClasses gl'

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.wordClasses_cons
declarations.doc: Prepending a generator inserts its class.
declarations.statement:
lemma wordClasses_cons (a : Generators) (gl : List Generators) :
    wordClasses (a :: gl) = insert a.kind (wordClasses gl)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.classWeight
declarations.doc: The total mass weight carried by the generators of a given class in a word.
declarations.statement: def classWeight (c : GeneratorClass) (gl : List Generators) : ℕ

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.classWeight_nil
declarations.statement: lemma classWeight_nil (c : GeneratorClass) : classWeight c [] = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.classWeight_cons_of_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma classWeight_cons_of_eq {c : GeneratorClass} {g : Generators} (hg : g.kind = c)
    (t : List Generators) :
    classWeight c (g :: t) = g.weight + classWeight c t

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.classWeight_cons_of_ne
declarations.statement:
lemma classWeight_cons_of_ne {c : GeneratorClass} {g : Generators} (hg : g.kind ≠ c)
    (t : List Generators) : classWeight c (g :: t) = classWeight c t

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.Generators.weight_pos
declarations.doc: Every generator carries a non-zero mass weight.
declarations.statement: lemma Generators.weight_pos (g : Generators) : 0 < g.weight

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.classWeight_ne_zero
declarations.doc: A class realised by a word carries a non-zero part of its weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma classWeight_ne_zero {c : GeneratorClass} {gl : List Generators}
    (hc : c ∈ wordClasses gl) : classWeight c gl ≠ 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.classWeight_add
declarations.doc:
Over a word realising only two classes, the two class weights add up to the total
weight.

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.le_classWeight_of_mem
declarations.doc:
A class realised by a word carries at least the minimum weight of that class: the
generator witnessing the realisation already contributes that much, and the
remaining generators of the class only add more.

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.classWeight_add_three
declarations.doc:
The three class weights exhaust the total weight of a word: every generator has
exactly one of the three kinds.
declarations.statement:
lemma classWeight_add_three (gl : List Generators) :
    classWeight GeneratorClass.gauge gl + classWeight GeneratorClass.higgs gl
      + classWeight GeneratorClass.fermion gl = (gl.map Generators.weight).sum

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.generatorVal
declarations.doc:
The value in `B` of a covariant generator: the corresponding covariant tower
applied to the indicated dual basis vector of its value space.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def generatorVal
    (h : CovAlgebraRealization B repGauge repLorentz massWeightPoly) : Generators → B

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.massWeightPoly_generatorVal
declarations.doc: Every covariant generator is a `massWeightPoly`-eigenvector of its weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightPoly_generatorVal (g : Generators) :
    massWeightPoly (h.generatorVal g) = Polynomial.monomial g.weight (h.generatorVal g)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.generatorVal_mem_fieldAlgebra
declarations.statement:
lemma generatorVal_mem_fieldAlgebra (g : Generators) :
    h.generatorVal g ∈ h.fieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.fieldAlgebra_le_adjoin_range
declarations.doc:
Expanding every dual vector in the dual basis of its value space: the field
algebra is already generated by the countable family of basis generators.
declarations.statement:
lemma fieldAlgebra_le_adjoin_range :
    h.fieldAlgebra ≤ Algebra.adjoin ℂ (Set.range h.generatorVal)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.fieldAlgebra_eq_adjoin_range
declarations.doc: The field algebra is generated by the covariant basis generators.
declarations.statement:
lemma fieldAlgebra_eq_adjoin_range :
    h.fieldAlgebra = Algebra.adjoin ℂ (Set.range h.generatorVal)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.exists_list_map_eq
declarations.doc: A list of generator values is the list of values of a list of generators.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_list_map_eq (l₀ : List B) :
    (∀ y ∈ l₀, y ∈ Set.range h.generatorVal) →
    ∃ gl : List Generators, gl.map h.generatorVal = l₀

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.massWeightPoly_generatorVal_list_prod
declarations.doc:
A word in the covariant generators is a `massWeightPoly`-eigenvector whose
weight is the sum of the weights of its factors.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightPoly_generatorVal_list_prod (gl : List Generators) :
    massWeightPoly ((gl.map h.generatorVal).prod) =
      Polynomial.monomial ((gl.map Generators.weight).sum) ((gl.map h.generatorVal).prod)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.commute_F_generatorVal
declarations.doc:
The field-strength symbols commute with the value of every covariant
generator.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_F_generatorVal {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (ψ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) (g : Generators) :
    Commute (h.covF l μ ν ψ) (h.generatorVal g)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.commute_H_generatorVal
declarations.doc: The Higgs symbols commute with the value of every covariant generator.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_H_generatorVal {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ HiggsVec) (g : Generators) :
    Commute (h.covH l φ) (h.generatorVal g)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.commute_barH_generatorVal
declarations.doc:
The conjugate-Higgs symbols commute with the value of every covariant
generator.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_barH_generatorVal {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule HiggsVec)) (g : Generators) :
    Commute (h.covBarH l φ) (h.generatorVal g)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.commute_generatorVal_of_even
declarations.doc:
A covariant generator of even mass weight is bosonic: its value commutes with
the value of every covariant generator.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_generatorVal_of_even {g : Generators} (hg : g.weight % 2 = 0)
    (g' : Generators) : Commute (h.generatorVal g) (h.generatorVal g')

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.generatorVal_anticomm_of_odd_of_odd
declarations.doc:
Fermionic generator values anticommute: the values of two covariant generators
of odd mass weight exchange with a sign.
declarations.statement:
lemma generatorVal_anticomm_of_odd_of_odd {g g' : Generators}
    (hg : g.weight % 2 = 1) (hg' : g'.weight % 2 = 1) :
    h.generatorVal g * h.generatorVal g'
      = -(h.generatorVal g' * h.generatorVal g)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.generatorVal_mul_generatorVal
declarations.doc:
Two covariant generators exchange up to the sign determined by their mass
weights: the weight is odd exactly on the fermionic generators, so the sign is
`-1` precisely when both generators are fermionic.
declarations.statement:
lemma generatorVal_mul_generatorVal (g g' : Generators) :
    h.generatorVal g * h.generatorVal g' =
      ((-1 : ℂ) ^ (g.weight * g'.weight)) • (h.generatorVal g' * h.generatorVal g)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.generatorVal_mul_list_prod
declarations.doc:
A generator value moves past a word of generators up to the sign of the
product of the weights.
declarations.statement:
lemma generatorVal_mul_list_prod (g : Generators) (gl : List Generators) :
    h.generatorVal g * (gl.map h.generatorVal).prod =
      ((-1 : ℂ) ^ (g.weight * (gl.map Generators.weight).sum)) •
        ((gl.map h.generatorVal).prod * h.generatorVal g)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.list_prod_mul_list_prod
declarations.doc:
Two words of covariant generators exchange up to the sign of the product of
their total weights.
declarations.statement:
lemma list_prod_mul_list_prod (gl gl' : List Generators) :
    (gl.map h.generatorVal).prod * (gl'.map h.generatorVal).prod =
      ((-1 : ℂ) ^ ((gl.map Generators.weight).sum * (gl'.map Generators.weight).sum)) •
        ((gl'.map h.generatorVal).prod * (gl.map h.generatorVal).prod)

modules.title: The mass-weight grading of the field algebra
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The elements of the field algebra of a given mass weight form a submodule, which is
exactly the span of the words in the covariant generators of that total weight
(`massWeightSubmodule_eq_span`). Weight-homogeneous elements supercommute,
the gauge and Lorentz actions preserve the weight, and consequently an invariant
element decomposing into components of pairwise distinct weights has invariant
components.

## ii. Key results

- `massWeightSubmodule_eq_span` : the weight grading of the field algebra

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The mass-weight submodules
- B. The weight grading of the field algebra
- C. Supercommutativity of weight-homogeneous elements
- D. Invariance of the weight components

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The mass-weight submodules
## B. The weight grading of the field algebra
## C. Supercommutativity of weight-homogeneous elements

## D. Invariance of the weight components

The gauge and Lorentz actions preserve the mass weight: they carry each covariant
tower into combinations of towers of the same derivative order. The weight
components of the field algebra are independent, so an invariant element that is
a sum of components of pairwise distinct weights has invariant components.

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
All elements of the field algebra of mass weight exactly `n`: the intersection of
the algebra generated by the covariant fields with the part on which
`massWeightPoly` is the monomial `X ^ n`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def massWeightSubmodule
    (h : CovAlgebraRealization B repGauge repLorentz massWeightPoly) (n : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ B

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.massWeightPoly_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule
StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mem_fieldAlgebra_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_fieldAlgebra_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule {n : ℕ} {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule n) : x ∈ h.fieldAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mem_massWeightSubmodule_of
declarations.doc:
Membership in a mass-weight submodule: an element of the field algebra which
`massWeightPoly` sends to the monomial of that weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_of {n : ℕ} {x : B} (hmem : x ∈ h.fieldAlgebra)
    (hpoly : massWeightPoly x = Polynomial.monomial n x) :
    x ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule n

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.list_prod_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
A word in the covariant generators lies in the mass-weight submodule of its total
weight.

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.coeff_massWeightPoly_mem_span
declarations.doc:
Reading off the `X ^ w` coefficient of `massWeightPoly` sends the field algebra
into the span of the words of total weight `w` — the projection onto the weight-`w`
component, with no independence argument needed.

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmodule_eq_span
declarations.doc:
**The weight grading of the field algebra.** The submodule of elements of the
field algebra of mass weight `w` is exactly the span of the words in the covariant
basis generators of total weight `w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eq_span (w : ℕ) :
    h.massWeightSubmodule w = Submodule.span ℂ
      {x | ∃ gl : List Generators,
        (gl.map Generators.weight).sum = w ∧ (gl.map h.generatorVal).prod = x}

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mul_eq_smul_mul_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
Weight-homogeneous elements of the field algebra supercommute: elements of the
mass-weight submodules of weights `w` and `w'` exchange up to the sign
`(-1) ^ (w * w')` — fermion parity is the parity of the mass weight.

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.exists_smul_mul_comm_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: Weight-homogeneous elements of the field algebra commute up to a scalar.

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.span_mul_comm_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
Reordering a product of two weight-homogeneous elements does not change its
span.

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mul_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The mass-weight submodules are multiplicative: weights add under multiplication.

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.H_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: Any Higgs tower symbol lies in the mass-weight submodule of its weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma H_mem_massWeightSubmodule {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ HiggsVec) : h.covH l φ ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule (2 * (1 + n))

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.barH_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: Any conjugate-Higgs tower symbol lies in the mass-weight submodule of its weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma barH_mem_massWeightSubmodule {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule HiggsVec)) :
    h.covBarH l φ ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule (2 * (1 + n))

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.F_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: Any field-strength tower symbol lies in the mass-weight submodule of its weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma F_mem_massWeightSubmodule {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) :
    h.covF l μ ν φ ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule (2 * (2 + n))

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.d_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: Any `d` tower symbol lies in the mass-weight submodule of its weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma d_mem_massWeightSubmodule (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ DownSinglet) : h.covD i l φ ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule (3 + 2 * n)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.d_supercommute_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
A `d` tower symbol supercommutes with any weight-homogeneous element: its own
weight `3 + 2 * n` is odd, so moving it past an element of weight `w` costs
`(-1) ^ w`.

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.bard_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: Any `bard` tower symbol lies in the mass-weight submodule of its weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma bard_mem_massWeightSubmodule (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule DownSinglet)) : h.covBarD i l φ ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule (3 + 2 *
      n)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.u_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: Any `u` tower symbol lies in the mass-weight submodule of its weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma u_mem_massWeightSubmodule (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ UpSinglet) : h.covU i l φ ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule (3 + 2 * n)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.baru_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: Any `baru` tower symbol lies in the mass-weight submodule of its weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma baru_mem_massWeightSubmodule (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule UpSinglet)) :
    h.covBarU i l φ ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule (3 + 2 * n)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.Q_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: Any `Q` tower symbol lies in the mass-weight submodule of its weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma Q_mem_massWeightSubmodule (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ QuarkDoublet) : h.covQ i l φ ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule (3 + 2 * n)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.barQ_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: Any `barQ` tower symbol lies in the mass-weight submodule of its weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma barQ_mem_massWeightSubmodule (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)

      n)

declarations.doc: Any `L` tower symbol lies in the mass-weight submodule of its weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma L_mem_massWeightSubmodule (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ LeptonDoubletV) : h.covL i l φ ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule (3 + 2 * n)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.barL_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: Any `barL` tower symbol lies in the mass-weight submodule of its weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma barL_mem_massWeightSubmodule (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule LeptonDoubletV)) : h.covBarL i l φ ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule (3 +

declarations.doc: Any `e` tower symbol lies in the mass-weight submodule of its weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma e_mem_massWeightSubmodule (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)

declarations.doc: Any `bare` tower symbol lies in the mass-weight submodule of its weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma bare_mem_massWeightSubmodule (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)

      2 * n)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.repGauge_generatorVal_mem
declarations.doc:
The gauge action carries a covariant generator into the mass-weight submodule
of its weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_generatorVal_mem (g : GaugeGroupI) (a : Generators) :
    repGauge g (h.generatorVal a) ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule a.weight

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.repLorentz_generatorVal_mem
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action carries a covariant generator into the mass-weight submodule
of its weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_generatorVal_mem (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (a : Generators) :
    repLorentz Λ (h.generatorVal a) ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule a.weight

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.repGauge_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The action `repGauge` preserves the mass-weight submodules.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_mem_massWeightSubmodule {w : ℕ} {x : B} (g : GaugeGroupI)
    (hx : x ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule w) : repGauge g x ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule w

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.repLorentz_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The action `repLorentz` preserves the mass-weight submodules.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_mem_massWeightSubmodule {w : ℕ} {x : B} (Λ : SL(2,ℂ))
    (hx : x ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule w) : repLorentz Λ x ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule w

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.eq_zero_of_sum_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
Components of pairwise distinct mass weights are independent: a vanishing sum
of weight-homogeneous elements has vanishing terms.

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.invariant_of_eq_sum_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
An invariant element decomposes into invariant weight components: if a gauge-
and Lorentz-invariant `x` is the sum of components of pairwise distinct mass
weights, every component is itself gauge and Lorentz invariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariant_of_eq_sum_massWeightSubmodule {n : ℕ} {x : B} {w : Fin n → ℕ}
    (hw : Function.Injective w) (f : Fin n → B) (hf : x = ∑ i, f i)
    (hx : ∀ i, f i ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule (w i))
    (hgauge : ∀ g, repGauge g x = x) (hlorentz : ∀ Λ, repLorentz Λ x = x) :
    ∀ i, (∀ g, repGauge g (f i) = f i) ∧ ∀ Λ, repLorentz Λ (f i) = f i

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.invaraint_of_eq_sum_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
The reduction of questions on invariants to invariants within
mass weight submodules.
declarations.statement:
lemma invaraint_of_eq_sum_massWeightSubmodule {n : ℕ} {x : B}
    (f : Fin n → B) (hf : x = ∑ i, f i) (hx : ∀ i, f i ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule i.val)
    (hgauge : ∀ g, repGauge g x = x) (hlorentz : ∀ Λ, repLorentz Λ x = x) :
    ∀ i, (∀ g, repGauge g (f i) = f i) ∧ ∀ Λ, repLorentz Λ (f i) = f i

modules.title: The mass-weight filtration and the constant term
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The grading of the field algebra by mass weight answers one weight at a time. A
Lagrangian is not graded: it is a sum of terms of every weight up to a cut-off, and the
object that holds such a sum is the filtration `massWeightSubmoduleLE w`, the join of the
weight pieces of weight at most `w`.

Passing from the grading to the filtration adds exactly one thing, and it is the thing the
graded statement had to exclude. `Invariants.lean` classifies the invariants of
`massWeightSubmodule w` for `0 < w ≤ 8`, and the lower bound is not an artefact: at weight
zero the field algebra contains the scalars, which are fixed by both groups and lie in no
given `S`, so no classification into a span plus a remainder in `S` can hold there. The
filtration contains weight zero, so the scalars have to be met rather than avoided — and
they are a genuine invariant, the constant term of mass dimension zero, the cosmological
term.

Section B settles what the weight-zero piece is: the only word of total weight zero is the
empty word, every generator carrying positive weight, so `massWeightSubmodule 0` is exactly
the scalars, and the unit is fixed by both groups because both act by algebra maps.

The classification then runs as it does for the grading. `ReducesInvariantsTo` is closed under
joins in its source, and the filtration is a join: each weight from one to eight reduces to
the Standard-Model span of that weight by `reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmodule`, weight
zero reduces to itself, and the join of the nine is a reduction of the filtration. No independence
of the sectors, and none of the weights, is used anywhere.

The answer at bound eight is spanned by the constant term, the Higgs mass term `H† H`, and
the dimension-four span of `Invariants.lean`, with the same scope: formal expressions,
spanning generators, and no quotient by total derivatives or the equations of motion.

## ii. Key results

- `massWeightSubmoduleLE` : the elements of the field algebra of mass weight at most `w`: the join
  of the mass-weight submodules of weight `0` through `w`
- `massWeightSubmodule_le_massWeightSubmoduleLE` : each graded piece of weight at most `w` sits
  inside the filtration at `w`
- `mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE` : an element of a graded piece of weight at most `w` lies in the
  filtration at `w`
- `massWeightSubmoduleLE_le` : a submodule containing every graded piece of weight at most `w`
  contains the filtration at `w`: the join is taken over exactly those pieces

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The mass-weight filtration
- B. The constant term at weight zero
- C. The span of the filtration
- D. Reducing the filtration
- E. The classification up to mass dimension four
- F. The Standard Model Lagrangian with its constant and mass terms

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.doc:
The elements of the field algebra of mass weight at most `w`: the join of the
mass-weight submodules of weight `0` through `w`. This is where a Lagrangian lives, a
sum of terms of every mass dimension up to a cut-off rather than of a single one.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def massWeightSubmoduleLE (w : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ B

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmodule_le_massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.doc: Each graded piece of weight at most `w` sits inside the filtration at `w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_le_massWeightSubmoduleLE {k w : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ w) :
    h.massWeightSubmodule k ≤ h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.doc: An element of a graded piece of weight at most `w` lies in the filtration at `w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE {k w : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ w) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule k) : x ∈ h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmoduleLE_le
declarations.doc:
A submodule containing every graded piece of weight at most `w` contains the
filtration at `w`: the join is taken over exactly those pieces.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmoduleLE_le {w : ℕ} {V : Submodule ℂ B}
    (hV : ∀ k ≤ w, h.massWeightSubmodule k ≤ V) : h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w ≤ V

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmoduleLE_mono
declarations.doc: The filtration grows with the bound.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmoduleLE_mono {w w' : ℕ} (hw : w ≤ w') :
    h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w ≤ h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w'

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmoduleLE_eq_iSup
declarations.doc:
The filtration as a join over a finite index type, which is the form in which the
reduction of a join consumes it.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmoduleLE_eq_iSup (w : ℕ) :
    h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w = ⨆ k : Fin (w + 1), h.massWeightSubmodule (k : ℕ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.isStableUnder_massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.doc:
The filtration is carried into itself by both groups: each graded piece is, and a
join of stable submodules is stable.
declarations.statement:
lemma isStableUnder_massWeightSubmoduleLE (w : ℕ) :
    IsStableUnder (gaugeLorentzMaps repGauge repLorentz) (h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmodule_zero
declarations.doc:
The weight-zero part of the field algebra is the scalars. Every covariant generator
carries positive mass weight, so the only word of total weight zero is the empty one,
whose value is the unit. This is the constant term of the Lagrangian, of mass dimension
zero — the cosmological term.
declarations.statement: lemma massWeightSubmodule_zero : h.massWeightSubmodule 0 = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.isFixedBy_massWeightSubmodule_zero
declarations.doc:
The scalars are fixed by both groups: each acts by an algebra map, so each fixes the
unit. This is what makes the constant term an invariant, and it is what the backward
direction of the classification needs of the weight-zero part of the span.
declarations.statement:
lemma isFixedBy_massWeightSubmodule_zero :
    IsFixedBy (gaugeLorentzMaps repGauge repLorentz) (h.massWeightSubmodule 0)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.standardModelSpanLE
declarations.doc:
The gauge- and Lorentz-invariant content of the Standard Model up to mass weight `w`:
the weight-zero part of the field algebra, which is the constant term, joined with the
Standard-Model span of every weight up to `w`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def standardModelSpanLE (w : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ B

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmodule_zero_le_standardModelSpanLE
declarations.doc: The constant term lies in the span of the filtration, at every bound.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_zero_le_standardModelSpanLE (w : ℕ) :
    h.massWeightSubmodule 0 ≤ h.standardModelSpanLE w

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.standardModelSpan_le_standardModelSpanLE
declarations.doc: The graded span of a weight at most `w` lies in the span of the filtration at `w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma standardModelSpan_le_standardModelSpanLE {k w : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ w) :
    h.standardModelSpan k ≤ h.standardModelSpanLE w

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.standardModelSpanLE_le_massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.doc:
The span of the filtration at `w` has mass weight at most `w`: the constant term has
weight zero and each graded span has its own weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma standardModelSpanLE_le_massWeightSubmoduleLE (w : ℕ) :
    h.standardModelSpanLE w ≤ h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.isFixedBy_standardModelSpanLE
declarations.doc:
The span of the filtration is fixed pointwise by the gauge and Lorentz groups
together. At positive weight this is the fixedness of the graded spans; at weight zero
it is the fixedness of the unit, and that is the only new content of the filtration.
declarations.statement:
lemma isFixedBy_standardModelSpanLE (w : ℕ) :
    IsFixedBy (gaugeLorentzMaps repGauge repLorentz) (h.standardModelSpanLE w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.repGauge_of_mem_standardModelSpanLE
declarations.doc: Every element of the span of the filtration is a gauge invariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_of_mem_standardModelSpanLE (w : ℕ) (g : GaugeGroupI) {y : B}
    (hy : y ∈ h.standardModelSpanLE w) : repGauge g y = y

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.repLorentz_of_mem_standardModelSpanLE
declarations.doc: Every element of the span of the filtration is a Lorentz invariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_of_mem_standardModelSpanLE (w : ℕ) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) {y : B}
    (hy : y ∈ h.standardModelSpanLE w) : repLorentz Λ y = y

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.standardModelSpanLE_eight
declarations.doc:
The span of the filtration at bound eight in reduced form. Of the nine graded spans
only two are non-trivial, the Higgs mass term at weight four and the dimension-four
Lagrangian at weight eight, so what survives up to mass dimension four is the constant
term, the Higgs mass term, and the Lagrangian.
declarations.statement:
lemma standardModelSpanLE_eight :
    h.standardModelSpanLE 8 = (1 : Submodule ℂ B) ⊔ (h.isHiggsSector.dotSpan 0 0
      ⊔ (h.isGaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
            ⊔ h.isHiggsSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
          ⊔ (h.isFermionSector.kineticSpan ⊔ h.yukawaSpan)))

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.doc:
The filtration reduces to its span, at every bound up to eight. The filtration is a
join of the graded pieces, each of them stable under both groups, and `ReducesInvariantsTo` is
closed under joins in its source: the weights are taken one at a time, each in turn joining the
error term of the others. At positive weight the graded reduction of `Invariants.lean` is
used; at weight zero a submodule reduces to itself, the constant term being carried in the
span.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_massWeightSubmoduleLE {w : ℕ} (hw : w ≤ 8) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (gaugeLorentzMaps repGauge repLorentz) (h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w)
      (h.standardModelSpanLE w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
declarations.doc:
The classification of the Standard Model up to mass weight `w ≤ 8` as an equivalence,
in the shape every sector uses: an element of `massWeightSubmoduleLE w ⊔ S`, with `S`
stable under both groups, is fixed by both groups exactly when it is a combination of
the constant term and the Standard-Model terms of weight at most `w`, up to a remainder
in `S` fixed by both groups.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff (w : ℕ) (hw : w ≤ 8)
    (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGauge g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ h.standardModelSpanLE w

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.exists_mem_standardModelSpanLE_of_gauge_and_lorentz_invariant
declarations.doc:
The gauge and Lorentz invariants of mass weight at most `w`, for `w ≤ 8`, modulo a
submodule `S` stable under both groups: such an invariant is a combination of the
constant term and the Standard-Model terms of weight at most `w`, plus a remainder in
`S`, and the remainder is fixed by both groups as well, being the difference of two
invariants.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_mem_standardModelSpanLE_of_gauge_and_lorentz_invariant (w : ℕ) (hw : w ≤ 8)
    (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGauge g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w ⊔ S)
    (hG : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
    (hL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) :
    ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g y = y)
      ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g y = y)
      ∧ x - y ∈ h.standardModelSpanLE w

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
declarations.doc:
The same classification without the existential: at every bound up to eight an element
of `massWeightSubmoduleLE w ⊔ S` fixed by both groups is an element of the span of the
filtration joined with `S` fixed by both groups, and conversely.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem (w : ℕ)
    (hw : w ≤ 8) (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGauge g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)
      ↔ (x ∈ h.standardModelSpanLE w ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
          ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
declarations.doc:
The classification at bound eight, that is at mass dimension at most four, as an
equivalence: an element of `massWeightSubmoduleLE 8 ⊔ S`, with `S` stable under both
groups, is fixed by both groups exactly when it lies in the span of the filtration up to
a remainder in `S` fixed by both groups.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
    (S : Submodule ℂ B) (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGauge g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.massWeightSubmoduleLE 8 ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ h.standardModelSpanLE 8

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
declarations.doc: The same at bound eight without the existential.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
    (S : Submodule ℂ B) (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGauge g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.massWeightSubmoduleLE 8 ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)
      ↔ (x ∈ h.standardModelSpanLE 8 ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
          ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovAlgebraRealization.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_lagrangian
declarations.doc:
The invariant content of the Standard Model up to mass dimension four. An element of
`massWeightSubmoduleLE 8 ⊔ S`, for `S` a submodule stable under both groups, is fixed by
the gauge group and the Lorentz group exactly when it is a combination of
the constant term, of mass dimension zero,
the Higgs mass term `H† H`, of mass dimension two (`HiggsAlgebraCovRealization.dotSpan`),
and the dimension-four span — the four Lorentz contractions of the three `F·F` trace
families and of the twice-derived hypercharge field strength, among them the gauge
kinetic and theta terms (`IsGaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan`), the Higgs
kinetic term, its quartic potential and its two box terms
(`HiggsAlgebraCovRealization.lorentzContractionEightSpan`), the kinetic terms of the ten fermion
species over the nine family pairs (`IsFermionSector.kineticSpan`), and the six Yukawa
couplings over the nine family pairs (`yukawaSpan`) —
up to a remainder in `S` fixed by both groups, and nothing else. The generators span;
they are not shown to be independent, and no quotient by total derivatives is taken.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_lagrangian
    (S : Submodule ℂ B) (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGauge g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.massWeightSubmoduleLE 8 ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ (1 : Submodule ℂ B) ⊔ (h.isHiggsSector.dotSpan 0 0
              ⊔ (h.isGaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
                    ⊔ h.isHiggsSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
                  ⊔ (h.isFermionSector.kineticSpan ⊔ h.yukawaSpan)))

modules.title: The invariant content of the Standard Model
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

This is where the classification of the Standard Model closes. A word in the covariant
generators realises a set of generator classes — gauge, Higgs, fermion — and the eight
class sets cut the field algebra into eight sectors, each of which has been classified
separately at every mass weight up to eight, that is at every mass dimension up to four.
This file joins the eight.

At mass dimension four the gauge- and Lorentz-invariant content is spanned by the four
Lorentz contractions of each of the three `F·F` trace families and of the twice-derived
hypercharge field strength. The antisymmetry of the field strength cuts these to two of each
(`IsGaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan_eq`), and the two of the twice-derived hypercharge
field strength vanish, its covariant derivatives being ordinary ones (A.1). What is left is the
kinetic-shape and theta-shape contractions of the three gauge groups. Beside them stand the
Higgs kinetic term with its quartic potential and its two box terms; the kinetic terms of the
ten fermion species over the nine family pairs; and the six Yukawa couplings over the nine
family pairs. Below mass dimension four there is a single term, the Higgs mass term `H† H` at
mass weight four; below that, nothing.

The statement is about formal expressions, the elements of the field algebra with complex
coefficients. It is a spanning statement: the listed generators are not shown to be
independent or nonzero. No reality condition is imposed, and nothing is identified modulo
total derivatives or the equations of motion, so both box terms, both placements of each
fermion derivative and the theta terms all appear.

The join is the delicate step. `massWeightSubmodule_eq_iSup_sectorMassWeight` writes the
weight-`w` submodule as the join of the eight sectors' weight-`w` parts, but reading off
from an invariant of the whole that its eight pieces are separately invariant would need
the pieces to be determined by their sum — the independence of the sectors, which does
not follow from `CovAlgebraRealization` (compare `sector_invariant_of_iSupIndep`).

Nothing here uses it. Each sector's classification is a reduction `ReducesInvariantsTo σ V W`
of `PhyslibAlpha.Mathematics.InvariantReduction` — every `σ`-invariant of `V ⊔ S` lies in
`W ⊔ S`, for every `σ`-stable `S` — and that relation is closed under joins in its source.
Joining the sectors therefore asks only that each of them be carried into itself by the two
groups, which they are (`repGauge_mem_sectorMassWeight`, `repLorentz_mem_sectorMassWeight`).
The eight are taken one at a time, each in turn joining the error term of the others, and
independence never enters.

Section A collects the surviving spans of the eight sectors into `standardModelSpan`, and
section B checks that it is made of invariants of the right mass weight, which is both the
easy direction of the classification and the stability the reduction asks of its target.
Section C restricts each sector's reduction to its weight part, section D joins them, and
sections E and F read off the equivalence, through
`ReducesInvariantsTo.mem_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff`, and its consequence at mass
dimension four.


The weight is bounded below as well as above. At weight zero the field algebra contains
the scalars, which are fixed by both groups and lie in no given `S`; every one of the
sector classifications combined here excludes that weight for the same reason.

## ii. Key results

- `standardModelSpan` : the gauge- and Lorentz-invariant content of the Standard Model at mass
  weight `w`: the join of the surviving spans of the eight sectors

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The span of the Standard Model Lagrangian
  - A.1. The twice-derived hypercharge contractions vanish
- B. The span is made of invariants of the right weight
- C. Each sector reduces to the span
- D. Joining the eight sectors
- E. The classification at mass dimension at most four
- F. The Standard Model Lagrangian

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The span of the Standard Model Lagrangian

### A.1. The twice-derived hypercharge contractions vanish

The hypercharge coordinate kills brackets, so the covariant derivatives of the hypercharge
field strength are ordinary derivatives, which commute (`covF_comp_perm_of_map_lie` with
`GaugeAlgebra.stdBasis_coord_inr_inr_lie`). The twice-derived hypercharge family is therefore
symmetric in its two derivative slots as well as antisymmetric in its two field-strength slots,
and `RankFour` sends both of its remaining contractions to zero. So six generators span the
gauge contribution: for each of the gluon, `W` and hypercharge trace families, the `(0,2)(1,3)`
metric contraction `η^{μρ} η^{νσ} F_{μν} F_{ρσ}` and the Levi-Civita contraction
`ε^{μνρσ} F_{μν} F_{ρσ}`, gauge index summed, as the plain component sums of `RankFour` with no
further normalisation. These are identities of local expressions; no integration by parts,
total-derivative quotient or equation of motion is involved.

The derivative symmetry is not a law of `IsGaugeSector`, which relates no derivative slots. It
holds here because `B` receives the covariant jet algebra, and it covers every ordinary
realization through `AlgebraRealization.toCovAlgebraRealization`. Nothing is said about the
gluon and `W` components, whose covariant derivatives do not commute.
