modules.title: The type corresponding to quark doublets
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define the type corresponding to
the target vector space of a quark field in the Standard Model.

On this type we define a representation of the Lorentz group, and a
representation of the Standard Model gauge group.

## ii. Key results

- `basis` : a basis on the quark doublets
- `colourWeakEquiv` : the colour and weak factors of the quark doublet combined into a single
  Euclidean factor over `Fin 3 × Fin 2`
- `colourWeakEquiv_tmul`
- `jetValLinEquiv`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Equivalence with the underlying tensor product space
- B. The structure of a module
- C. The basis of the quark doublet space
- D. Lorentz group representation
- E. The representation of the Standard Model gauge group
- F. The representation of the jet gauge group
- G. Component transformation laws
- H. The gauge weight of the QuarkDoublet components
- I. The boost weight of the QuarkDoublet components

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Equivalence with the underlying tensor product space

## B. The structure of a module

The AddCommGroup and module instances are inherited from the underlying tensor product space.
## C. The basis of the quark doublet space
## D. Lorentz group representation
## E. The representation of the Standard Model gauge group

## F. The representation of the jet gauge group

The colour and weak indices are combined into the single index `Fin 3 × Fin 2`, on which
the `SU(3)` and `SU(2)` power-series matrices of a jet of gauge transformations act
together through their Kronecker product, scaled by the hypercharge power series `u`.

## G. Component transformation laws

The basis of `QuarkDoublet` splits as a left-handed Weyl index, a colour index and a
weak-isospin index. The Lorentz group moves only the first, the gauge group only the last
two (up to the hypercharge scalar), so each action is recorded as a sum over the indices it
moves. Dualising inverts and transposes the coefficient matrices, and conjugating stars
them; the four combinations below are what a component of a quark-doublet symbol needs.

## H. The gauge weight of the QuarkDoublet components

The gauge torus acts diagonally on the basis of `QuarkDoublet`; the weights are recorded by
`QuarkDoublet.valueGaugeWeight`, and pass to the dual and conjugate-dual coordinate
functionals with the expected signs.
## I. The boost weight of the QuarkDoublet components

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.basis
declarations.doc: A basis on the quark doublets.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def basis : Module.Basis (Fin 2 × Fin 3 × Fin 2) ℂ QuarkDoublet
instance : Module.Finite ℂ QuarkDoublet
instance : Module.Free ℂ QuarkDoublet

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.colourWeakEquiv
declarations.doc:
The colour and weak factors of the quark doublet combined into a single Euclidean
factor over `Fin 3 × Fin 2`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def colourWeakEquiv :
    EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 3) ⊗[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 2) ≃ₗ[ℂ] (Fin 3 × Fin 2 → ℂ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.colourWeakEquiv_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma colourWeakEquiv_tmul (c : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 3)) (w : EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 2))
    (p : Fin 3 × Fin 2) :
    colourWeakEquiv (c ⊗ₜ[ℂ] w) p = c.ofLp p.1 * w.ofLp p.2

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.jetValLinEquiv
declarations.doc:
Absorbs the jet ring into the combined colour–weak index: a jet of a quark doublet is
the same thing as a left-handed Weyl spinor tensored with a `SpaceTimeAlgebra`-valued
colour–weak vector,

  `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] QuarkDoublet ≃
    LeftHandedWeyl ⊗[ℂ] EuclideanSpace SpaceTimeAlgebra (Fin 3 × Fin 2)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetValLinEquiv :
    SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] QuarkDoublet ≃ₗ[ℂ]
      Fermion.LeftHandedWeyl ⊗[ℂ] EuclideanSpace SpaceTimeAlgebra (Fin 3 × Fin 2)

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.jetGaugeMatrix
declarations.doc:
The matrix of jets through which a jet of gauge transformations acts on the combined
colour–weak index of the quark doublet: the Kronecker product of the `SU(3)` and `SU(2)`
power-series matrices, scaled by the hypercharge power series `u`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetGaugeMatrix (U : JetGaugeGroupI) :
    Matrix (Fin 3 × Fin 2) (Fin 3 × Fin 2) SpaceTimeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.jetGaugeMatrix_one
declarations.statement: lemma jetGaugeMatrix_one : jetGaugeMatrix 1 = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.jetGaugeMatrix_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma jetGaugeMatrix_mul (U₁ U₂ : JetGaugeGroupI) :
    jetGaugeMatrix (U₁ * U₂) = jetGaugeMatrix U₁ * jetGaugeMatrix U₂

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repJetGaugeGroupI
declarations.doc:
The `(3, 2)_{1}` action of the jet gauge group on the jet space of the quark doublet.
Through `jetValLinEquiv` the Kronecker matrix of the gauge jet, carrying the hypercharge
phase `u`, acts `SpaceTimeAlgebra`-linearly on the combined colour–weak factor by matrix-vector
multiplication, while the Weyl factor is untouched.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repJetGaugeGroupI :
    Representation ℂ JetGaugeGroupI (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] QuarkDoublet)

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.jetGaugeMatrix_ofConstant
declarations.doc:
The entries of the gauge matrix of a jet of a constant gauge transformation are the
constant power series with the global gauge coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetGaugeMatrix_ofConstant (g : GaugeGroupI) (p q : Fin 3 × Fin 2) :
    jetGaugeMatrix (JetGaugeGroupI.ofConstant g) p q =
      MvPowerSeries.C ((g.toU1.1 : ℂ) * (g.toSU3.1 p.1 q.1 * g.toSU2.1 p.2 q.2))

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.jetValLinEquiv_smul
declarations.doc:
The identification of the jets of the quark doublet intertwines multiplication by a
scalar jet with the `SpaceTimeAlgebra`-scalar action on the colour–weak coordinates.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetValLinEquiv_smul (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] QuarkDoublet) :
    jetValLinEquiv (χ • z)
      = Module.End.lTensorAlgHom ℂ (EuclideanSpace SpaceTimeAlgebra (Fin 3 × Fin 2))
          Fermion.LeftHandedWeyl
          ((LinearMap.lsmul SpaceTimeAlgebra
            (EuclideanSpace SpaceTimeAlgebra (Fin 3 × Fin 2)) χ).restrictScalars ℂ)
          (jetValLinEquiv z)

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repJetGaugeGroupI_smul
declarations.doc:
**The jet gauge action on the jets of the quark doublet is fibrewise**: it commutes
with multiplication by scalar jets.
declarations.statement:
lemma repJetGaugeGroupI_smul (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra)
    (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] QuarkDoublet) :
    repJetGaugeGroupI U (χ • z) = χ • repJetGaugeGroupI U z

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repJetGaugeGroupI_ofConstant
declarations.doc:
On jets of constant gauge transformations the jet action reduces to the global gauge
action on the fibre: the `(3, 2)_{1}` action on the quark-doublet factor, and the trivial
action on the jet ring.
declarations.statement:
lemma repJetGaugeGroupI_ofConstant (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    repJetGaugeGroupI (JetGaugeGroupI.ofConstant g) =
      TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (repGaugeGroupI g)

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.basis_eq_mk
declarations.doc: The quark-doublet basis vector as an explicit spinor–colour–weak tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_eq_mk (k : Fin 2) (c : Fin 3) (w : Fin 2) : basis (k, c, w) =
    ⟨Fermion.LeftHandedWeyl.basis k ⊗ₜ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin 3) ℂ c
      ⊗ₜ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin 2) ℂ w⟩

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repLorentzGroup_apply_basis
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on the quark-doublet basis: the colour and weak indices are inert
and the spinor index transforms by the matrix itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_apply_basis (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3 × Fin 2) :
    repLorentzGroup Λ (basis j) = ∑ β, Λ.1 β j.1 • basis (β, j.2.1, j.2.2)

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repLorentzGroup_dual_dualBasis
declarations.doc:
The quark-doublet coordinate functionals transform contragrediently, by the inverse
matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_dual_dualBasis (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3 × Fin 2) :
    repLorentzGroup.dual Λ (basis.dualBasis j) =
      ∑ β, (Λ⁻¹).1 j.1 β • basis.dualBasis (β, j.2.1, j.2.2)

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repLorentzGroup_conj_apply_basis
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on the conjugate quark-doublet basis: the coefficients are the
conjugates of those of the quark-doublet action.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_conj_apply_basis (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3 × Fin 2) :
    repLorentzGroup.conj Λ ((Basis.conj basis) j) =
      ∑ β, star (Λ.1 β j.1) • (Basis.conj basis) (β, j.2.1, j.2.2)

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repLorentzGroup_conj_dual_dualBasis
declarations.doc:
The conjugate quark-doublet coordinate functionals transform by the entrywise
conjugate of the inverse matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_conj_dual_dualBasis (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3 × Fin 2) :
    repLorentzGroup.conj.dual Λ ((Basis.conj basis).dualBasis j) =
      ∑ β, star ((Λ⁻¹).1 j.1 β) • (Basis.conj basis).dualBasis (β, j.2.1, j.2.2)

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repLorentzGroup_neg_one
declarations.doc:
**The centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` acts on the quark-doublet space by `-1`**: the value space carries a
single Weyl-spinor index, and `-1` is not the identity on a half-integer spin.
declarations.statement: lemma repLorentzGroup_neg_one : repLorentzGroup (-1) = -LinearMap.id

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repLorentzGroup_conj_neg_one
declarations.doc:
The centre acts on the conjugate quark-doublet space by `-1` as well: conjugation does not
move a real sign.
declarations.statement: lemma repLorentzGroup_conj_neg_one : repLorentzGroup.conj (-1) = -LinearMap.id

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repGaugeGroupI_apply_basis
declarations.doc:
The gauge action on the quark-doublet basis: the spinor index is inert, the colour
index transforms by the `SU(3)` matrix and the weak index by the `SU(2)` matrix, scaled
by the hypercharge factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_apply_basis (g : GaugeGroupI) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3 × Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (basis j) =
      ∑ c, ∑ w, (g.toU1.1 * g.toSU3.1 c j.2.1 * g.toSU2.1 w j.2.2) • basis (j.1, c, w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repGaugeGroupI_dual_dualBasis
declarations.doc:
The quark-doublet coordinate functionals carry the contragredient gauge action: the
hypercharge, `SU(3)` and `SU(2)` factors of the inverse group element, transposed.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_dual_dualBasis (g : GaugeGroupI) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3 × Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI.dual g (basis.dualBasis j) =
      ∑ c, ∑ w, ((g⁻¹).toU1.1 * (g⁻¹).toSU3.1 j.2.1 c * (g⁻¹).toSU2.1 j.2.2 w) •
        basis.dualBasis (j.1, c, w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repGaugeGroupI_conj_apply_basis
declarations.doc:
The gauge action on the conjugate quark-doublet basis: the coefficients of the
quark-doublet action, conjugated.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_conj_apply_basis (g : GaugeGroupI) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3 × Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI.conj g ((Basis.conj basis) j) =
      ∑ c, ∑ w, star (g.toU1.1 * g.toSU3.1 c j.2.1 * g.toSU2.1 w j.2.2) •
        (Basis.conj basis) (j.1, c, w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repGaugeGroupI_conj_dual_dualBasis
declarations.doc:
The conjugate quark-doublet coordinate functionals carry the conjugate of the
contragredient gauge action.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_conj_dual_dualBasis (g : GaugeGroupI) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3 × Fin 2) :
    repGaugeGroupI.conj.dual g ((Basis.conj basis).dualBasis j) =
      ∑ c, ∑ w, star ((g⁻¹).toU1.1 * (g⁻¹).toSU3.1 j.2.1 c * (g⁻¹).toSU2.1 j.2.2 w) •
        (Basis.conj basis).dualBasis (j.1, c, w)

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.valueGaugeWeight
declarations.doc:
The gauge weight of the quark-doublet basis: the colour and isospin weights and
hypercharge `1`.
declarations.statement: def QuarkDoublet.valueGaugeWeight (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3 × Fin 2) : GaugeWeight

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repGaugeGroupI_gaugeTorusGen_basis
declarations.doc:
The gauge torus acts diagonally on the basis of `QuarkDoublet`, with the weights
`QuarkDoublet.valueGaugeWeight`.
declarations.statement:
lemma QuarkDoublet.repGaugeGroupI_gaugeTorusGen_basis (i : Fin 4) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3 × Fin 2) :
    QuarkDoublet.repGaugeGroupI (gaugeTorusGen i) (QuarkDoublet.basis j)
      = ((expI : ℂ) ^ GaugeWeight.coord (QuarkDoublet.valueGaugeWeight j) i) •
        QuarkDoublet.basis j

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repGaugeGroupI_dual_gaugeTorusGen_coord
declarations.doc:
The dual action of the gauge torus on the coordinate functionals of
`QuarkDoublet`: the weights are negated.
declarations.statement:
lemma QuarkDoublet.repGaugeGroupI_dual_gaugeTorusGen_coord (i : Fin 4)
    (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3 × Fin 2) :
    QuarkDoublet.repGaugeGroupI.dual (gaugeTorusGen i) (QuarkDoublet.basis.coord j)
      = ((expI : ℂ) ^ (-(GaugeWeight.coord (QuarkDoublet.valueGaugeWeight j) i))) •
        QuarkDoublet.basis.coord j

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repGaugeGroupI_conj_dual_gaugeTorusGen_coord
declarations.doc:
The dual of the conjugate action of the gauge torus on the coordinate functionals
of the conjugate of `QuarkDoublet`: the two negations cancel and the weights are those of
the value space.
declarations.statement:
lemma QuarkDoublet.repGaugeGroupI_conj_dual_gaugeTorusGen_coord (i : Fin 4)
    (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3 × Fin 2) :
    QuarkDoublet.repGaugeGroupI.conj.dual (gaugeTorusGen i)
      (((Basis.conj QuarkDoublet.basis)).coord j)
      = ((expI : ℂ) ^ GaugeWeight.coord (QuarkDoublet.valueGaugeWeight j) i) •
        ((Basis.conj QuarkDoublet.basis)).coord j

declarations.name: StandardModel.quarkDoublet_repLorentzGroup_boostAxis_two_basis
declarations.doc:
The quark-doublet basis diagonalises the `z`-boost: the colour and isospin indices are
inert.
declarations.statement:
lemma quarkDoublet_repLorentzGroup_boostAxis_two_basis (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0)
    (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3 × Fin 2) :
    QuarkDoublet.repLorentzGroup (SL2C.boostAxis 2 t ht) (QuarkDoublet.basis j)
      = ((t : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ (weylWeight j.1) • QuarkDoublet.basis j

modules.title: The infinitesimal gauge action on the quark doublet
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The `(3, 2)_{1}` action of the gauge algebra on the quark doublet: the colour and weak
parts of the algebra element act on the combined colour–weak index through the Kronecker
sum, and the hypercharge part scales, all through the physicists' factor of `i`, matching
the group action `u • (U₃ ⊗ₖ U₂)` infinitesimally. The main theorem shows this is the
infinitesimal action underlying the jet gauge action `QuarkDoublet.repJetGaugeGroupI`,
in the sense of `LocalGaugeData.IsInfinitesimalActionOf`.

## ii. Key results

- `colourWeakEnd` : the endomorphism of the quark doublet defined by a colour–weak
  matrix.
- `gaugeAlgebraAction` : the infinitesimal `(3, 2)_{1}` action of the gauge algebra.
- `jetGaugeMatrix_map_pderiv` : the derivative identity for the colour–weak matrix.
- `jetGaugeMatrix_mul_jetActionMatrix` : the equivariance identity for the colour–weak
  matrix.
- `isInfinitesimalActionOf` : the gauge-algebra action is the infinitesimal action
  underlying the jet gauge action.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The action of the gauge algebra
- B. The colour–weak matrix of the jet gauge action
- C. The infinitesimal action underlies the jet gauge action
- D. The gauge action commutes with the Lorentz action

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The action of the gauge algebra

## B. The colour–weak matrix of the jet gauge action

## C. The infinitesimal action underlies the jet gauge action

The `(3, 2)_{1}` action of the gauge algebra is the infinitesimal action underlying the
jet gauge action, in the sense of `LocalGaugeData.IsInfinitesimalActionOf`: the base-point
Taylor coefficients of the jet action satisfy the Maurer–Cartan Leibniz law and
intertwine the action with the adjoint transports. The proofs work through the
colour–weak matrix `jetGaugeMatrix` of the jet action and the all-orders matrix Leibniz
rule at the base point.
## D. The gauge action commutes with the Lorentz action

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.colourWeakValLinEquiv
declarations.doc:
The identification of the quark doublet with a left-handed Weyl spinor tensored with
a colour–weak vector over the combined index `Fin 3 × Fin 2`: the `ℂ`-level analogue
of `jetValLinEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def colourWeakValLinEquiv :
    QuarkDoublet ≃ₗ[ℂ] Fermion.LeftHandedWeyl ⊗[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 3 × Fin 2)

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.colourWeakEnd
declarations.doc:
The endomorphism of the quark doublet defined by a complex matrix over the
combined colour–weak index, with the Weyl factor untouched.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def colourWeakEnd (A : Matrix (Fin 3 × Fin 2) (Fin 3 × Fin 2) ℂ) :
    QuarkDoublet →ₗ[ℂ] QuarkDoublet

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.colourWeakEnd_apply_mk
declarations.statement:
lemma colourWeakEnd_apply_mk (A : Matrix (Fin 3 × Fin 2) (Fin 3 × Fin 2) ℂ)
    (v : QuarkDoublet) :
    colourWeakEnd A v
      = colourWeakValLinEquiv.symm
          (Module.End.lTensorAlgHom ℂ (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 3 × Fin 2))
            Fermion.LeftHandedWeyl
            (Matrix.toLpLinAlgEquiv 2 A) (colourWeakValLinEquiv v))

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.colourWeakEnd_add
declarations.statement:
lemma colourWeakEnd_add (A B : Matrix (Fin 3 × Fin 2) (Fin 3 × Fin 2) ℂ) :
    colourWeakEnd (A + B) = colourWeakEnd A + colourWeakEnd B

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.colourWeakEnd_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma colourWeakEnd_smul (z : ℂ) (A : Matrix (Fin 3 × Fin 2) (Fin 3 × Fin 2) ℂ) :
    colourWeakEnd (z • A) = z • colourWeakEnd A

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.colourWeakEnd_zero
declarations.statement: lemma colourWeakEnd_zero : colourWeakEnd 0 = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.colourWeakEnd_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma colourWeakEnd_neg (A : Matrix (Fin 3 × Fin 2) (Fin 3 × Fin 2) ℂ) :
    colourWeakEnd (-A) = -colourWeakEnd A

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.colourWeakEnd_multiset_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma colourWeakEnd_multiset_sum
    (m : Multiset (Matrix (Fin 3 × Fin 2) (Fin 3 × Fin 2) ℂ)) :
    colourWeakEnd m.sum = (m.map colourWeakEnd).sum

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.colourWeakEnd_mul
declarations.doc: The colour–weak endomorphisms compose through matrix multiplication.
declarations.statement:
lemma colourWeakEnd_mul (A B : Matrix (Fin 3 × Fin 2) (Fin 3 × Fin 2) ℂ) :
    colourWeakEnd (A * B) = colourWeakEnd A ∘ₗ colourWeakEnd B

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.actionMatrix
declarations.doc:
The matrix of the infinitesimal `(3, 2)_{1}` action of a gauge algebra element on
the combined colour–weak index: `i` times the Kronecker sum of the colour and weak
parts, shifted by `i` times the hypercharge.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def actionMatrix (c : GaugeAlgebra) :
    Matrix (Fin 3 × Fin 2) (Fin 3 × Fin 2) ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.gaugeAlgebraAction
declarations.doc:
**The infinitesimal action of the gauge algebra on the quark doublet**: the
derivative of the `(3, 2)_{1}` action of the gauge group, real-linear in the
algebra slot and complex-linear in the value slot — the form consumed by the
covariant derivative `GaugeAlgebraRealization.covDerivIter` and by
`LocalGaugeData.IsInfinitesimalActionOf`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def gaugeAlgebraAction :
    GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] QuarkDoublet →ₗ[ℂ] QuarkDoublet

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.jetActionMatrix
declarations.doc:
The jet-valued matrix of the infinitesimal `(3, 2)_{1}` action of a jet of gauge
algebra elements: the jet analogue of `actionMatrix`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetActionMatrix (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    Matrix (Fin 3 × Fin 2) (Fin 3 × Fin 2) SpaceTimeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.jetActionMatrix_map_cc_foldl
declarations.doc:
The base-point Taylor coefficients of the jet action matrix are the action matrices
of the base-point Taylor coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetActionMatrix_map_cc_foldl (p : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    ((jetActionMatrix a).map fun f =>
        constantCoeff (SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv p f))
      = actionMatrix (JetGaugeAlgebra.eval (JetGaugeAlgebra.iteratedDeriv p a))

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repJetGaugeGroupI_eq_jetGaugeMatrix
declarations.statement:
lemma repJetGaugeGroupI_eq_jetGaugeMatrix (U : JetGaugeGroupI)
    (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] QuarkDoublet) :
    repJetGaugeGroupI U z
      = jetValLinEquiv.symm
          (Module.End.lTensorAlgHom ℂ (EuclideanSpace SpaceTimeAlgebra (Fin 3 × Fin 2))
            Fermion.LeftHandedWeyl
            ((Matrix.toLpLinAlgEquiv 2 (jetGaugeMatrix U)).restrictScalars ℂ)
            (jetValLinEquiv z))

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.jetGaugeMatrix_map_pderiv
declarations.doc:
**The derivative identity** for the colour–weak matrix of the jet gauge action: the
formal derivative of the colour–weak matrix is minus the jet action matrix of the
Maurer–Cartan form times the colour–weak matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetGaugeMatrix_map_pderiv (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (jetGaugeMatrix U).map (fun f => pderiv μ f)
      = -(jetActionMatrix (maurerCartanForm U μ) * jetGaugeMatrix U)

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.jetGaugeMatrix_mul_jetActionMatrix
declarations.doc:
**The equivariance identity** for the colour–weak matrix of the jet gauge action:
the colour–weak matrix intertwines the constant jet action matrix with its adjoint
transform.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetGaugeMatrix_mul_jetActionMatrix (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (c : GaugeAlgebra) :
    jetGaugeMatrix U * jetActionMatrix (JetGaugeAlgebra.ofConstant c)
      = jetActionMatrix (JetGaugeAlgebra.adjointMap U (JetGaugeAlgebra.ofConstant c))
        * jetGaugeMatrix U

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repCoeff_eq
declarations.doc:
**The base-point Taylor coefficients of the jet gauge action** on the quark
doublet are the colour–weak endomorphisms of the base-point Taylor coefficients of
the colour–weak matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCoeff_eq (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    GaugeAlgebraRealization.repCoeff repJetGaugeGroupI U x
      = colourWeakEnd ((jetGaugeMatrix U).map fun f =>
          constantCoeff (SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv x f))

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.colourWeakEnd_one
declarations.doc: The colour–weak endomorphism of the identity matrix is the identity.
declarations.statement: lemma colourWeakEnd_one : colourWeakEnd 1 = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.repCoeff_zero_of_eval_eq_one
declarations.doc:
At the base point, a gauge jet with trivial value acts trivially: the zeroth
Taylor coefficient of the jet gauge action is the identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCoeff_zero_of_eval_eq_one {U : JetGaugeGroupI} (hU : U.eval = 1) :
    GaugeAlgebraRealization.repCoeff repJetGaugeGroupI U 0 = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.isInfinitesimalActionOf
declarations.doc:
**The `(3, 2)_{1}` action of the gauge algebra is the infinitesimal action
underlying the jet gauge action on the quark doublet**: its base-point Taylor
coefficients obey the Maurer–Cartan Leibniz law and intertwine the action with the
adjoint transports.
declarations.statement:
lemma isInfinitesimalActionOf :
    localGaugeData.IsInfinitesimalActionOf gaugeAlgebraAction repJetGaugeGroupI

declarations.name: StandardModel.QuarkDoublet.gaugeAlgebraAction_comm_repLorentzGroup
declarations.doc:
The infinitesimal gauge action on the quark doublet acts on the combined colour–weak
factor, the Lorentz action on the Weyl factor, so the two commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAlgebraAction_comm_repLorentzGroup (c : GaugeAlgebra) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ))
    (v : QuarkDoublet) :
    QuarkDoublet.gaugeAlgebraAction c (QuarkDoublet.repLorentzGroup Λ v) =
      QuarkDoublet.repLorentzGroup Λ (QuarkDoublet.gaugeAlgebraAction c v)

modules.title: Up-type singlets
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define the type corresponding to
the target vector space of an up-type singlet quark field in the Standard Model.

On this type we define a representation of the Lorentz group, and a
representation of the Standard Model gauge group.

## ii. Key results

- `basis` : a basis on the up singlets
- `jetValLinEquiv` : absorbs the jet ring into the colour index: a jet of an up-type singlet is the
  same thing as a right-handed Weyl spinor tensored with a `SpaceTimeAlgebra`-valued colour vector,
  `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] UpSinglet ≃ RightHandedWeyl ⊗[ℂ] EuclideanSpace SpaceTimeAlgebra (Fin 3)`
- `repJetGaugeGroupI` : the `(3, 1)_{4}` action of the jet gauge group on the jet space of the
  up-type singlet
- `jetValLinEquiv_smul` : the identification of the jets of the up-type singlet intertwines
  multiplication by a scalar jet with the `SpaceTimeAlgebra`-scalar action on the colour coordinates

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Equivalence with the underlying tensor product space
- B. The structure of a module
- C. The basis of the up-singlet space
- D. Lorentz group representation
- E. The representation of the Standard Model gauge group
- F. The representation of the jet gauge group
- G. Component transformation laws
- H. The gauge weight of the UpSinglet components
- I. The boost weight of the UpSinglet components

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Equivalence with the underlying tensor product space

## B. The structure of a module

The AddCommGroup and module instances are inherited from the underlying tensor product space.
## C. The basis of the up-singlet space
## D. Lorentz group representation
## E. The representation of the Standard Model gauge group
## F. The representation of the jet gauge group

## G. Component transformation laws

The basis of `UpSinglet` splits as a right-handed Weyl index and a colour index. The
Lorentz group moves only the first, the gauge group only the second (up to the hypercharge
scalar), so both actions are recorded as a single sum over the index they move. Dualising
inverts and transposes the coefficient matrix, and conjugating stars it; the four
combinations below are what a component of an up-singlet symbol needs.

## H. The gauge weight of the UpSinglet components

The gauge torus acts diagonally on the basis of `UpSinglet`; the weights are recorded by
`UpSinglet.valueGaugeWeight`, and pass to the dual and conjugate-dual coordinate
functionals with the expected signs.
## I. The boost weight of the UpSinglet components

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.basis
declarations.doc: A basis on the up singlets.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def basis : Module.Basis (Fin 2 × Fin 3) ℂ UpSinglet
instance : Module.Finite ℂ UpSinglet
instance : Module.Free ℂ UpSinglet

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.jetValLinEquiv
declarations.doc:
Absorbs the jet ring into the colour index: a jet of an up-type singlet is the
same thing as a right-handed Weyl spinor tensored with a `SpaceTimeAlgebra`-valued colour
vector,

  `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] UpSinglet ≃ RightHandedWeyl ⊗[ℂ] EuclideanSpace SpaceTimeAlgebra (Fin 3)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetValLinEquiv :
    SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] UpSinglet ≃ₗ[ℂ]
      Fermion.RightHandedWeyl ⊗[ℂ] EuclideanSpace SpaceTimeAlgebra (Fin 3)

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repJetGaugeGroupI
declarations.doc:
The `(3, 1)_{4}` action of the jet gauge group on the jet space of the up-type
singlet. Through `jetValLinEquiv` the colour matrix of the gauge jet, carrying the
`4` hypercharge phase `u ^ 4`, acts `SpaceTimeAlgebra`-linearly on the colour factor by
matrix-vector multiplication, while the Weyl factor is untouched.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repJetGaugeGroupI :
    Representation ℂ JetGaugeGroupI (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] UpSinglet)

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.jetValLinEquiv_smul
declarations.doc:
The identification of the jets of the up-type singlet intertwines multiplication by
a scalar jet with the `SpaceTimeAlgebra`-scalar action on the colour coordinates.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetValLinEquiv_smul (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] UpSinglet) :
    jetValLinEquiv (χ • z)
      = Module.End.lTensorAlgHom ℂ (EuclideanSpace SpaceTimeAlgebra (Fin 3))
          Fermion.RightHandedWeyl
          ((LinearMap.lsmul SpaceTimeAlgebra
              (EuclideanSpace SpaceTimeAlgebra (Fin 3)) χ).restrictScalars ℂ)
          (jetValLinEquiv z)

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repJetGaugeGroupI_smul
declarations.doc:
**The jet gauge action on the jets of the up-type singlet is fibrewise**: it commutes
with multiplication by scalar jets.
declarations.statement:
lemma repJetGaugeGroupI_smul (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra)
    (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] UpSinglet) :
    repJetGaugeGroupI U (χ • z) = χ • repJetGaugeGroupI U z

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repJetGaugeGroupI_ofConstant
declarations.doc:
On jets of constant gauge transformations the jet action reduces to the global
gauge action on the fibre: the `(3, 1)_{4}` action on the up-singlet factor, and the
trivial action on the jet ring.
declarations.statement:
lemma repJetGaugeGroupI_ofConstant (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    repJetGaugeGroupI (JetGaugeGroupI.ofConstant g) =
      TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (repGaugeGroupI g)

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.basis_eq_mk
declarations.doc: The up-singlet basis vector as an explicit spinor–colour tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_eq_mk (k : Fin 2) (c : Fin 3) : basis (k, c) =
    ⟨Fermion.RightHandedWeyl.basis k ⊗ₜ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin 3) ℂ c⟩

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repLorentzGroup_apply_basis
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on the up-singlet basis: the colour index is inert and the
spinor index transforms by the entrywise conjugate matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_apply_basis (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    repLorentzGroup Λ (basis j) = ∑ β, star (Λ.1 β j.1) • basis (β, j.2)

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repLorentzGroup_dual_dualBasis
declarations.doc:
The up-singlet coordinate functionals transform contragrediently, by the entrywise
conjugate of the inverse matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_dual_dualBasis (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    repLorentzGroup.dual Λ (basis.dualBasis j) =
      ∑ β, star ((Λ⁻¹).1 j.1 β) • basis.dualBasis (β, j.2)

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repLorentzGroup_conj_apply_basis
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on the conjugate up-singlet basis: the coefficients are the
conjugates of those of the up-singlet action, that is, the matrix itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_conj_apply_basis (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    repLorentzGroup.conj Λ ((Basis.conj basis) j)
      = ∑ β, Λ.1 β j.1 • (Basis.conj basis) (β, j.2)

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repLorentzGroup_conj_dual_dualBasis
declarations.doc: The conjugate up-singlet coordinate functionals transform by the inverse matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_conj_dual_dualBasis (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    repLorentzGroup.conj.dual Λ ((Basis.conj basis).dualBasis j) =
      ∑ β, (Λ⁻¹).1 j.1 β • (Basis.conj basis).dualBasis (β, j.2)

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repLorentzGroup_neg_one
declarations.doc:
**The centre of `SL(2,ℂ)` acts on the up-singlet space by `-1`**: the value space carries a
single Weyl-spinor index, and `-1` is not the identity on a half-integer spin.
declarations.statement: lemma repLorentzGroup_neg_one : repLorentzGroup (-1) = -LinearMap.id

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repLorentzGroup_conj_neg_one
declarations.doc:
The centre acts on the conjugate up-singlet space by `-1` as well: conjugation does not
move a real sign.
declarations.statement: lemma repLorentzGroup_conj_neg_one : repLorentzGroup.conj (-1) = -LinearMap.id

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_apply_basis
declarations.doc:
The gauge action on the up-singlet basis: the spinor index is inert and the colour
index transforms by the `SU(3)` matrix, scaled by the hypercharge factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_apply_basis (g : GaugeGroupI) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    repGaugeGroupI g (basis j) =
      ∑ c, (g.toU1.1 ^ 4 * g.toSU3.1 c j.2) • basis (j.1, c)

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_dual_dualBasis
declarations.doc:
The up-singlet coordinate functionals carry the contragredient gauge action: the
hypercharge and `SU(3)` factors of the inverse group element, transposed.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_dual_dualBasis (g : GaugeGroupI) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    repGaugeGroupI.dual g (basis.dualBasis j) =
      ∑ c, ((g⁻¹).toU1.1 ^ 4 * (g⁻¹).toSU3.1 j.2 c) • basis.dualBasis (j.1, c)

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_conj_apply_basis
declarations.doc:
The gauge action on the conjugate up-singlet basis: the coefficients of the
up-singlet action, conjugated.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_conj_apply_basis (g : GaugeGroupI) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    repGaugeGroupI.conj g ((Basis.conj basis) j) =
      ∑ c, star (g.toU1.1 ^ 4 * g.toSU3.1 c j.2) • (Basis.conj basis) (j.1, c)

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_conj_dual_dualBasis
declarations.doc:
The conjugate up-singlet coordinate functionals carry the conjugate of the
contragredient gauge action.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeGroupI_conj_dual_dualBasis (g : GaugeGroupI) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    repGaugeGroupI.conj.dual g ((Basis.conj basis).dualBasis j) =
      ∑ c, star ((g⁻¹).toU1.1 ^ 4 * (g⁻¹).toSU3.1 j.2 c) •
        (Basis.conj basis).dualBasis (j.1, c)

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.valueGaugeWeight
declarations.doc:
The gauge weight of the up-singlet basis: the colour weights and hypercharge
`4`.
declarations.statement: def UpSinglet.valueGaugeWeight (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) : GaugeWeight

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_gaugeTorusGen_basis
declarations.doc:
The gauge torus acts diagonally on the basis of `UpSinglet`, with the weights
`UpSinglet.valueGaugeWeight`.
declarations.statement:
lemma UpSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_gaugeTorusGen_basis (i : Fin 4) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    UpSinglet.repGaugeGroupI (gaugeTorusGen i) (UpSinglet.basis j)
      = ((expI : ℂ) ^ GaugeWeight.coord (UpSinglet.valueGaugeWeight j) i) •
        UpSinglet.basis j

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_dual_gaugeTorusGen_coord
declarations.doc:
The dual action of the gauge torus on the coordinate functionals of
`UpSinglet`: the weights are negated.
declarations.statement:
lemma UpSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_dual_gaugeTorusGen_coord (i : Fin 4) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    UpSinglet.repGaugeGroupI.dual (gaugeTorusGen i) (UpSinglet.basis.coord j)
      = ((expI : ℂ) ^ (-(GaugeWeight.coord (UpSinglet.valueGaugeWeight j) i))) •
        UpSinglet.basis.coord j

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_conj_dual_gaugeTorusGen_coord
declarations.doc:
The dual of the conjugate action of the gauge torus on the coordinate functionals
of the conjugate of `UpSinglet`: the two negations cancel and the weights are those of
the value space.
declarations.statement:
lemma UpSinglet.repGaugeGroupI_conj_dual_gaugeTorusGen_coord (i : Fin 4) (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    UpSinglet.repGaugeGroupI.conj.dual (gaugeTorusGen i) (((Basis.conj UpSinglet.basis)).coord j)
      = ((expI : ℂ) ^ GaugeWeight.coord (UpSinglet.valueGaugeWeight j) i) •
        ((Basis.conj UpSinglet.basis)).coord j

declarations.name: StandardModel.upSinglet_repLorentzGroup_boostAxis_two_basis
declarations.doc: The up-singlet basis diagonalises the `z`-boost.
declarations.statement:
lemma upSinglet_repLorentzGroup_boostAxis_two_basis (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0)
    (j : Fin 2 × Fin 3) :
    UpSinglet.repLorentzGroup (SL2C.boostAxis 2 t ht) (UpSinglet.basis j)
      = ((t : ℝ) : ℂ) ^ (weylWeight j.1) • UpSinglet.basis j

modules.title: The infinitesimal gauge action on the up-type singlet
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The `(3, 1)_{4}` action of the gauge algebra on the up-type singlet: the colour part of
the algebra element acts on the colour index and the hypercharge part scales, both
through the physicists' factor of `i`, matching the group action `u ^ 4 • U₃`
infinitesimally. The main theorem shows this is the infinitesimal action underlying the
jet gauge action `UpSinglet.repJetGaugeGroupI`, in the sense of
`LocalGaugeData.IsInfinitesimalActionOf`.

## ii. Key results

- `colourEnd` : the endomorphism of the up singlet defined by a colour matrix.
- `gaugeAlgebraAction` : the infinitesimal `(3, 1)_{4}` action of the gauge algebra.
- `upMatrix` : the `SpaceTimeAlgebra`-valued colour matrix of the jet gauge action.
- `upMatrix_map_pderiv` : the derivative identity for the colour matrix.
- `upMatrix_mul_jetActionMatrix` : the equivariance identity for the colour matrix.
- `isInfinitesimalActionOf` : the gauge-algebra action is the infinitesimal action
  underlying the jet gauge action.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The action of the gauge algebra
- B. The colour matrix of the jet gauge action
- C. The infinitesimal action underlies the jet gauge action
- D. The gauge action commutes with the Lorentz action

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The action of the gauge algebra

## B. The colour matrix of the jet gauge action

## C. The infinitesimal action underlies the jet gauge action

The `(3, 1)_{4}` action of the gauge algebra is the infinitesimal action underlying the
jet gauge action, in the sense of `LocalGaugeData.IsInfinitesimalActionOf`: the base-point
Taylor coefficients of the jet action satisfy the Maurer–Cartan Leibniz law and
intertwine the action with the adjoint transports. The proofs work through the colour
matrix of the jet action and the all-orders matrix Leibniz rule at the base point.
## D. The gauge action commutes with the Lorentz action

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.colourEnd
declarations.doc:
The endomorphism of the up singlet defined by a `3 × 3` complex matrix acting on
the colour index, with the Weyl factor untouched.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def colourEnd (A : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ) :
    UpSinglet →ₗ[ℂ] UpSinglet

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.colourEnd_apply_mk
declarations.statement:
lemma colourEnd_apply_mk (A : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ) (v : UpSinglet) :
    colourEnd A v
      = valLinEquiv.symm
          (Module.End.lTensorAlgHom ℂ (EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin 3)) Fermion.RightHandedWeyl
            (Matrix.toLpLinAlgEquiv 2 A) (valLinEquiv v))

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.colourEnd_add
declarations.statement:
lemma colourEnd_add (A B : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ) :
    colourEnd (A + B) = colourEnd A + colourEnd B

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.colourEnd_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma colourEnd_smul (z : ℂ) (A : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ) :
    colourEnd (z • A) = z • colourEnd A

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.colourEnd_zero
declarations.statement: lemma colourEnd_zero : colourEnd 0 = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.colourEnd_neg
declarations.statement: lemma colourEnd_neg (A : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ) : colourEnd (-A) = -colourEnd A

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.colourEnd_multiset_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma colourEnd_multiset_sum (m : Multiset (Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ)) :
    colourEnd m.sum = (m.map colourEnd).sum

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.colourEnd_mul
declarations.doc: The colour endomorphisms compose through matrix multiplication.
declarations.statement:
lemma colourEnd_mul (A B : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ) :
    colourEnd (A * B) = colourEnd A ∘ₗ colourEnd B

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.actionMatrix
declarations.doc:
The matrix of the infinitesimal `(3, 1)_{4}` action of a gauge algebra element on
the colour index: `i` times the colour part, shifted by `i` times `4` the
hypercharge.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def actionMatrix (c : GaugeAlgebra) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.gaugeAlgebraAction
declarations.doc:
**The infinitesimal action of the gauge algebra on the up-type singlet**: the
derivative of the `(3, 1)_{4}` action of the gauge group, real-linear in the
algebra slot and complex-linear in the value slot — the form consumed by the
covariant derivative `GaugeAlgebraRealization.covDerivIter` and by
`LocalGaugeData.IsInfinitesimalActionOf`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def gaugeAlgebraAction :
    GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] UpSinglet →ₗ[ℂ] UpSinglet

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.jetActionMatrix
declarations.doc:
The jet-valued matrix of the infinitesimal `(3, 1)_{4}` action of a jet of gauge
algebra elements: the jet analogue of `actionMatrix`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def jetActionMatrix (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) SpaceTimeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.jetActionMatrix_map_cc_foldl
declarations.doc:
The base-point Taylor coefficients of the jet action matrix are the action matrices
of the base-point Taylor coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetActionMatrix_map_cc_foldl (p : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    ((jetActionMatrix a).map fun f =>
        constantCoeff (SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv p f))
      = actionMatrix (JetGaugeAlgebra.eval (JetGaugeAlgebra.iteratedDeriv p a))

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.upMatrix
declarations.doc:
The `SpaceTimeAlgebra`-valued colour matrix of the jet gauge action on the up singlet: the
colour matrix of the gauge jet carrying the `4` hypercharge phase.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def upMatrix (U : JetGaugeGroupI) : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) SpaceTimeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repJetGaugeGroupI_eq_upMatrix
declarations.statement:
lemma repJetGaugeGroupI_eq_upMatrix (U : JetGaugeGroupI)
    (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] UpSinglet) :
    repJetGaugeGroupI U z
      = jetValLinEquiv.symm
          (Module.End.lTensorAlgHom ℂ (EuclideanSpace SpaceTimeAlgebra (Fin 3))
            Fermion.RightHandedWeyl
            ((Matrix.toLpLinAlgEquiv 2 (upMatrix U)).restrictScalars ℂ)
            (jetValLinEquiv z))

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.upMatrix_map_pderiv
declarations.doc:
**The derivative identity** for the colour matrix of the jet gauge action: the
formal derivative of the colour matrix is minus the jet action matrix of the
Maurer–Cartan form times the colour matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma upMatrix_map_pderiv (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (upMatrix U).map (fun f => pderiv μ f)
      = -(jetActionMatrix (maurerCartanForm U μ) * upMatrix U)

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.upMatrix_mul_jetActionMatrix
declarations.doc:
**The equivariance identity** for the colour matrix of the jet gauge action: the
colour matrix intertwines the constant jet action matrix with its adjoint
transform.
declarations.statement:
lemma upMatrix_mul_jetActionMatrix (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (c : GaugeAlgebra) :
    upMatrix U * jetActionMatrix (JetGaugeAlgebra.ofConstant c)
      = jetActionMatrix (JetGaugeAlgebra.adjointMap U (JetGaugeAlgebra.ofConstant c))
        * upMatrix U

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repCoeff_eq
declarations.doc:
**The base-point Taylor coefficients of the jet gauge action** on the up-type
singlet are the colour endomorphisms of the base-point Taylor coefficients of the
colour matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCoeff_eq (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    GaugeAlgebraRealization.repCoeff repJetGaugeGroupI U x
      = colourEnd ((upMatrix U).map fun f =>
          constantCoeff (SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv x f))

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.colourEnd_one
declarations.doc: The colour endomorphism of the identity matrix is the identity.
declarations.statement: lemma colourEnd_one : colourEnd 1 = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.repCoeff_zero_of_eval_eq_one
declarations.doc:
At the base point, a gauge jet with trivial value acts trivially: the zeroth
Taylor coefficient of the jet gauge action is the identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCoeff_zero_of_eval_eq_one {U : JetGaugeGroupI} (hU : U.eval = 1) :
    GaugeAlgebraRealization.repCoeff repJetGaugeGroupI U 0 = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.isInfinitesimalActionOf
declarations.doc:
**The `(3, 1)_{4}` action of the gauge algebra is the infinitesimal action
underlying the jet gauge action on the up-type singlet**: its base-point Taylor
coefficients obey the Maurer–Cartan Leibniz law and intertwine the action with the
adjoint transports.
declarations.statement:
lemma isInfinitesimalActionOf :
    localGaugeData.IsInfinitesimalActionOf gaugeAlgebraAction repJetGaugeGroupI

declarations.name: StandardModel.UpSinglet.gaugeAlgebraAction_comm_repLorentzGroup
declarations.doc:
The infinitesimal gauge action on the up-type singlet acts on the colour factor, the
Lorentz action on the Weyl factor, so the two commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeAlgebraAction_comm_repLorentzGroup (c : GaugeAlgebra) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ))
    (v : UpSinglet) :
    UpSinglet.gaugeAlgebraAction c (UpSinglet.repLorentzGroup Λ v) =
      UpSinglet.repLorentzGroup Λ (UpSinglet.gaugeAlgebraAction c v)

modules.title: The field data of the Standard Model
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

`GaugeFieldData jets` is the matter content of a gauge theory over a gauge context: a
family of fermionic species and a family of bosonic species, each given by a
`MatterField`. The Standard Model has all the pieces — `StandardModel.localGaugeData` with its
Taylor–Leibniz law, and the five fermion types and the Higgs already packaged as matter
fields — and this file assembles them into `StandardModel.fieldData`.

The fermionic species are the constructors of `FermionType`: fifteen multiplets, one of
the five types in one of the three generations, each occurring exactly once. The
generation index is an argument of each constructor, so the species type is the
enumeration itself and carries no further factor. The matter field does not depend on the
generation, three generations being three copies of one multiplet distinguished only by
their Yukawa couplings, which are not field data. The bosonic family has the single Higgs
multiplet. The fermions are declared fermionic and the Higgs bosonic, as `GaugeFieldData`
requires of its two families. The gauge bosons are not a species: their generator space is
fixed by the gauge algebra alone, and `GaugeFieldData` supplies it as the connection sector.

From the datum the generic theory produces the generator spaces, the local field algebra
`fieldData.LocalFieldAlgebra`, the transformation data and the realization arrow, with no
further Standard Model input.

## ii. Key results

- `StandardModel.FermionType` : the fifteen fermion species, the five types in each of
  the three generations.
- `StandardModel.fieldData` : the field data of the Standard Model.
- `StandardModel.card_fieldData_fermionSpecies`,
  `StandardModel.card_fieldData_bosonSpecies` : fifteen fermionic multiplets, one Higgs.
- `StandardModel.fieldData_pureJetsActTrivially`,
  `StandardModel.fieldData_gaugeLorentzCompatible` : the datum satisfies the two
  conditions of the covariant derivative theory, assembled from the species-wise lemmas
  `StandardModel.fieldData_fermion_pureJetsActTrivially` and companions.
- `StandardModel.fieldData_massWeightScaleFermion_inclFermion_basis_tmul` : a fermionic
  component function `∂_s ψ_α` scales by `c ^ (3 + 2 |s|)`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The fermion species
- B. The field datum
- C. The conditions of the covariant derivative theory
- D. The mass weights

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The fermion species
## B. The field datum

## C. The conditions of the covariant derivative theory

Every species of the Standard Model satisfies the two conditions
`MatterField.PureJetsActTrivially` and `MatterField.GaugeLorentzCompatible`, species by
species, and the datum therefore satisfies the conjunctions
`GaugeFieldData.PureJetsActTrivially` and `GaugeFieldData.GaugeLorentzCompatible`.

## D. The mass weights

A Standard Model fermion carries mass weight three and the Higgs weight two, in the units
in which a derivative has weight two. The first two are read off the matter fields, the
third is already built into the generator spaces.

declarations.name: StandardModel.FermionType
declarations.doc:
The fifteen fermion species of the Standard Model: each of the five fermion types in
each of the three generations, the generation `i : Fin 3` carried by the constructor.
Two generations of one type share a representation package but are distinct species.
declarations.statement:
inductive FermionType where
  /-- The lepton doublet of generation `i`, `(1, 2)_{-3}`. -/
  | leptonDoublet (i : Fin 3) : FermionType
  /-- The charged-lepton singlet of generation `i`, `(1, 1)_{-6}`. -/
  | leptonSinglet (i : Fin 3) : FermionType
  /-- The quark doublet of generation `i`, `(3, 2)_{1}`. -/
  | quarkDoublet (i : Fin 3) : FermionType
  /-- The up-type quark singlet of generation `i`, `(3, 1)_{4}`. -/

  /-- The down-type quark singlet of generation `i`, `(3, 1)_{-2}`. -/
  | downSinglet (i : Fin 3) : FermionType

modules.title: The gauge algebra of the Standard Model
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The gauge algebra of the Standard Model is the Lie algebra of
`GaugeGroupI`, which is the direct sum of the Lie algebras of `SU(3)`, `SU(2)` and `U(1)`.
This is a matrix Lie algebra, so the bracket is given by the commutator of matrices.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeAlgebra` : the gauge algebra of the Standard Model: the Lie algebra of `GaugeGroupI`, with
  one factor per gauge group factor — traceless self-adjoint `3 × 3` and `2 × 2` complex matrices
  and a self-adjoint (i
- `toSU3Matrix` : the `su(3)`-factor component of an element of the gauge algebra
- `toSU2Matrix` : the `su(2)`-factor component of an element of the gauge algebra
- `toU1Value` : the `u(1)`-factor component of an element of the gauge algebra

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Basic projections
- B. Constructor from a product of matrices
- C. The Lie algebra instance
- D. The adjoint action of the global gauge group

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The gauge algebra of the Standard Model: the Lie algebra of `GaugeGroupI`, with one
factor per gauge group factor — traceless self-adjoint `3 × 3` and `2 × 2` complex
matrices and a self-adjoint (i.e. real) scalar. This is the constant-coefficient
analogue of `JetGaugeAlgebra`, and the value at the base point of the jets it contains.
declarations.statement: abbrev GaugeAlgebra

declarations.doc:
The self-adjoint scalars form a finite-dimensional real vector space, through the
identification with the corresponding submodule.
declarations.statement: instance : Module.Finite ℝ (selfAdjoint ℂ)
instance : Module.Finite ℝ GaugeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.ext_of_matrix
declarations.statement:

declarations.doc:
The bracket on the gauge algebra: `I` times the matrix commutator on the
`su(3)` and `su(2)` factors, and zero on the (commutative) `u(1)` factor. The
factor of `I` is what makes the bracket of two hermitian matrices hermitian
again; it is also why the bracket is only `ℝ`-bilinear, not `ℂ`-bilinear.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance : Bracket GaugeAlgebra GaugeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.bracket_toSU3Matrix
declarations.statement:
lemma bracket_toSU3Matrix (a b : GaugeAlgebra) :
    ⁅a, b⁆.toSU3Matrix =
      Complex.I • (a.toSU3Matrix * b.toSU3Matrix - b.toSU3Matrix * a.toSU3Matrix)

declarations.statement:

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.bracket_toU1Value
declarations.statement:
lemma bracket_toU1Value (a b : GaugeAlgebra) :
    ⁅a, b⁆.toU1Value = 0

modules.title: The standard basis of the gauge algebra
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The standard basis of the gauge algebra of the Standard Model, indexed by
`Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1`: the eight Gell-Mann matrices on the `su(3)` factor, the three
Pauli matrices on the `su(2)` factor, and `1` on the `u(1)` factor.

In this basis the adjoint action of the gauge group is the block-diagonal matrix
`adjointMatrix`, whose blocks are the trace pairings of the basis elements with their
conjugates; `adjoint_stdBasis` and `toMatrix_adjoint` identify its action with the
adjoint action.

## ii. Key results

- `adjointMatrix`
- `adjoint_stdBasis` : the adjoint action of the gauge group acts on the standard basis through
  `adjointMatrix`
- `toMatrix_adjoint` : the matrix of the adjoint action in the standard basis is `adjointMatrix`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Gell-Mann matrices
- B. Coordinates in the Gell-Mann and Pauli bases
- C. The Gell-Mann basis of the su(3) factor
- D. The Pauli basis of the su(2) factor
- E. The basis of the u(1) factor
- F. The standard basis of the gauge algebra
- G. The adjoint action in the standard basis
- H. Orthogonality of the adjoint matrix

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The Gell-Mann matrices

The Pauli matrices `σ1`, `σ2`, `σ3` embedded along the three coordinate planes of
`Fin 3`, together with the normalised traceless diagonal matrix.

## B. Coordinates in the Gell-Mann and Pauli bases

The coordinates of a traceless hermitian matrix in the Gell-Mann and Pauli bases, read
off from its entries; they coincide with the trace pairings
`2⁻¹ * (trace (T k * M)).re` with the basis matrices.
## C. The Gell-Mann basis of the su(3) factor
## D. The Pauli basis of the su(2) factor
## E. The basis of the u(1) factor
## F. The standard basis of the gauge algebra

## G. The adjoint action in the standard basis

In the standard basis the adjoint action of a gauge group element is the block-diagonal
matrix `adjointMatrix`: the `su(3)` and `su(2)` blocks pair the basis elements with
their conjugates through the trace, and the `u(1)` entry is `1`.

## H. Orthogonality of the adjoint matrix

The adjoint action preserves the trace pairing of the standard basis, so `adjointMatrix`
is an orthogonal matrix. Multiplicativity turns the star of a group element into the
transpose of its matrix, and the two combine to the orthogonality relation.

declarations.name: StandardModel.gellMannMatrix
declarations.doc:
The Gell-Mann matrices: the standard basis of the traceless hermitian `3 × 3`
matrices. The first seven are the Pauli matrices `σ1`, `σ2`, `σ3` embedded along the
three coordinate planes; the eighth is the normalised traceless diagonal matrix.

lemma gellMannMatrix_one :

declarations.name: StandardModel.gellMannMatrix_two

declarations.name: StandardModel.gellMannMatrix_three
declarations.statement: lemma gellMannMatrix_three : gellMannMatrix 3 = !![0, 0, 1; 0, 0, 0; 1, 0, 0]

declarations.statement:
lemma gellMannMatrix_seven :
    gellMannMatrix 7 = (((Real.sqrt 3 : ℝ) : ℂ))⁻¹ • !![1, 0, 0; 0, 1, 0; 0, 0, -2]

declarations.name: StandardModel.gellMannMatrix_selfAdjoint
declarations.doc: The Gell-Mann matrices are hermitian.
declarations.statement:
lemma gellMannMatrix_selfAdjoint (k : Fin 8) :
    star (gellMannMatrix k) = gellMannMatrix k

declarations.name: StandardModel.gellMannMatrix_trace
declarations.doc: The Gell-Mann matrices are traceless.
declarations.statement: lemma gellMannMatrix_trace (k : Fin 8) : (gellMannMatrix k).trace = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.sum_smul_gellMannMatrix
declarations.doc: A combination of the Gell-Mann matrices, entry by entry.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_smul_gellMannMatrix (g : Fin 8 → ℝ) :
    ∑ k, g k • gellMannMatrix k =
      !![((g 2 + (Real.sqrt 3)⁻¹ * g 7 : ℝ) : ℂ),
          ((g 0 : ℝ) : ℂ) - ((g 1 : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I,
          ((g 3 : ℝ) : ℂ) - ((g 4 : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I;
        ((g 0 : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((g 1 : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I,
          ((-g 2 + (Real.sqrt 3)⁻¹ * g 7 : ℝ) : ℂ),
          ((g 5 : ℝ) : ℂ) - ((g 6 : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I;
        ((g 3 : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((g 4 : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I,
          ((g 5 : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((g 6 : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I,
          ((-2 * (Real.sqrt 3)⁻¹ * g 7 : ℝ) : ℂ)]

declarations.name: StandardModel.sum_smul_pauliMatrix_inr
declarations.doc: A combination of the three Pauli matrices `σ1`, `σ2`, `σ3`, entry by entry.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_smul_pauliMatrix_inr (g : Fin 3 → ℝ) :
    ∑ i, g i • pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i) =
      !![((g 2 : ℝ) : ℂ), ((g 0 : ℝ) : ℂ) - ((g 1 : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I;
        ((g 0 : ℝ) : ℂ) + ((g 1 : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I, ((-g 2 : ℝ) : ℂ)]

declarations.name: StandardModel.pauliMatrix_inr_star

declarations.statement:

    star (pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i)) = pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i)

lemma stdBasis_coord_inr_inr_lie (i : Fin 1) (x y : GaugeAlgebra) :
    stdBasis.coord (Sum.inr (Sum.inr i)) ⁅x, y⁆ = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.toSU3Matrix_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma toSU3Matrix_sum {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → GaugeAlgebra) :
    (∑ x ∈ s, f x).toSU3Matrix = ∑ x ∈ s, (f x).toSU3Matrix

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.toSU2Matrix_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma toSU2Matrix_sum {ι : Type*} (s : Finset ι) (f : ι → GaugeAlgebra) :
    (∑ x ∈ s, f x).toSU2Matrix = ∑ x ∈ s, (f x).toSU2Matrix

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.toU1Value_sum

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix
declarations.doc:
The matrix of the adjoint action of a gauge group element in the standard basis:
block diagonal, with the `su(3)` and `su(2)` blocks the trace pairings
`2⁻¹ * (trace (T a * g T b g⁻¹)).re` of the basis elements with the conjugated basis
elements, `1` on the `u(1)` entry, and `0` between different factors.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def adjointMatrix (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    Matrix (Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) (Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) ℝ

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_inl_inl
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_inl_inl (g : GaugeGroupI) (a b : Fin 8) :
    adjointMatrix g (Sum.inl a) (Sum.inl b)
      = 2⁻¹ * (Matrix.trace (gellMannMatrix a *
          (g.toSU3.1 * gellMannMatrix b * star g.toSU3.1))).re

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_inl_inr
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_inl_inr (g : GaugeGroupI) (a : Fin 8) (x : Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) :
    adjointMatrix g (Sum.inl a) (Sum.inr x) = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_inr_inl
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_inr_inl (g : GaugeGroupI) (x : Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) (b : Fin 8) :
    adjointMatrix g (Sum.inr x) (Sum.inl b) = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_inr_inl_inr_inl
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_inr_inl_inr_inl (g : GaugeGroupI) (i j : Fin 3) :
    adjointMatrix g (Sum.inr (Sum.inl i)) (Sum.inr (Sum.inl j))
      = 2⁻¹ * (Matrix.trace (pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i) *
          (g.toSU2.1 * pauliMatrix (Sum.inr j) * star g.toSU2.1))).re

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_inr_inl_inr_inr
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_inr_inl_inr_inr (g : GaugeGroupI) (i : Fin 3) (u : Fin 1) :
    adjointMatrix g (Sum.inr (Sum.inl i)) (Sum.inr (Sum.inr u)) = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_inr_inr_inr_inl
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_inr_inr_inr_inl (g : GaugeGroupI) (u : Fin 1) (j : Fin 3) :
    adjointMatrix g (Sum.inr (Sum.inr u)) (Sum.inr (Sum.inl j)) = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_inr_inr_inr_inr
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_inr_inr_inr_inr (g : GaugeGroupI) (u v : Fin 1) :
    adjointMatrix g (Sum.inr (Sum.inr u)) (Sum.inr (Sum.inr v)) = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjoint_stdBasis
declarations.doc:
The adjoint action of the gauge group acts on the standard basis through
`adjointMatrix`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoint_stdBasis (g : GaugeGroupI) (b : Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) :
    adjoint g (stdBasis b) = ∑ a, adjointMatrix g a b • stdBasis a

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.toMatrix_adjoint
declarations.doc: The matrix of the adjoint action in the standard basis is `adjointMatrix`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toMatrix_adjoint (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    LinearMap.toMatrix stdBasis stdBasis (adjoint g) = adjointMatrix g

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_mulVec_repr
declarations.doc:
The action of `adjointMatrix` on coordinates in the standard basis corresponds to
the adjoint action of the gauge group on the gauge algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_mulVec_repr (g : GaugeGroupI) (a : GaugeAlgebra) :
    (adjointMatrix g).mulVec (stdBasis.repr a) = ⇑(stdBasis.repr (adjoint g a))

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjoint_dualMap_coord
declarations.doc:
The dual adjoint action on the dual standard basis: the coordinate functions
transform through the rows of `adjointMatrix`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoint_dualMap_coord (g : GaugeGroupI) (a : Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) :
    (adjoint g).dualMap (stdBasis.coord a)
      = ∑ b, adjointMatrix g a b • stdBasis.coord b

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_mul
declarations.doc:
The matrix of the adjoint action turns a product in the gauge group into the
product of the corresponding matrices.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_mul (g h : GaugeGroupI) :
    GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix (g * h)
      = GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix g * GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix h

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_one
declarations.doc: The matrix of the adjoint action of the identity is the identity matrix.
declarations.statement: lemma adjointMatrix_one : GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix (1 : GaugeGroupI) = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.gaugeGroup_mul_star_self
declarations.doc: The star of a gauge group element is its inverse.
declarations.statement: lemma gaugeGroup_mul_star_self (g : GaugeGroupI) : g * star g = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_star
declarations.doc:
The matrix of the adjoint action of the star of a gauge group element is the
transpose of the matrix of the adjoint action, since the trace pairing is symmetric
under moving the conjugation from one argument to the other.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_star (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix (star g) = (GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix g)ᵀ

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_mul_transpose
declarations.doc: The matrix of the adjoint action is orthogonal.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_mul_transpose (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix g * (GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix g)ᵀ = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.sum_adjointMatrix_inl_row_mul
declarations.doc:
The rows of the `su(3)` block of the adjoint matrix are orthonormal. The matrix is
block diagonal, so orthogonality of the whole matrix restricts to each block.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_adjointMatrix_inl_row_mul (g : GaugeGroupI) (c d : Fin 8) :
    ∑ a : Fin 8, adjointMatrix g (Sum.inl c) (Sum.inl a) *
      adjointMatrix g (Sum.inl d) (Sum.inl a) = if c = d then 1 else 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.sum_adjointMatrix_inr_inl_row_mul
declarations.doc: The rows of the `su(2)` block of the adjoint matrix are orthonormal.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_adjointMatrix_inr_inl_row_mul (g : GaugeGroupI) (c d : Fin 3) :
    ∑ a : Fin 3, adjointMatrix g (Sum.inr (Sum.inl c)) (Sum.inr (Sum.inl a)) *
      adjointMatrix g (Sum.inr (Sum.inl d)) (Sum.inr (Sum.inl a))
      = if c = d then 1 else 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix_inv_apply
declarations.doc:
The matrix of the adjoint action of the inverse of a gauge group element is the
transpose of the matrix of the adjoint action.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMatrix_inv_apply (g : GaugeGroupI) (a b : Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) :
    adjointMatrix g⁻¹ a b = adjointMatrix g b a

modules.title: The jet gauge algebra
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

We define `JetGaugeAlgebra` as the Lie algebra of `JetGaugeGroupI`,
defined explicitly as traceless self-adjoint matrices, and giving it an instance `LieAlgebra`.
This is a matrix Lie algebra, so the bracket is given by the commutator of matrices.

Note here that `JetGaugeAlgebra` is a module over `ℝ` not `ℂ` or `SpaceTimeAlgebra`.

On this Lie algebra define a preferred basis, `basis`, indexed by
`basisIndex × Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)`.
Here `basisIndex` is the sum `Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1`. The first factor
corresponds to the Gell-Mann matrices which form a basis of `su(3)`,
the second factor corresponds to the Pauli matrices which form a basis of `su(2)`,
and the third factor corresponds to the identity matrix which forms a basis of `u(1)`.

We let `structuralConstant` (typically called `f`) be the structure constants of the Lie algebra
with respect to this preferred basis, so that
```
  [basis i, basis j] = i * ∑ k, structuralConstant i j k • basis k
```

On `JetGaugeAlgebra` we define the adjoint representation of `JetGaugeGroupI`,
`adjointRep`, which acts via `x ↦ g * x * g⁻¹`.

There is also a derivative `deriv : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 → JetLieAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] JetLieAlgebra`
whose action can be defined componentwise in terms of the basis.

The derivative acts on brackets via the Leibniz rule:
```
  deriv μ [x, y] = [deriv μ x, y] + [x, deriv μ y]
```

## ii. Key results

- `JetGaugeAlgebra` : the jet gauge algebra: the Lie-algebra analogue of `JetGaugeGroupI`, with one
  factor per gauge group factor — traceless self-adjoint `3 × 3` and `2 × 2` matrices and a
  self-adjoint scalar, all with coefficients in the ring `SpaceTimeAlgebra` of formal power series
  in the spacetime coordinates

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Basic projections
- B. Constructor from a product of matrices
- C. The Lie algebra instance
- D. The derivative on the jet gauge algebra
- E. Multiplication by the coordinates
- F. The iterated derivative
- G. Taylor coefficients and evaluation at the base point
- H. The basis
- I. The adjoint representation of Jet Gauge group

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The jet gauge algebra: the Lie-algebra analogue of `JetGaugeGroupI`, with one factor per gauge
group factor — traceless self-adjoint `3 × 3` and `2 × 2` matrices and a self-adjoint scalar, all
with coefficients in the ring `SpaceTimeAlgebra` of formal power series in the spacetime
coordinates. The Maurer–Cartan forms of the jet gauge group are valued here, hermiticity being
`star_maurerCartanSU3` and its companions.
declarations.statement: abbrev JetGaugeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.ofMatrixProd
declarations.doc:
A jet of the gauge algebra from a triple of matrices of jets: the `SU(3)` and `SU(2)`
components self-adjoint and traceless, the `U(1)` component self-adjoint.
declarations.statement:
def ofMatrixProd (A : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) SpaceTimeAlgebra ×
    Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) SpaceTimeAlgebra × SpaceTimeAlgebra)
        (hA : star A.1 = A.1 ∧ A.1.trace = 0)
    (hB : star A.2.1 = A.2.1 ∧ A.2.1.trace = 0) (hC : star A.2.2 = A.2.2) : JetGaugeAlgebra

declarations.statement:
lemma ofMatrixProd_toSU3Matrix (A : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) SpaceTimeAlgebra ×
    Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) SpaceTimeAlgebra × SpaceTimeAlgebra)
        (hA : star A.1 = A.1 ∧ A.1.trace = 0)
    (hB : star A.2.1 = A.2.1 ∧ A.2.1.trace = 0) (hC : star A.2.2 = A.2.2) :
    (ofMatrixProd A hA hB hC).toSU3Matrix = A.1

lemma ofMatrixProd_toSU2Matrix (A : Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) SpaceTimeAlgebra ×

    (hB : star A.2.1 = A.2.1 ∧ A.2.1.trace = 0) (hC : star A.2.2 = A.2.2) :
    (ofMatrixProd A hA hB hC).toSU2Matrix = A.2.1

    (ofMatrixProd A hA hB hC).toU1Value = A.2.2

lemma sub_toSU3Matrix (a b : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    (a - b).toSU3Matrix = a.toSU3Matrix - b.toSU3Matrix
