declarations.doc:
The bracket on the jet gauge algebra: `I` times the matrix commutator on the
`su(3)` and `su(2)` factors, and zero on the (commutative) `u(1)` factor. The
factor of `I` is what makes the bracket of two hermitian matrices hermitian
again; it is also why the bracket is only `ℝ`-bilinear, not `ℂ`-bilinear.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance : Bracket JetGaugeAlgebra JetGaugeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.bracket_toSU3Matrix
declarations.statement:
lemma bracket_toSU3Matrix (a b : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    ⁅a, b⁆.toSU3Matrix =
      Complex.I • (a.toSU3Matrix * b.toSU3Matrix - b.toSU3Matrix * a.toSU3Matrix)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.bracket_toSU2Matrix
declarations.statement:
lemma bracket_toSU2Matrix (a b : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    ⁅a, b⁆.toSU2Matrix =
      Complex.I • (a.toSU2Matrix * b.toSU2Matrix - b.toSU2Matrix * a.toSU2Matrix)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.bracket_toU1Value
declarations.statement:
lemma bracket_toU1Value (a b : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    ⁅a, b⁆.toU1Value = 0
noncomputable instance : LieRing JetGaugeAlgebra
noncomputable instance : LieAlgebra ℝ JetGaugeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.deriv
declarations.doc:
The formal derivative in the direction `μ` on the jet gauge algebra, acting
entrywise on each factor. It preserves hermiticity since `star` commutes with
`pderiv`, and tracelessness since the trace of the entrywise derivative is the
derivative of the trace.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def deriv (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : JetGaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] JetGaugeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.deriv_toSU3Matrix
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_toSU3Matrix (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    (deriv μ a).toSU3Matrix = a.toSU3Matrix.map (pderiv μ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.deriv_toSU2Matrix
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_toSU2Matrix (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    (deriv μ a).toSU2Matrix = a.toSU2Matrix.map (pderiv μ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.deriv_toU1Value
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_toU1Value (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    (deriv μ a).toU1Value = pderiv μ a.toU1Value

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.coord
declarations.doc:
Multiplication by the spacetime coordinate `x_μ`, entrywise on each factor. It
preserves hermiticity since the coordinates are self-adjoint, and tracelessness since
it is a scalar.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def coord (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : JetGaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] JetGaugeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.coord_toSU3Matrix
declarations.statement:
lemma coord_toSU3Matrix (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    (coord μ a).toSU3Matrix = (X μ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) • a.toSU3Matrix

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.coord_toSU2Matrix
declarations.statement:
lemma coord_toSU2Matrix (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    (coord μ a).toSU2Matrix = (X μ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) • a.toSU2Matrix

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.coord_toU1Value
declarations.statement:
lemma coord_toU1Value (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    (coord μ a).toU1Value = (X μ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) * a.toU1Value

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.deriv_coord
declarations.doc: The Leibniz rule for a coordinate: `∂_μ (x_ν a) = x_ν ∂_μ a + δ_{μν} a`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_coord (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    deriv μ (coord ν a) = coord ν (deriv μ a) + if μ = ν then a else 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.coord_lie
declarations.doc: The coordinates are central for the bracket.
declarations.statement:
lemma coord_lie (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a b : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    ⁅coord μ a, b⁆ = coord μ ⁅a, b⁆

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.deriv_comm
declarations.doc: Formal derivatives on the jet gauge algebra commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_comm (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    deriv μ (deriv ν a) = deriv ν (deriv μ a)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.deriv_bracket
declarations.doc:
The derivative is a derivation of the bracket: the Leibniz rule
`deriv μ ⁅x, y⁆ = ⁅deriv μ x, y⁆ + ⁅x, deriv μ y⁆`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_bracket (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x y : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    deriv μ ⁅x, y⁆ = ⁅deriv μ x, y⁆ + ⁅x, deriv μ y⁆

declarations.doc:
Post-composition with `deriv` is right-commutative, since formal derivatives
commute (`deriv_comm`). This is what allows iterated derivatives to be indexed by a
`Multiset` of directions.
declarations.statement:
instance : RightCommutative
    (fun (D : JetGaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] JetGaugeAlgebra) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) => D.comp (deriv μ))

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.iteratedDeriv
declarations.doc:
The iterated formal derivative on the jet gauge algebra, in the (unordered, since
derivatives commute) directions given by the multiset `μs`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def iteratedDeriv (μs : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    JetGaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] JetGaugeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.iteratedDeriv_zero
declarations.statement: lemma iteratedDeriv_zero : iteratedDeriv 0 = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.iteratedDeriv_cons
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDeriv_cons (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μs : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    iteratedDeriv (μ ::ₘ μs) = (deriv μ).comp (iteratedDeriv μs)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.iteratedDeriv_add
declarations.doc:
The iterated derivative is additive in the multiset of directions: deriving
along `s + t` is deriving along `t` and then along `s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDeriv_add (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    iteratedDeriv (s + t) = (iteratedDeriv s).comp (iteratedDeriv t)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.iteratedDeriv_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDeriv_singleton (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    iteratedDeriv ({μ} : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) = deriv μ

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.iteratedDeriv_toSU3Matrix
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDeriv_toSU3Matrix (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    (iteratedDeriv s a).toSU3Matrix =
      a.toSU3Matrix.map fun f => SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv s f

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.iteratedDeriv_toSU2Matrix
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDeriv_toSU2Matrix (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    (iteratedDeriv s a).toSU2Matrix =
      a.toSU2Matrix.map fun f => SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv s f

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.iteratedDeriv_toU1Value
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDeriv_toU1Value (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    (iteratedDeriv s a).toU1Value = SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv s a.toU1Value

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.taylorCoeff
declarations.doc:
The Taylor coefficient of an element of the jet gauge algebra at the monomial
given by the multiset `r` of spacetime directions, taken entrywise, as an
`ℝ`-linear map to the constant gauge algebra `GaugeAlgebra`.

For `r ≠ 0` this is only linear: the coefficient of a product is a convolution of
coefficients, so it does not respect the bracket. The zeroth coefficient does; see
`eval` for that morphism of Lie algebras.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def taylorCoeff (r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    JetGaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] GaugeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.taylorCoeff_toSU3Matrix
declarations.statement:
lemma taylorCoeff_toSU3Matrix (r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    (taylorCoeff r a).toSU3Matrix = a.toSU3Matrix.map (coeff r.toFinsupp)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.taylorCoeff_toSU2Matrix
declarations.statement:
lemma taylorCoeff_toSU2Matrix (r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    (taylorCoeff r a).toSU2Matrix = a.toSU2Matrix.map (coeff r.toFinsupp)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.taylorCoeff_toU1Value
declarations.statement:
lemma taylorCoeff_toU1Value (r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    (taylorCoeff r a).toU1Value = coeff r.toFinsupp a.toU1Value

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.taylorCoeff_zero_bracket
declarations.doc:
The zeroth Taylor coefficient respects the bracket, since the constant coefficient
of a product of jets is the product of the constant coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma taylorCoeff_zero_bracket (a b : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    taylorCoeff 0 ⁅a, b⁆ = ⁅taylorCoeff 0 a, taylorCoeff 0 b⁆

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.eval
declarations.doc:
Evaluation of the jet gauge algebra at the base point: the zeroth Taylor
coefficient, as a morphism of Lie algebras.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def eval : JetGaugeAlgebra →ₗ⁅ℝ⁆ GaugeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.ofConstant
declarations.doc:
The inclusion of the constant gauge algebra into the jet gauge algebra: the jets
with no spacetime dependence, given entrywise by the constant power series. This is
a section of `eval`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def ofConstant : GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] JetGaugeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.ofConstant_toSU3Matrix
declarations.statement:
lemma ofConstant_toSU3Matrix (a : GaugeAlgebra) :
    (ofConstant a).toSU3Matrix = a.toSU3Matrix.map (C : ℂ → SpaceTimeAlgebra)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.ofConstant_toSU2Matrix
declarations.statement:
lemma ofConstant_toSU2Matrix (a : GaugeAlgebra) :
    (ofConstant a).toSU2Matrix = a.toSU2Matrix.map (C : ℂ → SpaceTimeAlgebra)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.ofConstant_toU1Value
declarations.statement:
lemma ofConstant_toU1Value (a : GaugeAlgebra) :
    (ofConstant a).toU1Value = C a.toU1Value

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.eval_apply
declarations.statement: lemma eval_apply (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) : eval a = taylorCoeff 0 a

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.eval_ofConstant
declarations.statement: lemma eval_ofConstant (a : GaugeAlgebra) : eval (ofConstant a) = a

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.eval_toSU3Matrix_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma eval_toSU3Matrix_apply (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) (i j : Fin 3) :
    (eval a).toSU3Matrix i j = constantCoeff (a.toSU3Matrix i j)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.eval_toSU2Matrix_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma eval_toSU2Matrix_apply (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) (i j : Fin 2) :
    (eval a).toSU2Matrix i j = constantCoeff (a.toSU2Matrix i j)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.eval_toU1Value_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma eval_toU1Value_eq (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    (eval a).toU1Value = constantCoeff a.toU1Value

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.eval_coord
declarations.doc: A coordinate multiple vanishes at the base point.
declarations.statement: lemma eval_coord (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) : eval (coord μ a) = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.eval_iteratedDeriv_toSU3Matrix
declarations.doc: The `su(3)` component of the base-point Taylor coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma eval_iteratedDeriv_toSU3Matrix (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    (eval (iteratedDeriv x a)).toSU3Matrix
      = a.toSU3Matrix.map fun f => constantCoeff (SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv x f)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.eval_iteratedDeriv_toSU2Matrix
declarations.doc: The `su(2)` component of the base-point Taylor coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma eval_iteratedDeriv_toSU2Matrix (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    (eval (iteratedDeriv x a)).toSU2Matrix
      = a.toSU2Matrix.map fun f => constantCoeff (SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv x f)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.eval_iteratedDeriv_toU1Value
declarations.doc: The `u(1)` component of the base-point Taylor coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma eval_iteratedDeriv_toU1Value (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    (eval (iteratedDeriv x a)).toU1Value
      = constantCoeff (SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv x a.toU1Value)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.ext_of_eval_iteratedDeriv
declarations.doc:
Taylor determinacy: a jet gauge algebra element is determined by the base-point
values of its iterated derivatives.
declarations.statement:
lemma ext_of_eval_iteratedDeriv {x y : JetGaugeAlgebra}
    (h : ∀ s, eval (iteratedDeriv s x) = eval (iteratedDeriv s y)) : x = y

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.adjointMap
declarations.doc:
The adjoint action of an element `U` of the jet gauge group on the jet gauge algebra,
acting on the `su(3)` and `su(2)` factors by `a ↦ U a U⁻¹`, with `U⁻¹ = star U` by
unitarity, and trivially on the `u(1)` factor since `SpaceTimeAlgebra` is commutative.
Hermiticity is preserved since `star (U a (star U)) = U (star a) (star U)`, and
tracelessness since the trace is invariant under conjugation.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def adjointMap (U : JetGaugeGroupI) : JetGaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] JetGaugeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.adjointMap_toSU3Matrix
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMap_toSU3Matrix (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    (adjointMap U a).toSU3Matrix = U.1.1 * a.toSU3Matrix * star U.1.1

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.adjointMap_toSU2Matrix
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMap_toSU2Matrix (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    (adjointMap U a).toSU2Matrix = U.2.1.1 * a.toSU2Matrix * star U.2.1.1

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.adjointMap_toU1Value
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMap_toU1Value (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (a : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    (adjointMap U a).toU1Value = a.toU1Value

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.adjoint
declarations.doc:
The adjoint representation of the jet gauge group on the jet gauge algebra,
`U ↦ (a ↦ U a U⁻¹)` factorwise.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def adjoint : Representation ℝ JetGaugeGroupI JetGaugeAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.eval_adjointMap
declarations.doc:
At the base point the adjoint action of a gauge jet is the adjoint action of its
value: the constant coefficient of `U x U†` is `U₀ x₀ U₀†`.
declarations.statement:
lemma eval_adjointMap (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (x : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    eval (adjointMap U x) = GaugeAlgebra.adjoint U.eval (eval x)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.ofConstant_lie
declarations.doc:
The constant inclusion is a morphism of Lie algebras: constants bracket to
constants.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofConstant_lie (a b : GaugeAlgebra) :
    ofConstant ⁅a, b⁆ = ⁅ofConstant a, ofConstant b⁆

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetGaugeAlgebra.adjointMap_lie
declarations.doc:
The adjoint action preserves the bracket: conjugation is an automorphism of the
Lie algebra, using unitarity to cancel the inner `U† U` factors.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMap_lie (U : JetGaugeGroupI) (x y : JetGaugeAlgebra) :
    adjointMap U ⁅x, y⁆ = ⁅adjointMap U x, adjointMap U y⁆

modules.title: The root decomposition of the gauge algebra
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The gauge torus acts on the gauge algebra by conjugation with a diagonal matrix, so it
scales the matrix entry `(j, k)` of the `su(3)` and `su(2)` blocks by `d j * star (d k)`.
Off the diagonal this makes the real and imaginary parts of an entry a rotating pair —
the root directions, recorded by `rootIdx`, `rootEntry` and `rootWeight` — while the
diagonal directions and the `u(1)` generator are fixed, and are recorded by `cartanIdx`,
which is assembled from the Cartan indices `su3CartanId` and `su2CartanId` of the
individual factors.

This is the adjoint analogue of the weights carried by the matter representations, and
is what the gauge sector's gauge weight decomposition is built from.

Section E makes that last sentence a theorem. A gauge weight is a character of the torus,
so the real Lie algebra carries no gauge weight decomposition of its own; but for any
complex algebra receiving the dual adjoint action, `adjointDecomposition` decomposes the
span of the resulting symbols, and its pieces are a single root line at each of the eight
nonzero weights and the span of the four Cartan symbols at weight zero. That is the sense
in which the root decomposition and the gauge weight decomposition of the adjoint are the
same thing.

## ii. Key results

- `rootIdx` : the four root directions of the adjoint
- `rootWeight` : the gauge weight of each root direction
- `rootEntry` : the matrix entry scaled by the torus along each root direction
- `su3CartanId` : the Gell-Mann indices of the two Cartan directions of `su(3)`
- `su2CartanId` : the Pauli index of the Cartan direction of `su(2)`
- `cartanIdx` : the four weight-zero directions: the two `su(3)` Cartan generators, the `su(2)`
  Cartan generator and the `u(1)` generator
- `adjointDecomposition` : the root decomposition read as a gauge weight decomposition: the span of
  the symbols of a coadjoint map, joined out of the twelve root and Cartan lines

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The coordinates of the standard basis
- B. The torus acts by conjugation with a diagonal matrix
- C. An entrywise scaling rotates the real pair of coordinate functionals
- D. The root and Cartan directions of the adjoint
- E. The root decomposition as a gauge weight decomposition
- F. The weight coordinates of one factor

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The coordinates of the standard basis
## B. The torus acts by conjugation with a diagonal matrix
## C. An entrywise scaling rotates the real pair of coordinate functionals

## D. The root and Cartan directions of the adjoint

The `su(3)` and `su(2)` blocks each contribute root directions — pairs of standard
basis indices whose coordinate functionals are the real part and minus the imaginary
part of one matrix entry — together with Cartan directions on which the torus acts
trivially; the `u(1)` generator is also fixed.

The Cartan directions are named one factor at a time first, by `su3CartanId` in the
Gell-Mann indices and `su2CartanId` in the Pauli indices, and `cartanIdx` assembles those
with the `u(1)` generator into the four weight-zero directions of the whole algebra. The
factorwise names are the ones section F uses; they are reducible, so they behave exactly
like the index literals they name.

## E. The root decomposition as a gauge weight decomposition

A gauge weight is a character of the torus, so the vectors carrying one are complex,
whereas the gauge algebra is a real Lie algebra and `GaugeWeightDecomposition` asks for a
complex algebra. The relation is therefore not a statement about `GaugeAlgebra`, which
carries no gauge weight decomposition at all, but about any complex algebra receiving the
dual adjoint action: a real-linear map `F` out of `Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra`
intertwining the gauge action with the coadjoint one, which is how the field strength of
the gauge sector meets the adjoint.

For such an `F` the root data of section D is exactly a gauge weight decomposition of the
span of the symbols. Each root contributes the two combinations `F φ₁ ± i F φ₂` of its
paired coordinate symbols, of weights `± rootWeight r`, and each Cartan direction
contributes its symbol, of weight zero; `exists_rootIdx_or_cartanIdx` says these twelve
vectors are enough, and `adjointDecomposition` joins their lines one weight at a time.

The pieces are the identification itself. `adjointDecomposition_piece_rootWeight` and
`adjointDecomposition_piece_neg_rootWeight` give a single root line at each of the eight
nonzero weights, and `adjointDecomposition_piece_zero` gives the span of the four Cartan
symbols at weight zero: the root directions are the nonzero-weight pieces and the Cartan
directions are the zero-weight piece.

Section F gives the Gell-Mann and Pauli coordinates of the vectors `adjVec` that belong to one
non-abelian factor.

## F. The weight coordinates of one factor

The vectors `adjVec` that belong to the `su(3)` or the `su(2)` factor have Gell-Mann or Pauli
coordinates `x₁ ± i x₂` on a root pair, and the Cartan coordinate itself on a Cartan
direction. `su3WeightCoeff` and `su2WeightCoeff` record these coordinates, indexed by
`su3WeightIdx` and `su2WeightIdx`. The lemmas `rootIdx_castSucc`, `cartanIdx_castSucc`,
`rootIdx_three` and `cartanIdx_two` identify the root pairs and Cartan indices of one factor
with those of the whole algebra.

declarations.name: StandardModel.star_expI_zpow
declarations.doc: Conjugation inverts a power of `expI`.
declarations.statement: lemma star_expI_zpow (z : ℤ) : star ((expI : ℂ) ^ z) = (expI : ℂ) ^ (-z)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.stdCoeff
declarations.doc: coords
declarations.statement: noncomputable def stdCoeff (x : GaugeAlgebra) : Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1 → ℝ

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.eq_sum_stdCoeff
declarations.statement: lemma eq_sum_stdCoeff (x : GaugeAlgebra) : x = ∑ y, stdCoeff x y • stdBasis y

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.stdBasis_coord_apply
declarations.doc:
The coordinate functionals of `stdBasis` read off a gauge-algebra element's matrix
entries.
declarations.statement:
lemma stdBasis_coord_apply (y : GaugeAlgebra) (a : Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) :
    stdBasis.coord a y = stdCoeff y a

declarations.name: StandardModel.torusSU3Diag
declarations.doc: su3 diagonals of inverse torus gens
declarations.statement: noncomputable def torusSU3Diag : Fin 4 → Fin 3 → ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.torusSU2Diag
declarations.doc: su2
declarations.statement: noncomputable def torusSU2Diag : Fin 4 → Fin 2 → ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.toSU3_inv_gaugeTorusGen
declarations.statement:
lemma toSU3_inv_gaugeTorusGen (i : Fin 4) :
    ((GaugeGroupI.toSU3 (gaugeTorusGen i)⁻¹ : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) :
      Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ) = Matrix.diagonal (torusSU3Diag i)

declarations.name: StandardModel.toSU2_inv_gaugeTorusGen
declarations.statement:
lemma toSU2_inv_gaugeTorusGen (i : Fin 4) :
    ((GaugeGroupI.toSU2 (gaugeTorusGen i)⁻¹ : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) :
      Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) = Matrix.diagonal (torusSU2Diag i)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMap_toSU3Matrix_apply_diagonal
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMap_toSU3Matrix_apply_diagonal {g : GaugeGroupI} {d : Fin 3 → ℂ}
    (hg : ((GaugeGroupI.toSU3 g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) :
      Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℂ) = Matrix.diagonal d)
    (x : GaugeAlgebra) (j k : Fin 3) :
    (adjointMap g x).toSU3Matrix j k = d j * star (d k) * x.toSU3Matrix j k

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointMap_toSU2Matrix_apply_diagonal
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointMap_toSU2Matrix_apply_diagonal {g : GaugeGroupI} {d : Fin 2 → ℂ}
    (hg : ((GaugeGroupI.toSU2 g : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) :
      Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) = Matrix.diagonal d)
    (x : GaugeAlgebra) (j k : Fin 2) :
    (adjointMap g x).toSU2Matrix j k = d j * star (d k) * x.toSU2Matrix j k

declarations.name: StandardModel.torusSU3Diag_mul_star
declarations.statement:
lemma torusSU3Diag_mul_star (i : Fin 4) (j : Fin 3) :
    torusSU3Diag i j * star (torusSU3Diag i j) = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.torusSU2Diag_mul_star
declarations.statement:
lemma torusSU2Diag_mul_star (i : Fin 4) (j : Fin 2) :
    torusSU2Diag i j * star (torusSU2Diag i j) = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.coord_rootIdx_fst
declarations.statement:
lemma coord_rootIdx_fst (r : Fin 4) (x : GaugeAlgebra) :
    stdBasis.coord (rootIdx r).1 x = (rootEntry r x).re

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.coord_rootIdx_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma coord_rootIdx_snd (r : Fin 4) (x : GaugeAlgebra) :
    stdBasis.coord (rootIdx r).2 x = -(rootEntry r x).im

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.rootEntry_adjointMap
declarations.statement:
lemma rootEntry_adjointMap (r : Fin 4) (i : Fin 4) (x : GaugeAlgebra) :
    rootEntry r (adjointMap (gaugeTorusGen i)⁻¹ x)
      = star ((expI : ℂ) ^ GaugeWeight.coord (rootWeight r) i) * rootEntry r x

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.dualMap_coord_cartanIdx
declarations.statement:
lemma dualMap_coord_cartanIdx (c : Fin 4) (i : Fin 4) :
    (adjointMap (gaugeTorusGen i)⁻¹).dualMap (stdBasis.coord (cartanIdx c))
      = stdBasis.coord (cartanIdx c)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.real_smul_eq_complex_smul
declarations.doc: A real scalar acts on a complex algebra through its complex image.
declarations.statement: lemma real_smul_eq_complex_smul (r : ℝ) (b : B) : r • b = ((r : ℂ)) • b

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.IsCoadjointSymbol
declarations.doc:
A coadjoint symbol map: a real-linear map from the dual of the gauge algebra into a
complex algebra which intertwines the gauge action with the dual adjoint action. The
field strength of the gauge sector is one such map.
declarations.statement:
def IsCoadjointSymbol (rep : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI B)
    (F : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) : Prop

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.AdjIdx
declarations.doc:
The index type of the adjoint weight vectors: four positive roots, four negative
roots and four Cartan directions.
declarations.statement: abbrev AdjIdx : Type

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjWeight
declarations.doc: The gauge weight carried by each adjoint weight vector.
declarations.statement: def adjWeight : AdjIdx → GaugeWeight

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjVec
declarations.doc:
The weight vectors of the adjoint in the image of a coadjoint symbol map: for each
root the two combinations of its paired coordinate symbols, and for each Cartan
direction the symbol itself.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def adjVec (F : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) : AdjIdx → B

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjWeight_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc:
A weight vector carries zero gauge weight exactly when it is a Cartan direction; the
eight root directions all carry a nonzero weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjWeight_eq_zero_iff (k : AdjIdx) :
    adjWeight k = 0 ↔ ∃ c : Fin 4, k = Sum.inr (Sum.inr c)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.exists_rootIdx_or_cartanIdx
declarations.doc:
The root and Cartan directions exhaust the standard basis: every standard index is
one of the two members of a root pair, or a Cartan index.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_rootIdx_or_cartanIdx (a : Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1) :
    (∃ r : Fin 4, a = (rootIdx r).1) ∨ (∃ r : Fin 4, a = (rootIdx r).2)
      ∨ ∃ c : Fin 4, a = cartanIdx c

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.rep_pair_add
declarations.doc: The positive combination of a rotating pair of symbols is scaled by the rotation.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_pair_add (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F) (g : GaugeGroupI)
    (φ₁ φ₂ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) (z : ℂ)
    (h1 : (adjointMap g⁻¹).dualMap φ₁ = z.re • φ₁ - z.im • φ₂)
    (h2 : (adjointMap g⁻¹).dualMap φ₂ = z.im • φ₁ + z.re • φ₂) :
    rep g (F φ₁ + Complex.I • F φ₂) = z • (F φ₁ + Complex.I • F φ₂)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.rep_pair_sub
declarations.doc:
The negative combination of a rotating pair of symbols is scaled by the conjugate
rotation.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_pair_sub (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F) (g : GaugeGroupI)
    (φ₁ φ₂ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) (z : ℂ)
    (h1 : (adjointMap g⁻¹).dualMap φ₁ = z.re • φ₁ - z.im • φ₂)
    (h2 : (adjointMap g⁻¹).dualMap φ₂ = z.im • φ₁ + z.re • φ₂) :
    rep g (F φ₁ - Complex.I • F φ₂)
      = (starRingEnd ℂ z) • (F φ₁ - Complex.I • F φ₂)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.rep_fixed
declarations.doc: A symbol at a fixed coordinate functional is itself fixed.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_fixed (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F) (g : GaugeGroupI)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) (h1 : (adjointMap g⁻¹).dualMap φ = φ) :
    rep g (F φ) = F φ

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.rep_adjVec
declarations.doc:
Each adjoint weight vector is a simultaneous eigenvector of the four torus
generators, at the character of its weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_adjVec (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F) (k : AdjIdx) (i : Fin 4) :
    rep (gaugeTorusGen i) (adjVec F k)
      = ((expI : ℂ) ^ GaugeWeight.coord (adjWeight k) i) • adjVec F k

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.symbol_rootIdx_fst
declarations.doc: The first symbol of a root pair, recovered from the two weight vectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma symbol_rootIdx_fst (F : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) (r : Fin 4) :
    F (stdBasis.coord (rootIdx r).1)
      = (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ • (adjVec F (Sum.inl r) + adjVec F (Sum.inr (Sum.inl r)))

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.symbol_rootIdx_snd
declarations.doc: The second symbol of a root pair, recovered from the two weight vectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma symbol_rootIdx_snd (F : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) (r : Fin 4) :
    F (stdBasis.coord (rootIdx r).2)
      = (-(Complex.I / 2)) • (adjVec F (Sum.inl r) - adjVec F (Sum.inr (Sum.inl r)))

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.symbol_mem_iSup
declarations.doc: Every standard coordinate symbol lies in the join of the twelve weight lines.

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.span_range_eq_iSup
declarations.doc: The span of the symbols is the join of the twelve weight lines.
declarations.statement:
lemma span_range_eq_iSup (F : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range F) = ⨆ k : AdjIdx, Submodule.span ℂ {adjVec F k}

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointDecomposition
declarations.doc:
The root decomposition read as a gauge weight decomposition: the span of the symbols
of a coadjoint map, joined out of the twelve root and Cartan lines.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def adjointDecomposition (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F) :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition rep (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range F))

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointDecomposition_supp
declarations.doc:
The gauge weights of the adjoint: the six `su(3)` roots, the two `su(2)` roots and
the zero weight of the Cartan and `u(1)` directions. Every one of them has vanishing
hypercharge.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDecomposition_supp (hmul : IsMulRep rep) (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F) :
    (adjointDecomposition hmul hF).supp
      = {((2, -1, 0, 0) : GaugeWeight), (1, 1, 0, 0), (-1, 2, 0, 0), (0, 0, 2, 0),
        (-2, 1, 0, 0), (-1, -1, 0, 0), (1, -2, 0, 0), (0, 0, -2, 0), (0, 0, 0, 0)}

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointDecomposition_piece
declarations.doc:
The pieces of the decomposition: the weight-`w` piece is the join of the weight lines
whose weight is `w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDecomposition_piece (hmul : IsMulRep rep) (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F)
    (w : GaugeWeight) :
    (adjointDecomposition hmul hF).piece w
      = ⨆ k : AdjIdx, if w = adjWeight k then Submodule.span ℂ {adjVec F k} else ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointDecomposition_piece_rootWeight
declarations.doc: The piece at a root weight is the line of that root alone.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDecomposition_piece_rootWeight (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F) (r : Fin 4) :
    (adjointDecomposition hmul hF).piece (rootWeight r)
      = Submodule.span ℂ {adjVec F (Sum.inl r)}

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointDecomposition_piece_neg_rootWeight
declarations.doc: The piece at the opposite of a root weight is the line of the opposite root.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDecomposition_piece_neg_rootWeight (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F) (r : Fin 4) :
    (adjointDecomposition hmul hF).piece (-(rootWeight r))
      = Submodule.span ℂ {adjVec F (Sum.inr (Sum.inl r))}

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointDecomposition_piece_zero
declarations.doc:
The weight-zero piece is the span of the four Cartan symbols: the two `su(3)` Cartan
generators, the `su(2)` Cartan generator and the `u(1)` generator.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDecomposition_piece_zero (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F) :
    (adjointDecomposition hmul hF).piece 0
      = ⨆ c : Fin 4, Submodule.span ℂ {F (stdBasis.coord (cartanIdx c))}

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.adjointDecomposition_piece_eq_bot
declarations.doc: Every weight outside the nine is absent from the adjoint.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDecomposition_piece_eq_bot (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (hF : IsCoadjointSymbol rep F) {w : GaugeWeight}
    (hw : w ∉ (adjointDecomposition hmul hF).supp) :
    (adjointDecomposition hmul hF).piece w = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.su3WeightIdx
declarations.doc:

roots and two Cartan directions.

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.rootIdx_castSucc
declarations.doc: The `su(3)` root pairs are the first three root pairs of the whole gauge algebra.
declarations.statement:

    rootIdx r.castSucc = (Sum.inl (su3RootPair r).1, Sum.inl (su3RootPair r).2)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.cartanIdx_castSucc

The `su(3)` Cartan indices are the first two Cartan indices of the whole gauge
algebra.
declarations.statement:

    cartanIdx c.castSucc.castSucc = Sum.inl (su3CartanId c)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.su3WeightCoeff

and the Cartan coordinates themselves.

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.su2WeightIdx

and the Cartan direction.
declarations.statement: abbrev su2WeightIdx : Type

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.su2RootPair

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.rootIdx_three
declarations.doc: The `su(2)` root pair is the fourth root pair of the whole gauge algebra.
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.cartanIdx_two

declarations.statement: lemma cartanIdx_two : cartanIdx 2 = Sum.inr (Sum.inl su2CartanId)

The `su(2)` weight coordinates in Pauli coordinates: `x₁ ± i x₂` on the root pair, and

modules.title: The adjoint matrices of `SU(2)` and `SU(3)`
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

`su2AdjointMatrix U` and `su3AdjointMatrix U` are the real matrices of `X ↦ U X U⁻¹` on
`su(2)` and `su(3)` in the Pauli and Gell-Mann bases, read off with the trace pairing
`(X, Y) ↦ ½ tr (X Y)`. They are the `su(2)` and `su(3)` blocks of `GaugeAlgebra.adjointMatrix`,
which gives their orthonormal rows and their transposition at `U⁻¹`.

## ii. Key results

- `su2AdjointMatrix` : the adjoint matrix of an element of `SU(2)`: the trace pairing of the Pauli
  basis of `su(2)` with the Pauli basis conjugated by that element
- `su2AdjointMatrix_apply` : the entries of the adjoint matrix
- `sum_su2AdjointMatrix_row_mul` : the rows of the adjoint matrix are orthonormal
- `su2AdjointMatrix_inv` : the adjoint matrix of the inverse is the transpose

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The adjoint matrix of `SU(2)`
- B. The adjoint matrix of `SU(3)`

## iv. References

* None.

## B. The adjoint matrix of `SU(3)`

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2AdjointMatrix
declarations.doc:
The adjoint matrix of an element of `SU(2)`: the trace pairing of the Pauli basis of
`su(2)` with the Pauli basis conjugated by that element.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def su2AdjointMatrix (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) :
    Matrix (Fin 3) (Fin 3) ℝ

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2AdjointMatrix_apply
declarations.doc: The entries of the adjoint matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma su2AdjointMatrix_apply (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) (i j : Fin 3) :
    su2AdjointMatrix U i j
      = 2⁻¹ * (Matrix.trace (pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i) *
          (U.1 * pauliMatrix (Sum.inr j) * star U.1))).re

declarations.name: StandardModel.sum_su2AdjointMatrix_row_mul
declarations.doc: The rows of the adjoint matrix are orthonormal.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_su2AdjointMatrix_row_mul (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) (c d : Fin 3) :
    ∑ a : Fin 3, su2AdjointMatrix U c a * su2AdjointMatrix U d a
      = if c = d then 1 else 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2AdjointMatrix_inv
declarations.doc: The adjoint matrix of the inverse is the transpose.
declarations.statement:
lemma su2AdjointMatrix_inv (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ) (a b : Fin 3) :
    su2AdjointMatrix U⁻¹ a b = su2AdjointMatrix U b a

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3AdjointMatrix
declarations.doc:
The adjoint matrix of `U ∈ SU(3)`: the trace pairing of the Gell-Mann basis with the
Gell-Mann basis conjugated by `U`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def su3AdjointMatrix (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) :
    Matrix (Fin 8) (Fin 8) ℝ

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3AdjointMatrix_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma su3AdjointMatrix_apply (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) (i j : Fin 8) :
    su3AdjointMatrix U i j
      = 2⁻¹ * (Matrix.trace (gellMannMatrix i * (U.1 * gellMannMatrix j * star U.1))).re

declarations.name: StandardModel.sum_su3AdjointMatrix_row_mul
declarations.doc: The rows of the adjoint matrix are orthonormal.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_su3AdjointMatrix_row_mul (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) (c d : Fin 8) :
    ∑ a : Fin 8, su3AdjointMatrix U c a * su3AdjointMatrix U d a
      = if c = d then 1 else 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3AdjointMatrix_inv
declarations.doc: The adjoint matrix of the inverse is the transpose.
declarations.statement:
lemma su3AdjointMatrix_inv (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) (a b : Fin 8) :
    su3AdjointMatrix U⁻¹ a b = su3AdjointMatrix U b a

modules.title: A primitive cube root of unity
modules.doc:
The root of unity `ω = exp (2 π i / 3)`, which both non-abelian factors of the gauge group see.

## i. Overview

`Physlib.Particles.StandardModel.GaugeGroup.Basic` carries the gauge group `GaugeGroupI` of
the Standard Model and its discrete quotients. One scalar recurs throughout the structure of its
non-abelian factors: the primitive cube root of unity `ω = exp (2 π i / 3)`. The element
`ω • 1` generates the centre of `SU(3)`, the cyclic colour permutation has eigenvalues the
powers of `ω`, and `diag(ω, ω²)` lies in `SU(2)`. Collected here are the facts about `ω` those
uses need: that it is a primitive cube root of unity, that it cubes to one, that it is nonzero
and of modulus one, and that its powers only see the exponent modulo three.

## ii. Key results

- `StandardModel.cubeRootOfUnity` : the primitive cube root of unity `ω = exp (2 π i / 3)`.
- `StandardModel.cubeRootOfUnity_isPrimitiveRoot` : it is a primitive cube root of unity.
- `StandardModel.cubeRootOfUnity_pow_three`, `StandardModel.cubeRootOfUnity_pow_mod` : it cubes
  to one, so its powers only see the exponent modulo three.
- `StandardModel.cubeRootOfUnity_ne_zero`, `StandardModel.cubeRootOfUnity_mul_star` : it is
  nonzero and of modulus one.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. A primitive cube root of unity

## iv. References

The gauge group and its quotients are in `Physlib.Particles.StandardModel.GaugeGroup.Basic`.

sections.text:

`ω = exp (2 π i / 3)` appears in both non-abelian factors: `ω • 1` generates the centre of
`SU(3)`, the cyclic colour permutation has eigenvalues the powers of `ω`, and `diag(ω, ω²)`
lies in `SU(2)`.

modules.title: Gauge weight decompositions
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The operators that may appear in a Standard Model Lagrangian are those the gauge group leaves
fixed, and finding them means searching a large space of composite operators.

The maximal torus of the gauge group is four-dimensional, and a **gauge weight** is the
quadruple of charges

  `(colour₁, colour₂, isospin, hypercharge) : ℤ × ℤ × ℤ × ℤ`,

recording how a vector scales under four chosen elements of it. Two count colour, one counts
weak isospin normalized as `2T₃`, and one counts hypercharge normalized as `6Y`. A **gauge
weight decomposition** of a submodule `V` presents it as a finitely supported family of
subspaces on each of which those four elements act by one such character.

Carrying all four charges at once costs nothing, since the four elements commute. They lie in
different factors of the product group, and the two colour elements are both diagonal, so the
four gradings are simultaneously realizable. An invariant operator is fixed by the whole gauge
group, so in particular by these four elements, so it carries zero weight and the search can
be confined to the zero-weight piece.

In the adjoint representation this grading is the root decomposition of the gauge algebra.
That identification cannot be made here, since the file recording the root data imports
this one; it is `GaugeAlgebra.adjointDecomposition` in
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.StandardModel.GaugeAlgebra.RootDecomposition`.

## ii. Key results

- `gaugeTorusGen` : the four commuting torus generators.
- `GaugeWeight` : the quadruple of charges measured against them.
- `GaugeWeightDecomposition` : a finitely supported family of pure-weight subspaces with
  supremum `V`.
- `GaugeWeightDecomposition.sup` : decompositions combine one weight at a time along
  `V ⊔ V'`.
- `GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul` : weights add under multiplication, decomposing `V * V'`.
- `GaugeWeightDecomposition.piece_eq_inf` : the pieces are cut out of `V` by the torus alone.
- `GaugeWeightDecomposition.mem_zero_of_invariant` : a gauge-invariant element lies in the
  zero-weight piece.
- `GaugeWeightDecomposition.reducesInvariantsTo_piece_zero` : modulo a torus-stable
  submodule `S`, an element fixed by the four torus generators lies in the zero-weight
  piece; `mem_piece_zero_sup_of_invariant` is the unfolded form.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The scalar `exp i` and the torus generators
- B. The four torus generators and gauge weights
- C. Gauge weight decompositions
- D. Powers of `expI` under conjugation
- E. The torus weights of the fundamental representations
- F. The torus action on dual and conjugate bases
- G. Joins
- H. Products
- I. Invariants

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The scalar `exp i` and the torus generators

Every charge here is measured by one scalar. The unit complex number `exp i` has infinite
order, since `π` is irrational, so its integer powers are pairwise distinct and a single
element of the torus already separates all the weights in a given direction.

The torus generators are built by placing `exp i` and its inverse on a diagonal. The maximal
torus of `SU(3)` is two-dimensional, so colour is a two-component charge and needs the two
elements `diag (exp i, exp (-i), 1)` and `diag (1, exp i, exp (-i))`. Weak isospin needs one,
`diag (exp i, exp (-i))`. Each lies in its special unitary group because the diagonal entries
have modulus one and multiply to one. Hypercharge needs no matrix, since its factor of the
gauge group is already the unit circle.

The generators are elements of the group, and the purity of a weight space is recorded by a
character equation `rep g x = c • x`.

## B. The four torus generators and gauge weights

Weights are measured against four chosen elements of the maximal torus, one element per
direction, collected in `gaugeTorusGen`. Four suffice because of the separation in section A.

Both abelian charges are normalized to integers. Weak isospin is measured as `2T₃`, so the two
components of a doublet carry weights `+1` and `-1`, and hypercharge as `6Y`, the smallest
rescaling under which every Standard Model hypercharge is an integer, the quark doublet at `Y = 1/6`
becoming `6Y = 1`. Integrality is what allows every eigenvalue here to be an integer power
`(exp i) ^ k` of one scalar.

`GaugeWeight.coord` reads a weight at a given generator. It is additive, which is why charges
add when operators are multiplied, and injective, so a weight can be recovered from the four
characters by which the torus acts.

## C. Gauge weight decompositions

A gauge weight decomposition is the weight-space decomposition of a representation, with two
differences. It is recorded rather than derived, since the submodules of interest are spans of
explicitly given operators whose charges are read off directly, and it is required only to
cover `V`. Independence of the pieces is not part of the data, because it is automatic, as
section F shows.

Multiplicativity of the representation is named by `IsMulRep` and stored in the `rep_mul`
field, so that a decomposition of a product can be assembled from decompositions of the factors
with no further input. `copy` moves a decomposition across an equality of submodules, needed
because a submodule arising in practice is usually only propositionally the one for which a
decomposition was recorded.
## D. Powers of `expI` under conjugation

## E. The torus weights of the fundamental representations

The colour and isospin weights of the fundamental representations of `SU(3)` and
`SU(2)` against the torus generators.  They are the building blocks of the gauge
weights of the matter representations.

## F. The torus action on dual and conjugate bases

If the torus acts diagonally on a basis then it acts diagonally on the dual basis with
the negated weights, and on the conjugate basis with the negated weights as well — so
the conjugate-dual action carries the original weights back.

## G. Joins

If `V` and `V'` are decomposed then so is their join `V ⊔ V'`, one weight at a time. Its
weight-`w` piece is the join of the two weight-`w` pieces, and its support is the union of the
supports. A vector of the join need not have definite charge, but it is a sum of vectors that
do, which is all a decomposition claims.

The binary case `sup`, the empty case `bot`, a finite indexed family `iSup` and a join over a
proposition `iSupProp` are all the same construction. Multiplicativity of `rep` is recovered
from a summand where there is one and supplied as an argument where there is not, since `bot`
decomposes the zero submodule and the indexed forms may range over an empty family.

## H. Products

Charges add when operators are multiplied, and this section is where we prove this fact.
If the torus acts on `x` by the character of `w₁` and on `y` by the character of `w₂` then,
because `rep` respects multiplication, it acts on `x * y` by the product of the two characters,
which additivity of `GaugeWeight.coord` identifies with the character of `w₁ + w₂`. So the
weight-`w` piece of `V * V'` is spanned by products of pieces whose weights sum to `w`, and the
support of a product is the sumset of the supports.

The defining formula `mul_piece` joins over all pairs of weights in `ℤ⁴ × ℤ⁴`. Only finitely
many weights occur, so one of the two can always be eliminated against a support, and
`mul_piece_eq_sub` and `mul_piece_eq_sub'` do this against the left and the right factor. The
resulting finite joins are what make the weight pieces of a product computable.

## I. Invariants

A gauge-invariant element is fixed by the torus in particular, so it ought to have zero weight.
Making that an argument requires knowing the pieces are independent. Along one generator this
is immediate, since the pieces sit in eigenspaces of a single operator at the eigenvalues
`(exp i) ^ k`, pairwise distinct because `exp i` is not a root of unity, and eigenspaces at
distinct eigenvalues meet trivially. At rank four no single generator separates the weights, so
the argument is made one generator at a time.

What this yields is stronger than the statement about invariants. `piece_eq_inf` identifies the
weight-`w` piece with the intersection of `V` and the joint eigenspace of the four generators,
so the pieces depend only on `V` and the representation.

Zero weight is necessary but not sufficient for invariance. The torus is abelian and sees only
characters, so it cannot distinguish a true singlet from the neutral component of a higher
multiplet. Both `H†H` and `H†σ³H` carry zero weight, and only the first is gauge invariant. So
what passes `mem_zero_of_invariant` must still be checked against the non-abelian part of the
group; no grading closes that gap, since a grading sees only the abelian subgroup generated by
the elements it uses. The `Invariants` files do that check representation by representation.

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3ExpIOne
declarations.doc: The first colour torus generator, `diag (exp i, exp (-i), 1)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def su3ExpIOne : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3ExpITwo
declarations.doc: The second colour torus generator, `diag (1, exp i, exp (-i))`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def su3ExpITwo : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2ExpI
declarations.doc: The `SU(2)` torus element, `diag (exp i, exp (-i))`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def su2ExpI : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2ExpI_coe
declarations.doc: The underlying matrix of the `SU(2)` torus element.
declarations.statement:
lemma su2ExpI_coe :
    (su2ExpI : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ).1
      = !![(expI : ℂ), 0; 0, star (expI : ℂ)]

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2ExpI_inv_coe
declarations.doc:
The inverse torus element is `diag (exp (-i), exp i)`, so on a doublet the two components
are scaled by the reciprocal characters.
declarations.statement:
lemma su2ExpI_inv_coe :
    (su2ExpI⁻¹ : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 2) ℂ).1
      = !![star (expI : ℂ), 0; 0, (expI : ℂ)]

declarations.name: StandardModel.gaugeTorusGen
declarations.doc: The four commuting generators of the maximal torus of the gauge group.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gaugeTorusGen : Fin 4 → GaugeGroupI

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeight
declarations.doc:
A **gauge weight**, the four exponents `(colour₁, colour₂, isospin, hypercharge)`
recording how a vector scales under `gaugeTorusGen`.
declarations.statement: abbrev GaugeWeight : Type

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeight.coord
declarations.doc: The exponent of a gauge weight against the `i`-th torus generator.
declarations.statement: def GaugeWeight.coord (w : GaugeWeight) : Fin 4 → ℤ

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeight.coord_zero
declarations.doc: The exponent at the first colour generator.
declarations.statement: lemma GaugeWeight.coord_zero (w : GaugeWeight) : w.coord 0 = w.1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeight.coord_one
declarations.doc: The exponent at the second colour generator.
declarations.statement: lemma GaugeWeight.coord_one (w : GaugeWeight) : w.coord 1 = w.2.1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeight.coord_two
declarations.doc: The exponent at the isospin generator, normalized as `2T₃`.
declarations.statement: lemma GaugeWeight.coord_two (w : GaugeWeight) : w.coord 2 = w.2.2.1

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeight.coord_three
declarations.doc: The exponent at the hypercharge generator, normalized as `6Y`.
declarations.statement: lemma GaugeWeight.coord_three (w : GaugeWeight) : w.coord 3 = w.2.2.2

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeight.coord_neg
declarations.doc: The zero gauge weight has vanishing exponent against every torus generator.
declarations.statement:
lemma GaugeWeight.coord_neg (w : GaugeWeight) (i : Fin 4) :
    (-w).coord i = -(w.coord i)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeight.zero_coord
declarations.statement: lemma GaugeWeight.zero_coord (i : Fin 4) : (0 : GaugeWeight).coord i = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeight.coord_add
declarations.doc:
Weights add coordinatewise. With `zero_coord` this says `coord` is additive, which is
what makes gauge weights add under multiplication.
declarations.statement:
lemma GaugeWeight.coord_add (w w' : GaugeWeight) (i : Fin 4) :
    (w + w').coord i = w.coord i + w'.coord i

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeight.coord_injective
declarations.doc:
A gauge weight is determined by its four exponents. This is what lets a weight be
recovered from the characters by which the torus acts; see `piece_eq_inf`.
declarations.statement: lemma GaugeWeight.coord_injective : Function.Injective GaugeWeight.coord

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsMulRep
declarations.doc:
A representation acts by algebra maps, respecting multiplication. This is the
hypothesis under which charges are additive.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsMulRep (rep : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI B) : Prop

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsMulRep.map_one
declarations.doc:
A representation that respects multiplication respects the unit, since `g` is invertible
and so `rep g 1` is cancellable.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsMulRep.map_one {rep : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI B} (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (g : GaugeGroupI) : rep g 1 = 1

declarations.name: StandardModel.starRingEnd_expI_pow
declarations.statement:
lemma starRingEnd_expI_pow (n : ℕ) :
    ((starRingEnd ℂ) (expI : ℂ)) ^ n = ((expI : ℂ) ^ n)⁻¹

declarations.name: StandardModel.starRingEnd_expI_zpow
declarations.statement:
lemma starRingEnd_expI_zpow (z : ℤ) :
    (starRingEnd ℂ) ((expI : ℂ) ^ z) = (expI : ℂ) ^ (-z)

declarations.name: StandardModel.expI_zpow_ne_zero
declarations.statement: lemma expI_zpow_ne_zero (z : ℤ) : ((expI : ℂ) ^ z) ≠ 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.colourWeight
declarations.doc:
The colour weights of the fundamental of `SU(3)` against the two colour torus
generators.
declarations.statement: def colourWeight (c : Fin 3) : ℤ × ℤ

declarations.name: StandardModel.isoWeight
declarations.doc:
The isospin weight of the fundamental of `SU(2)` against the isospin torus
generator.
declarations.statement: def isoWeight (s : Fin 2) : ℤ

declarations.name: StandardModel.dual_gaugeTorusGen_coord
declarations.statement:
lemma dual_gaugeTorusGen_coord (ρ : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI V)
    (b : Module.Basis ι ℂ V) (g : GaugeGroupI) (w : ι → ℤ)
    (hb : ∀ j, ρ g (b j) = ((expI : ℂ) ^ w j) • b j) (j : ι) :
    ρ.dual g (b.coord j) = ((expI : ℂ) ^ (-(w j))) • b.coord j

declarations.name: StandardModel.conj_gaugeTorusGen_basis
declarations.statement:
lemma conj_gaugeTorusGen_basis (ρ : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI V)
    (b : Module.Basis ι ℂ V) (g : GaugeGroupI) (w : ι → ℤ)
    (hb : ∀ j, ρ g (b j) = ((expI : ℂ) ^ w j) • b j) (j : ι) :
    ρ.conj g (Basis.conj b j)
      = ((expI : ℂ) ^ (-(w j))) • Basis.conj b j

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition
declarations.doc:
A **gauge weight decomposition** of a submodule `V`, a finitely supported family of
subspaces of pure gauge weight whose supremum is `V`. Purity is recorded against the four
commuting torus generators simultaneously.
declarations.statement:
class GaugeWeightDecomposition (rep : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI B)
    (V : Submodule ℂ B) where
  /-- The piece of gauge weight `w`. -/
  piece : GaugeWeight → Submodule ℂ B
  /-- The finite set of gauge weights that occur. -/
  supp : Finset GaugeWeight
  /-- Gauge transformations act by algebra maps. -/
  rep_mul : IsMulRep rep
  /-- Each piece is of pure gauge weight, as seen by all four torus generators. -/
  piece_le : ∀ w, ∀ x, x ∈ piece w → ∀ i,
    rep (gaugeTorusGen i) x = ((expI : ℂ) ^ w.coord i) • x
  /-- Only the gauge weights in `supp` occur. -/
  piece_eq_bot : ∀ w ∉ supp, piece w = ⊥
  /-- The pieces exhaust `V`. -/
  iSup_piece : (⨆ w, piece w) = V

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.piece_le_eigenspace
declarations.doc:
The weight-`w` piece lies in the eigenspace of the `i`-th torus generator at the
eigenvalue `(exp i) ^ (w.coord i)`. This is `piece_le` phrased as an inequality of
submodules.
declarations.statement:
lemma piece_le_eigenspace (d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V) (w : GaugeWeight) (i : Fin 4) :
    d.piece w ≤ Module.End.eigenspace (rep (gaugeTorusGen i)) ((expI : ℂ) ^ w.coord i)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.piece_eq_zero_of_not_mem_supp
declarations.doc:
A weight outside the support has vanishing piece. This is the `piece_eq_bot` field, in
the form a `simp` set can use to discard the absent weights of a computed product.
declarations.statement:
lemma piece_eq_zero_of_not_mem_supp (d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V) (w : GaugeWeight)
    (hw : w ∉ d.supp) : d.piece w = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.piece_le_self
declarations.doc: A weight piece lies inside the submodule it decomposes.
declarations.statement:
lemma piece_le_self (d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V) (w : GaugeWeight) :
    d.piece w ≤ V

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.copy
declarations.doc: Transport a decomposition along an equality of submodules.
declarations.statement:
def copy (d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V) (W : Submodule ℂ B) (hW : W = V) :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition rep W

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.copy_piece
declarations.statement:
lemma copy_piece (d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V) (W : Submodule ℂ B) (hW : W = V) :
    (copy d W hW).piece = d.piece

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.sup
declarations.doc:
The join of two gauge weight decompositions, decomposing `V ⊔ V'`. Pieces and supports
combine one weight at a time.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance sup [d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V]
    [d' : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V'] : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep (V ⊔ V')

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.sup_piece
declarations.statement:
lemma sup_piece [GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V] [GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V']
    (w : GaugeWeight) : piece rep (V ⊔ V') w = piece rep V w ⊔ piece rep V' w

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.bot
declarations.doc: The zero submodule carries the empty decomposition.
declarations.statement:
def bot (hmul : IsMulRep rep) :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition rep (⊥ : Submodule ℂ B)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.bot_piece
declarations.statement:
lemma bot_piece (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (w : GaugeWeight) : (bot hmul).piece w = ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.bot_supp
declarations.statement:
lemma bot_supp (hmul : IsMulRep rep) :
    (bot hmul).supp = ∅

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.spanSingleton
declarations.doc:
The span of a single simultaneous eigenvector of the gauge torus, as a
decomposition concentrated in its one weight. This is the base case from which the
decompositions of spans of weight vectors are assembled by `iSup` and `sup`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spanSingleton (hmul : IsMulRep rep) (x : B) (w : GaugeWeight)
    (hx : ∀ i, rep (gaugeTorusGen i) x = ((expI : ℂ) ^ w.coord i) • x) :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition rep (Submodule.span ℂ {x})

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.spanSingleton_piece
declarations.statement:
lemma spanSingleton_piece (hmul : IsMulRep rep) (x : B) (w : GaugeWeight)
    (hx : ∀ i, rep (gaugeTorusGen i) x = ((expI : ℂ) ^ w.coord i) • x)
    (w' : GaugeWeight) :
    (spanSingleton hmul x w hx).piece w'
      = if w' = w then Submodule.span ℂ {x} else ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.iSup
declarations.doc:
An indexed join of decompositions. A family of decompositions indexed by a finite type
decomposes the join, its pieces joined and its supports united one weight at a time. This is
the arbitrary-arity form of `sup`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def iSup {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {V : ι → Submodule ℂ B}
    (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (d : (a : ι) → GaugeWeightDecomposition rep (V a)) :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition rep (⨆ a, V a)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.piece_iSup
declarations.statement:
lemma piece_iSup {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {V : ι → Submodule ℂ B}
    (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (d : (a : ι) → GaugeWeightDecomposition rep (V a)) (w : GaugeWeight) :
    (iSup hmul d).piece w = ⨆ a, (d a).piece w

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.iSup_supp
declarations.doc: The support of an indexed join is the union of the supports.
declarations.statement:
lemma iSup_supp {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {V : ι → Submodule ℂ B}
    (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (d : (a : ι) → GaugeWeightDecomposition rep (V a)) :
    (iSup hmul d).supp = Finset.univ.biUnion fun a => (d a).supp

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.iSupProp
declarations.doc:
A join over a proposition. `⨆ _ : p, V` is `V` when `p` holds and `⊥` otherwise, so
it is decomposed by the given decomposition or by `bot`. The argument is a function of the
proof, so the decomposition of `V` may itself depend on `p`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def iSupProp {p : Prop} [Decidable p]
    (hmul : IsMulRep rep)
    (d : p → GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V) :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition rep (⨆ _ : p, V)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul
declarations.doc: The product of two gauge weight decompositions, decomposing `V * V'`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance mul [d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V]
    [d' : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V'] :
    GaugeWeightDecomposition rep (V * V')

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul_supp
declarations.doc: The support of a product is the pointwise sum of the supports.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_supp [GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V] [GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V'] :
    supp rep (V * V') = supp rep V + supp rep V'

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul_piece
declarations.doc:
Weights add under multiplication. The weight-`w` piece of a product is spanned by the
products of pieces whose weights sum to `w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_piece [GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V] [GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V']
    (w : GaugeWeight) :
    piece rep (V * V') w
      = ⨆ w₁, ⨆ w₂, ⨆ _ : w₁ + w₂ = w, piece rep V w₁ * piece rep V' w₂

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul_piece_eq_sub
declarations.doc:
The product formula with the second weight eliminated against the support of the left
factor, the right factor being read at the complement `w - w₁`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_piece_eq_sub [d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V]
    [d' : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V'] (w : GaugeWeight) :
    piece rep (V * V') w = ⨆ w₁ ∈ supp rep V, piece rep V w₁ * piece rep V' (w - w₁)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.mul_piece_eq_sub'
declarations.doc: The mirror of `mul_piece_eq_sub`, joining over the weights of the right factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_piece_eq_sub' [d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V]
    [d' : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V'] (w : GaugeWeight) :
    piece rep (V * V') w = ⨆ w₂ ∈ supp rep V', piece rep V (w - w₂) * piece rep V' w₂

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.mem_iSup_of_eigenvector
declarations.doc:
The one-generator refinement step. A vector in the span of a family graded along a
single operator, and an eigenvector of that operator at exponent `n`, lies in the span of
just those pieces at exponent `n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_iSup_of_eigenvector {ι : Type*} {T : Module.End ℂ B} {p : ι → Submodule ℂ B}
    {f : ι → ℤ} (hp : ∀ j, p j ≤ Module.End.eigenspace T ((expI : ℂ) ^ f j))
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ ⨆ j, p j) {n : ℤ} (hT : T x = ((expI : ℂ) ^ n) • x) :
    x ∈ ⨆ j, ⨆ _ : f j = n, p j

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.mem_iSup_of_forall_eigenvector
declarations.doc:
The many-generator refinement. The same for a finite family of operators. A vector in
the span of the family and an eigenvector of every operator lies in the span of just those
pieces whose exponents match throughout.

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.piece_eq_inf
declarations.doc:
The pieces are canonical. The weight-`w` piece is exactly the part of `V` on which the
four torus generators act by the weight-`w` characters. See `piece_congr`.
declarations.statement:
lemma piece_eq_inf (d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V) (w : GaugeWeight) :
    d.piece w
      = V ⊓ ⨅ i, Module.End.eigenspace (rep (gaugeTorusGen i)) ((expI : ℂ) ^ w.coord i)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.piece_congr
declarations.doc:
The pieces depend only on the submodule. Two decompositions of equal submodules have
the same pieces, so a computation of `piece` may be carried along any equality of
submodules.
declarations.statement:
lemma piece_congr {W : Submodule ℂ B} [d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V]
    [d' : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep W] (hVW : V = W) (w : GaugeWeight) :
    d.piece w = d'.piece w

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.mem_zero_of_invariant
declarations.doc:
A gauge-invariant element sits in the zero-weight piece. Only invariance under the
four torus generators is used. The converse is false; see the warning in section F.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_zero_of_invariant (d : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V) {x : B} (hx : x ∈ V)
    (hV : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, rep g x = x) : x ∈ d.piece 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.reducesInvariantsTo_piece_zero
declarations.doc:
The torus sieve as a reduction for the four torus generators: modulo a torus-stable
submodule, their invariants in `V` lie in the weight-zero piece. Every other weight in the
support is scaled by some generator by `(exp i) ^ n` with `n ≠ 0`, a scalar other than `1`,
so its piece reduces to `⊥` by `reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_apply_eq_smul`; each piece is
carried into itself by the torus, and `ReducesInvariantsTo.iSup` joins the pieces.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_piece_zero (dV : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun i => rep (gaugeTorusGen i)) V (dV.piece 0)

declarations.name: StandardModel.GaugeWeightDecomposition.mem_piece_zero_sup_of_invariant
declarations.doc:
An element of `V ⊔ S` fixed by the four torus generators, for `S` closed under them,
lies in the weight-zero piece joined with `S`. This is `reducesInvariantsTo_piece_zero`
unfolded, the form used to sieve a sector with `S` the part already understood. Only the
torus is used, so gauge invariance of the element and gauge stability of `S` are more than
is needed.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_piece_zero_sup_of_invariant {S : Submodule ℂ B}
    (dV : GaugeWeightDecomposition rep V)
    (hS : ∀ (i : Fin 4) (y : B), y ∈ S → rep (gaugeTorusGen i) y ∈ S)
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ V ⊔ S) (hinv : ∀ i : Fin 4, rep (gaugeTorusGen i) x = x) :
    x ∈ dV.piece 0 ⊔ S

modules.title: Families of adjoint components and their invariants
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The Standard Model labels the adjoint indices of `su(3)` by the eight Gell-Mann matrices
`gellMannMatrix`, and those of `su(2)` by the three Pauli matrices, and moves them by the adjoint
matrices `su3AdjointMatrix` and `su2AdjointMatrix`. These are the generalized Gell-Mann matrices of
`LocalGaugeData.SU.GellMann` for `N = 3` and `N = 2` under a relabelling, `su3Label` and
`su2Label`, and the adjoint matrices are the matrices of the adjoint action in those bases (A).

A family with one adjoint index has no invariant in its span, and a family with two adjoint
indices of the same factor has its invariants reduced to the trace contraction `∑ a, T ![a, a]`
(C for colour, D for isospin): the invariant tensors of `SuT[N, .adj]` and `SuT[N, .adj, .adj]` of
`LocalGaugeData.SU.Invariants.Adjoint`, read on the components through the relabelled
component maps of B.

## ii. Key results

- `StandardModel.su3Label`, `StandardModel.su2Label` : the Gell-Mann and Pauli labels as
  generalized Gell-Mann labels.
- `StandardModel.IsSU3Adjoint.reducesInvariantsTo_bot` : one colour adjoint index carries no
  invariant, and its isospin twin.
- `StandardModel.IsSU3BiAdjoint.reducesInvariantsTo_span_traceContraction` : two colour adjoint
  indices reduce to the trace contraction, and its isospin twin.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Gell-Mann labels
- B. Relabelled adjoint families
- C. The colour adjoint families
- D. The isospin adjoint families

## iv. References

* None.

## B. Relabelled adjoint families

A family indexed by the Standard Model labels of the adjoint index and moved by the Standard Model
adjoint matrices is, after relabelling, a family moved by the matrices of the adjoint action.
## C. The colour adjoint families
## D. The isospin adjoint families

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3LabelFun
declarations.doc:
The labels of the Gell-Mann matrices of `su(3)` as generalized Gell-Mann labels: the
symmetric and antisymmetric matrices of the planes `(0, 1)`, `(0, 2)` and `(1, 2)`, and the two
diagonal matrices.
declarations.statement: def su3LabelFun : Fin 8 → GellMann.Index 3

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3Label
declarations.doc: The relabelling of the Gell-Mann matrices of `su(3)` by generalized Gell-Mann labels.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def su3Label : Fin 8 ≃ GellMann.Index 3

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2LabelFun
declarations.doc: The labels of the Pauli matrices of `su(2)` as generalized Gell-Mann labels.
declarations.statement: def su2LabelFun : Fin 3 → GellMann.Index 2

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2Label
declarations.doc: The relabelling of the Pauli matrices of `su(2)` by generalized Gell-Mann labels.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def su2Label : Fin 3 ≃ GellMann.Index 2

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3Label_apply
declarations.statement: lemma su3Label_apply (a : Fin 8) : su3Label a = su3LabelFun a

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2Label_apply
declarations.statement: lemma su2Label_apply (i : Fin 3) : su2Label i = su2LabelFun i

declarations.name: StandardModel.gellMannMatrix_eq_matrix
declarations.doc: The Gell-Mann matrices of `su(3)` are the generalized Gell-Mann matrices.
declarations.statement:
lemma gellMannMatrix_eq_matrix (a : Fin 8) :
    gellMannMatrix a = GellMann.matrix (su3Label a)

declarations.name: StandardModel.pauliMatrix_inr_eq_matrix
declarations.doc: The Pauli matrices are the generalized Gell-Mann matrices of `su(2)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pauliMatrix_inr_eq_matrix (i : Fin 3) :
    pauliMatrix (Sum.inr i) = GellMann.matrix (su2Label i)

declarations.name: StandardModel.ofReal_half_re_trace
declarations.doc: A complex number fixed by conjugation is the image of its real part.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofReal_half_re_trace {z : ℂ} (hz : star (z / 2) = z / 2) :
    ((2⁻¹ * z.re : ℝ) : ℂ) = z / 2

declarations.name: StandardModel.su3AdjointMatrix_eq_adjMatrix
declarations.doc:
The adjoint matrix of `SU(3)` is the matrix of the adjoint action in the Gell-Mann
basis.
declarations.statement:
lemma su3AdjointMatrix_eq_adjMatrix (U : SU 3) (a b : Fin 8) :
    ((su3AdjointMatrix U a b : ℝ) : ℂ) = adjMatrix U (su3Label a) (su3Label b)

declarations.name: StandardModel.su2AdjointMatrix_eq_adjMatrix
declarations.doc: The adjoint matrix of `SU(2)` is the matrix of the adjoint action in the Pauli basis.
declarations.statement:
lemma su2AdjointMatrix_eq_adjMatrix (U : SU 2) (i j : Fin 3) :
    ((su2AdjointMatrix U i j : ℝ) : ℂ) = adjMatrix U (su2Label i) (su2Label j)

declarations.name: StandardModel.adjMap_smul_of_relabel_law
declarations.doc:
A linear map moving a family with one adjoint label by the Standard Model adjoint matrix of
`U` intertwines the map of the relabelled family with the action of `U`.

declarations.name: StandardModel.adjPairMap_smul_of_relabel_law
declarations.doc:
A linear map moving a family with two adjoint labels by the Standard Model adjoint matrix of
`U` on each label intertwines the map of the relabelled family with the action of `U`.
declarations.statement:

modules.title: Families of colour and isospin components and their invariants
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The invariant tensors of `SU(N)` are classified in `LocalGaugeData.SU.Invariants`, for
equivariant maps out of the tensors of `suTensor N`. Here those results are applied to the
Standard Model. A family `T : ι → B` of components, indexed by colour or isospin labels and moved
by the colour factor `repGauge (U, 1, 1)` or the isospin factor `repGauge (1, V, 1)` of the gauge
group, is turned into a linear map out of the tensors of `SU(3)` or `SU(2)`, and its transformation
law is exactly the equivariance of that map (A).

A law is named by how the members of the family move as vectors of `B`. Under a fundamental law
`f (T l) = ∑ a, U a l • T a`, so `T l` moves like the standard basis vector `e_l` of `ℂⁿ`; an
anti-fundamental law has `conj U` in place of `U`. The component symbols of a field are values of
an equivariant map on dual vectors, so they obey the dual of the field's law: the symbols of a
doublet or triplet field form an anti-fundamental family, and those of its conjugate a fundamental
one.

For a family with a fundamental and an anti-fundamental index the invariants reduce to the delta
contraction (B). For two fundamental or two anti-fundamental indices of `SU(2)` they reduce to the
epsilon contraction (C), and for four fundamental indices of `SU(2)` to the two epsilon pairings
(D). The contractions are written out on the components, and the maps `…Mat` record the laws a
single linear map obeys, for the reductions over the whole gauge group.

## ii. Key results

- `StandardModel.IsSU3FundamentalAntiFundamental.invariantReductionToSpan` : the colour invariants
  of a family with one fundamental and one anti-fundamental colour index.
- `StandardModel.IsSU2FundamentalAntiFundamental.invariantReductionToSpan` : its isospin twin.
- `StandardModel.IsSU2BiFundamental.invariantReductionToSpan`,
  `StandardModel.IsSU2BiAntiFundamental.invariantReductionToSpan` : two isospin indices of the
  same kind.
- `StandardModel.IsSU2QuadFundamental.reducesInvariantsTo_span_epsilonContractions` : four
  fundamental isospin indices.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The factors of the gauge group
- B. One fundamental and one anti-fundamental index
- C. Two isospin indices of the same kind
- D. Four fundamental isospin indices

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: Families with two `u(1)` adjoint indices
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The hypercharge factor is abelian, so its adjoint action on `u(1)` is trivial. A family
`T : (Fin 2 → Fin 1) → B` obeys the `u(1)` bi-adjoint law when a hypercharge rotation moves
it by one factor of the `1 × 1` adjoint matrix `1` per index, which is to say not at all
(`isU1BiAdjointMat_iff`). The law has the same shape as `IsSU2BiAdjoint` and
`IsSU3BiAdjoint`, so that the three factors can be treated alike. The trace contraction is the
one component of the family, and every map obeying the law fixes it.

## ii. Key results

- `isU1BiAdjointMat_iff` : the `u(1)` transformation law says exactly that the map fixes every
  component: the adjoint matrix is `1`, and there is a single family of two `u(1)` indices to sum
  over

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The adjoint matrix and the transformation law
- B. The trace contraction

## iv. References

* None.
