declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.hyperchargeTrace_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The hypercharge trace contraction has mass weight eight.
declarations.statement:
lemma hyperchargeTrace_mem_massWeightSubmodule (p : EightIdx) :
    h.hyperchargeTrace p ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule 8

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.hyperchargeDeriv_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The twice-derived hypercharge field strength has mass weight `2 * (2 + 2)`, eight.
declarations.statement:
lemma hyperchargeDeriv_mem_massWeightSubmodule (d : EightIdx) :
    h.hyperchargeDeriv d ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule 8

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.su3AdjIdx
declarations.doc:
The `su(3)` adjoint weight indices read as weight indices of the whole gauge
algebra: the three colour roots and the two colour Cartan directions.
declarations.statement: def su3AdjIdx : GaugeAlgebra.su3WeightIdx → Fin 4 ⊕ Fin 4 ⊕ Fin 4

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.su2AdjIdx
declarations.doc:
The `su(2)` adjoint weight indices read as weight indices of the whole gauge
algebra: the isospin root and the isospin Cartan direction.
declarations.statement: def su2AdjIdx : GaugeAlgebra.su2WeightIdx → Fin 4 ⊕ Fin 4 ⊕ Fin 4

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.sum_su3WeightCoeff_smul_gluonField
declarations.doc:
A weight vector of the colour part of the adjoint is the matching combination of
gluon field strengths.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_su3WeightCoeff_smul_gluonField {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (k : GaugeAlgebra.su3WeightIdx) :
    ∑ a : Fin 8, GaugeAlgebra.su3WeightCoeff k a • h.gluonField l μ ν a
      = h.adjVec l μ ν (su3AdjIdx k)

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.sum_su2WeightCoeff_smul_wField
declarations.doc:
A weight vector of the isospin part of the adjoint is the matching combination of
`W`-boson field strengths.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_su2WeightCoeff_smul_wField {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (k : GaugeAlgebra.su2WeightIdx) :
    ∑ i : Fin 3, GaugeAlgebra.su2WeightCoeff k i • h.wField l μ ν i
      = h.adjVec l μ ν (su2AdjIdx k)

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.adjVec_mul_adjVec_mem_gluonPair_span
declarations.doc:
A product of two colour weight vectors of the adjoint lies in the span of the matching
gluon pair family.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjVec_mul_adjVec_mem_gluonPair_span (p : EightIdx)
    (k₀ k₁ : GaugeAlgebra.su3WeightIdx) :
    h.adjVec ![] (p 0) (p 1) (su3AdjIdx k₀) * h.adjVec ![] (p 2) (p 3) (su3AdjIdx k₁)
      ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (h.gluonPair p))

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.adjVec_mul_adjVec_mem_wPair_span
declarations.doc:
A product of two isospin weight vectors of the adjoint lies in the span of the matching
`W`-boson pair family.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjVec_mul_adjVec_mem_wPair_span (p : EightIdx) (k₀ k₁ : GaugeAlgebra.su2WeightIdx) :
    h.adjVec ![] (p 0) (p 1) (su2AdjIdx k₀) * h.adjVec ![] (p 2) (p 3) (su2AdjIdx k₁)
      ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (h.wPair p))

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.gluonPairSpan
declarations.doc: The join, over all covector indices, of the spans of the gluon pair families.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gluonPairSpan : Submodule ℂ B

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.wPairSpan
declarations.doc: The join, over all covector indices, of the spans of the `W`-boson pair families.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def wPairSpan : Submodule ℂ B

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.gluonRootPart_le_gluonPairSpan
declarations.doc:
The gluon root part of the zero-weight piece, the three products of a colour raising
vector against the matching lowering vector, lies in the gluon pair spans.
declarations.statement: lemma gluonRootPart_le_gluonPairSpan : h.gluonRootPart ≤ h.gluonPairSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.isospinRootPart_le_wPairSpan
declarations.doc:
The isospin root part of the zero-weight piece, the product of the isospin raising
vector against the lowering vector, lies in the `W`-boson pair spans.
declarations.statement: lemma isospinRootPart_le_wPairSpan : h.isospinRootPart ≤ h.wPairSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.hyperchargeTraceSpan
declarations.doc: The span of the hypercharge trace contractions.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def hyperchargeTraceSpan : Submodule ℂ B

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.hyperchargeDerivSpan
declarations.doc: The span of the twice-derived hypercharge field strengths.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def hyperchargeDerivSpan : Submodule ℂ B

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.neutralVec
declarations.doc:
The two neutral underived directions that pair with a colour index in the mixed
neutral products: the isospin Cartan direction and hypercharge.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def neutralVec (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : Fin 2 → B

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.repGauge_su3_neutralVec
declarations.doc: The neutral directions are fixed by the colour factor of the gauge group.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_su3_neutralVec (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (j : Fin 2) : repGauge (U, 1, 1) (h.neutralVec μ ν j) = h.neutralVec μ ν j

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.DerivIdx
declarations.doc:
The index of a twice-derived symbol: the two derivative slots and the two covector
indices.
declarations.statement: abbrev DerivIdx : Type

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.MixIdx
declarations.doc:
The index of a mixed neutral product: the two covector indices of the colour factor,
the two of the neutral factor, and which of the two neutral directions it is.
declarations.statement: abbrev MixIdx : Type

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.ColourIdx
declarations.doc:
The index of a family carrying one unpaired `su(3)` adjoint index at mass weight
eight: a twice-derived gluon tower, or an underived gluon field strength against a
neutral underived factor on either side.
declarations.statement: abbrev ColourIdx : Type

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.colourFamily
declarations.doc: The families carrying one unpaired `su(3)` adjoint index.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def colourFamily : ColourIdx → Fin 8 → B

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.isSU3Adjoint_colourFamily
declarations.doc:
Each colour family is an `su(3)` adjoint family: the colour factor moves the gluon
index and fixes the neutral factor.
declarations.statement: lemma isSU3Adjoint_colourFamily : ∀ i : ColourIdx, IsSU3Adjoint B repGauge (h.colourFamily i)

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.IsospinIdx
declarations.doc:
The index of a family carrying one unpaired `su(2)` adjoint index at mass weight
eight: a twice-derived `W`-boson tower, or an underived `W`-boson field strength against
an underived hypercharge field strength on either side.
declarations.statement: abbrev IsospinIdx : Type

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.isospinFamily
declarations.doc: The families carrying one unpaired `su(2)` adjoint index.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def isospinFamily : IsospinIdx → Fin 3 → B

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.isSU2Adjoint_isospinFamily
declarations.doc:
Each isospin family is an `su(2)` adjoint family: the isospin factor moves the
`W`-boson index and fixes hypercharge.
declarations.statement: lemma isSU2Adjoint_isospinFamily : ∀ i : IsospinIdx, IsSU2Adjoint B repGauge (h.isospinFamily i)

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.repGauge_su3_isospinFamily
declarations.doc:
The isospin families are fixed by the colour factor, every one of their factors
being.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_su3_isospinFamily (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) :
    ∀ (i : IsospinIdx) (a : Fin 3),
      repGauge (U, 1, 1) (h.isospinFamily i a) = h.isospinFamily i a

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.unpairedColourSpan
declarations.doc: The join of the spans of the colour families.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def unpairedColourSpan : Submodule ℂ B

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.unpairedIsospinSpan
declarations.doc: The join of the spans of the isospin families.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def unpairedIsospinSpan : Submodule ℂ B

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.colourFamily_mem
declarations.doc: A component of a colour family lies in the join of the colour spans.
declarations.statement: lemma colourFamily_mem (i : ColourIdx) (a : Fin 8) : h.colourFamily i a ∈ h.unpairedColourSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.isospinFamily_mem
declarations.doc: A component of an isospin family lies in the join of the isospin spans.
declarations.statement:
lemma isospinFamily_mem (i : IsospinIdx) (a : Fin 3) :
    h.isospinFamily i a ∈ h.unpairedIsospinSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.repGauge_su3_of_mem_unpairedIsospinSpan
declarations.doc: The join of the isospin families is fixed pointwise by the colour factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_su3_of_mem_unpairedIsospinSpan (U : specialUnitaryGroup (Fin 3) ℂ) :
    ∀ y ∈ h.unpairedIsospinSpan, repGauge (U, 1, 1) y = y

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.colourCartanSpan
declarations.doc:
The colour Cartan directions of the underived tower: the two weight-zero directions of
the `su(3)` factor.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def colourCartanSpan : Submodule ℂ B

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.neutralSpan
declarations.doc:
The neutral directions of the underived tower: the isospin Cartan direction and
hypercharge.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def neutralSpan : Submodule ℂ B

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.adjVec_colourCartan
declarations.doc:
A colour Cartan weight vector is the gluon field strength on the matching Cartan
direction of `su(3)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjVec_colourCartan {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (c : Fin 2) :
    h.adjVec l μ ν (Sum.inr (Sum.inr c.castSucc.castSucc))
      = h.gluonField l μ ν (GaugeAlgebra.su3CartanId c)

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.cartanSpan_le
declarations.doc:
The weight-zero directions of the adjoint are the colour Cartan directions and the
neutral directions.
declarations.statement: lemma cartanSpan_le : h.cartanSpan ≤ h.colourCartanSpan ⊔ h.neutralSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.colourCartanSpan_mul_colourCartanSpan_le
declarations.doc: A product of two colour Cartan directions is a component of a gluon pair family.
declarations.statement:
lemma colourCartanSpan_mul_colourCartanSpan_le :
    h.colourCartanSpan * h.colourCartanSpan ≤ h.gluonPairSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.colourCartanSpan_mul_neutralSpan_le
declarations.doc:
A colour Cartan direction against a neutral direction is a component of a colour
family.
declarations.statement:
lemma colourCartanSpan_mul_neutralSpan_le :
    h.colourCartanSpan * h.neutralSpan ≤ h.unpairedColourSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.neutralSpan_mul_colourCartanSpan_le
declarations.doc:
A neutral direction against a colour Cartan direction is a component of a colour
family.
declarations.statement:
lemma neutralSpan_mul_colourCartanSpan_le :
    h.neutralSpan * h.colourCartanSpan ≤ h.unpairedColourSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.neutralSpan_mul_neutralSpan_le
declarations.doc:
A product of two neutral directions: isospin against isospin is a component of a
`W`-boson pair family, hypercharge against hypercharge is a hypercharge trace
contraction, and the two mixed products are components of isospin families.
declarations.statement:
lemma neutralSpan_mul_neutralSpan_le :
    h.neutralSpan * h.neutralSpan
      ≤ h.unpairedIsospinSpan ⊔ (h.wPairSpan ⊔ h.hyperchargeTraceSpan)

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.neutralCartanPart_le
declarations.doc:
The neutral part of the zero-weight piece: the products pairing a factor with itself
are components of the pair families or hypercharge trace contractions, and the mixed
products carry an unpaired non-abelian index.
declarations.statement:
lemma neutralCartanPart_le :
    h.neutralCartanPart ≤ (h.unpairedColourSpan ⊔ h.unpairedIsospinSpan)
      ⊔ (h.gluonPairSpan ⊔ (h.wPairSpan ⊔ h.hyperchargeTraceSpan))

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.derivCartanSpan_le
declarations.doc:
The twice-derived symbols on the weight-zero directions: on a colour or isospin Cartan
direction a component of an adjoint family, on hypercharge a twice-derived hypercharge
field strength.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivCartanSpan_le :
    (⨆ (l : Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (c : Fin 4),
        ℂ ∙ F l μ ν (GaugeAlgebra.stdBasis.coord (GaugeAlgebra.cartanIdx c)))
      ≤ (h.unpairedColourSpan ⊔ h.unpairedIsospinSpan) ⊔ h.hyperchargeDerivSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightEight_piece_zero_le
declarations.doc:
The zero-weight piece of mass weight eight is bounded by the joins of the unpaired
families together with the pair spans, the hypercharge trace contractions and the
twice-derived hypercharge field strengths.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightEight_piece_zero_le :
    (h.massWeightSubmoduleGaugeWeightEight).piece 0
      ≤ (h.unpairedColourSpan ⊔ h.unpairedIsospinSpan)
        ⊔ (h.gluonPairSpan
          ⊔ (h.wPairSpan ⊔ (h.hyperchargeTraceSpan ⊔ h.hyperchargeDerivSpan)))

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.reducesInvariantsTo_unpaired
declarations.doc:
The joins of the unpaired families reduce to `⊥` for the gauge group: the colour
families for the colour factor, with the colour-fixed isospin join kept in the target, and
then the isospin families for the isospin factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_unpaired :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g : GaugeGroupI => repGauge g)
      (h.unpairedColourSpan ⊔ h.unpairedIsospinSpan) ⊥

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.gluonTraceSpan
declarations.doc: The span of the gluon trace contractions.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gluonTraceSpan : Submodule ℂ B

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.wTraceSpan
declarations.doc: The span of the `W`-boson trace contractions.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def wTraceSpan : Submodule ℂ B

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.traceContractionEightSpan
declarations.doc:
The span of the three underived trace contractions, over all covector indices: the
gauge invariants of mass weight eight that the bi-adjoint classification produces.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def traceContractionEightSpan : Submodule ℂ B

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.isStableUnder_gluonPairSpan
declarations.doc: The gluon pair spans are stable under the gauge group.
declarations.statement:
lemma isStableUnder_gluonPairSpan :
    IsStableUnder (fun g : GaugeGroupI => repGauge g) h.gluonPairSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.isStableUnder_wPairSpan
declarations.doc: The `W`-boson pair spans are stable under the gauge group.
declarations.statement:
lemma isStableUnder_wPairSpan :
    IsStableUnder (fun g : GaugeGroupI => repGauge g) h.wPairSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.repGauge_of_mem_hyperchargeTraceSpan
declarations.doc: The hypercharge trace contractions are fixed pointwise by the gauge group.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_of_mem_hyperchargeTraceSpan (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    ∀ y ∈ h.hyperchargeTraceSpan, repGauge g y = y

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.repGauge_of_mem_hyperchargeDerivSpan
declarations.doc:
The twice-derived hypercharge field strengths are fixed pointwise by the gauge
group.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_of_mem_hyperchargeDerivSpan (g : GaugeGroupI) :
    ∀ y ∈ h.hyperchargeDerivSpan, repGauge g y = y

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.traceContractionEightSpan_sup_hyperchargeDerivSpan_le
declarations.doc:
The gauge span is a space of gauge invariants of mass weight eight: each generator is
fixed by the gauge group and has mass weight eight by section C. This is the converse of
the classification.
declarations.statement:
lemma traceContractionEightSpan_sup_hyperchargeDerivSpan_le :
    h.traceContractionEightSpan ⊔ h.hyperchargeDerivSpan
      ≤ h.massWeightSubmodule 8 ⊓ repGauge.invariants

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.isFixedBy_traceContractionEightSpan_sup
declarations.doc: The gauge span is fixed pointwise by the gauge group.
declarations.statement:
lemma isFixedBy_traceContractionEightSpan_sup :
    IsFixedBy (fun g : GaugeGroupI => repGauge g)
      (h.traceContractionEightSpan ⊔ h.hyperchargeDerivSpan)

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.reducesInvariantsTo_gluonPairSpan
declarations.doc:
The gluon pair spans reduce, for the gauge group, to the gluon trace contractions: each
gluon pair family is bi-adjoint for the colour factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_gluonPairSpan :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g : GaugeGroupI => repGauge g) h.gluonPairSpan h.gluonTraceSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.reducesInvariantsTo_wPairSpan
declarations.doc:
The `W`-boson pair spans reduce, for the gauge group, to the `W`-boson trace
contractions: each `W`-boson pair family is bi-adjoint for the isospin factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_wPairSpan :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g : GaugeGroupI => repGauge g) h.wPairSpan h.wTraceSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.reducesInvariantsTo_traceContractionEightSpan_sup
declarations.doc:
Mass weight eight reduces, for the gauge group, to the three underived trace
contractions and the twice-derived hypercharge field strengths. The torus puts a gauge
invariant in the zero-weight piece; of the parts bounding it, the unpaired joins reduce to
`⊥`, the pair spans to their trace contractions, and the hypercharge spans are already
fixed.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_traceContractionEightSpan_sup :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g : GaugeGroupI => repGauge g) (h.massWeightSubmodule 8)
      (h.traceContractionEightSpan ⊔ h.hyperchargeDerivSpan)

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.repLorentz_F_underived
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz transformation of an underived field-strength symbol: the general law of
`IsGaugeSector` at no covariant derivatives, where the sum over the derivative slots is
a single term, written with the two covector rotations gathered into one coefficient.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_F_underived (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) :
    repLorentz Λ (F ![] μ ν φ)
      = ∑ a : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, ∑ b : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3,
        ((((SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 a μ : ℝ) : ℂ) *
          (((SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 b ν : ℝ) : ℂ)) • F ![] a b φ

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.sum_mul_sum_eq_sum_pi_four
declarations.doc: A product of two double combinations is a combination indexed by quadruples.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_mul_sum_eq_sum_pi_four (c c' : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ)
    (X Y : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) :
    (∑ a, ∑ b, c a b • X a b) * (∑ x, ∑ y, c' x y • Y x y)
      = ∑ d : Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3,
        (c (d 0) (d 1) * c' (d 2) (d 3)) • (X (d 0) (d 1) * Y (d 2) (d 3))

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.isLorentzCovariant_F_mul
declarations.doc:
A product of two underived field-strength symbols, viewed as a family indexed by the
four covector indices it carries, is a quadruple Lorentz tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma isLorentzCovariant_F_mul (φ ψ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) :
    IsLorentzCovariant 4 B repLorentz (ofComponents
      fun d : Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 => F ![] (d 0) (d 1) φ * F ![] (d 2) (d 3) ψ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.isLorentzCovariant_sum
declarations.doc:
A finite sum of quadruple Lorentz tensors is a quadruple Lorentz tensor: the
transformation law is linear in the family.

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.isLorentzCovariant_of_eq_sum
declarations.doc:
A family of four four-vector indices whose members are sums of products of two
underived field-strength symbols is a quadruple Lorentz tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma isLorentzCovariant_of_eq_sum {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] {T : EightIdx → B}
    (φ : ι → Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra)
    (hT : ∀ d, T d = ∑ i, F ![] (d 0) (d 1) (φ i) * F ![] (d 2) (d 3) (φ i)) :
    IsLorentzCovariant 4 B repLorentz (ofComponents T)

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.isLorentzCovariant_gluonTrace
declarations.doc:
The gluon trace contractions, read as a family of four four-vector indices, form a
quadruple Lorentz tensor: a sum over the colour index of products of two underived
field-strength symbols.
declarations.statement:
lemma isLorentzCovariant_gluonTrace :
    IsLorentzCovariant 4 B repLorentz (ofComponents h.gluonTrace)

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.isLorentzCovariant_wTrace
declarations.doc: The `W`-boson trace contractions form a quadruple Lorentz tensor.
declarations.statement: lemma isLorentzCovariant_wTrace : IsLorentzCovariant 4 B repLorentz (ofComponents h.wTrace)

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.isLorentzCovariant_hyperchargeTrace
declarations.doc: The hypercharge trace contractions form a quadruple Lorentz tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma isLorentzCovariant_hyperchargeTrace :
    IsLorentzCovariant 4 B repLorentz (ofComponents h.hyperchargeTrace)

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.isLorentzCovariant_hyperchargeDeriv
declarations.doc:
The twice-derived hypercharge field strengths, read as a family of four four-vector
indices, form a quadruple Lorentz tensor: the two derivative slots and the two covector
indices all rotate. This is the second shape of mass weight eight.
declarations.statement:
lemma isLorentzCovariant_hyperchargeDeriv :
    IsLorentzCovariant 4 B repLorentz (ofComponents h.hyperchargeDeriv)

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.gluonTrace_comp_swap_two_three
declarations.doc:
The gluon trace contractions are antisymmetric in the last two covector indices, by
`F_antisymm` in the second factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma gluonTrace_comp_swap_two_three (d : EightIdx) :
    h.gluonTrace (d ∘ Equiv.swap 2 3) = -h.gluonTrace d

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.wTrace_comp_swap_two_three
declarations.doc: The `W`-boson trace contractions are antisymmetric in the last two covector indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma wTrace_comp_swap_two_three (d : EightIdx) :
    h.wTrace (d ∘ Equiv.swap 2 3) = -h.wTrace d

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.hyperchargeTrace_comp_swap_two_three
declarations.doc: The hypercharge trace contractions are antisymmetric in the last two covector indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma hyperchargeTrace_comp_swap_two_three (d : EightIdx) :
    h.hyperchargeTrace (d ∘ Equiv.swap 2 3) = -h.hyperchargeTrace d

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.hyperchargeDeriv_comp_swap_two_three
declarations.doc:
The twice-derived hypercharge field strengths are antisymmetric in their two covector
indices, the last two slots, by `F_antisymm` at two covariant derivatives. Nothing is
assumed about the two derivative slots.
declarations.statement:
lemma hyperchargeDeriv_comp_swap_two_three (d : EightIdx) :
    h.hyperchargeDeriv (d ∘ Equiv.swap 2 3) = -h.hyperchargeDeriv d

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.quadContractionSpan
declarations.doc:
The span of the four Lorentz contractions of a quadruple Lorentz tensor: the images of
the three metric pairings and of the Levi-Civita symbol.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def quadContractionSpan (T : (Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) : Submodule ℂ B

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.quadContractionSpan_le_span
declarations.doc:
The span of the four Lorentz contractions of a quadruple Lorentz family lies in the
span of its components: each contraction is a combination of components with constant
coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma quadContractionSpan_le_span {T : (Fin 4 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B} :
    quadContractionSpan T ≤ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range T)

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.quadContractionSpan_le_lorentzInvariants
declarations.doc:
The span of the four Lorentz contractions of a quadruple Lorentz family is a space of
Lorentz invariants, the four contractions being invariant by `RankFour`.

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.quadContractionSpan_eq_of_antisymm
declarations.doc:
For a quadruple family antisymmetric in its last two slots the four Lorentz contractions
reduce to two, the `(0,2)(1,3)` metric contraction and the Levi-Civita one: the
`(0,1)(2,3)` metric contraction vanishes and the `(0,3)(1,2)` one is minus the
`(0,2)(1,3)` one.

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
declarations.doc:
The span of the four Lorentz contractions of each of the three underived
trace-contraction families and of the twice-derived hypercharge family: the gauge and
Lorentz invariants of mass weight eight that the two classifications together produce.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def lorentzContractionEightSpan : Submodule ℂ B

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan_le_traceContractionEightSpan_sup
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz contraction span sits inside the gauge span: each of its four blocks is
spanned by the four contractions of a quadruple Lorentz family whose components generate
the matching block of the gauge span.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzContractionEightSpan_le_traceContractionEightSpan_sup :
    h.lorentzContractionEightSpan ≤ h.traceContractionEightSpan ⊔ h.hyperchargeDerivSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan_le_invariants
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz contraction span is a space of gauge invariants: it lies in the gauge
span, whose generators the gauge group fixes.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzContractionEightSpan_le_invariants :
    h.lorentzContractionEightSpan ≤ repGauge.invariants

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan_eq
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz contraction span is spanned by eight of its sixteen generators: for each
family the `(0,2)(1,3)` metric contraction and the Levi-Civita contraction. All four families
are antisymmetric in their last two slots by `F_antisymm`, which removes the other two
contractions of each.

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan_le_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The Lorentz contraction span lies in the mass-weight eight submodule.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzContractionEightSpan_le_massWeightSubmodule :
    h.lorentzContractionEightSpan ≤ h.massWeightSubmodule 8

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan_le_lorentzInvariants
declarations.doc: The Lorentz contraction span is a space of Lorentz invariants.
declarations.statement:
lemma lorentzContractionEightSpan_le_lorentzInvariants :
    h.lorentzContractionEightSpan ≤ repLorentz.invariants

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.isFixedBy_lorentzContractionEightSpan
declarations.doc: The Lorentz contraction span is fixed pointwise by both groups.
declarations.statement:
lemma isFixedBy_lorentzContractionEightSpan :
    IsFixedBy (gaugeLorentzMaps repGauge repLorentz) h.lorentzContractionEightSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.reducesInvariantsTo_lorentzContractionEightSpan
declarations.doc:
The gauge sector at mass weight eight reduces, for the gauge and Lorentz groups
together, to the four Lorentz contractions of each of the four families. The gauge group
leaves the trace contractions and the twice-derived hypercharge field strengths; each of
the four spans is spanned by a quadruple Lorentz tensor and reduces, for the Lorentz
group, to the span of its four contractions. Two of the four suffice for each family, by
`lorentzContractionEightSpan_eq`.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_lorentzContractionEightSpan :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (gaugeLorentzMaps repGauge repLorentz) (h.massWeightSubmodule 8)
      h.lorentzContractionEightSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_invariant_iff
declarations.doc:
The gauge classification of mass weight eight as an equivalence: an element of
`massWeightSubmodule 8 ⊔ S` is gauge invariant exactly when it is a combination of the
three underived trace contractions and the twice-derived hypercharge field strengths up
to a gauge-invariant remainder in `S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_invariant_iff (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGauge g y ∈ S) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule 8 ⊔ S ∧ ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ h.traceContractionEightSpan ⊔ h.hyperchargeDerivSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
declarations.doc:
The gauge and Lorentz classification of mass weight eight as an equivalence: an
element of `massWeightSubmodule 8 ⊔ S` is fixed by both groups exactly when it is a
combination of the four Lorentz contractions of the four families of section H up to a
remainder in `S` fixed by both groups. The version with two contractions of each family is
`mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_reduced`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
    (S : Submodule ℂ B) (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGauge g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule 8 ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ h.lorentzContractionEightSpan

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_reduced
declarations.doc:
The same equivalence with the eight generators of `lorentzContractionEightSpan_eq`: for
each of the three underived trace families its `(0,2)(1,3)` metric contraction, of the shape
`η^{μρ} η^{νσ} F_{μν} F_{ρσ}`, and its Levi-Civita contraction, of the shape
`ε^{μνρσ} F_{μν} F_{ρσ}`, and for the twice-derived hypercharge field strengths
`η^{μρ} η^{νσ} ∇_μ ∇_ν B_{ρσ}` and `ε^{μνρσ} ∇_μ ∇_ν B_{ρσ}`. The eight span; they are not
shown to be independent or nonzero.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_reduced
    (S : Submodule ℂ B) (hS : ∀ g : GaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repGauge g y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule 8 ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ Submodule.span ℂ {ofComponents h.gluonTrace (contractionTensor 1),
              ofComponents h.gluonTrace (contractionTensor 3)}
            ⊔ (Submodule.span ℂ {ofComponents h.wTrace (contractionTensor 1),
                ofComponents h.wTrace (contractionTensor 3)}
              ⊔ (Submodule.span ℂ {ofComponents h.hyperchargeTrace (contractionTensor 1),
                  ofComponents h.hyperchargeTrace (contractionTensor 3)}
                ⊔ Submodule.span ℂ {ofComponents h.hyperchargeDeriv (contractionTensor 1),
                  ofComponents h.hyperchargeDeriv (contractionTensor 3)}))

modules.title: The invariants below mass weight eight
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Mass weight eight is the first weight of the gauge sector carrying a gauge and Lorentz
invariant. Below it there is nothing: the odd weights and weight two are trivial
submodules, weight four is a single underived field strength and weight six a single
once-derived one, and neither of those two carries an invariant.

Weight four fails on parity of a different kind. An underived field strength carries two
covector indices and one adjoint index, so at a fixed gauge direction it is a bi-Lorentz
tensor, whose only invariant contraction is the metric trace. That trace vanishes, the
metric being symmetric in the pair of indices in which `IsGaugeSector.F_antisymm` says
the field strength is antisymmetric. Weight six fails on counting: a once-derived field
strength carries three covector indices, and three indices admit no invariant contraction
at all, the metric tying two and the Levi-Civita symbol four.

Neither argument needs the gauge group. The vanishing at weight four holds at every gauge
direction separately, the colour and isospin ones included, so no appeal to
`IsSU3Adjoint` or `IsSU2Adjoint` is required and Lorentz invariance alone does the work.
What the gauge algebra does contribute is finiteness: a field-strength symbol is
evaluated on a covector of the gauge algebra, and expanding that covector in the dual of
the standard basis writes each derivative submodule inside a finite join of Lorentz
spans, one for each of the twelve basis directions, which is what the peeling arguments
consume.


The final statement `mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff`
needs `0 < w` as well as `w < 8`: at `w = 0` the mass-weight submodule contains the
scalars, so `1` is an invariant of weight zero lying in no `S`.

## ii. Key results

- `mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff` : the classification below
  mass weight eight as an equivalence, in the shape of
  `mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff`: an element of
  `massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S` for `0 < w < 8` is fixed by both groups exactly when it is itself an
  element of `S` fixed by both groups

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The symbols on the standard basis of the gauge algebra
- B. Sums over tuples of covector indices
- C. The field-strength symbols as Lorentz families
- D. The vanishing of the metric trace of an antisymmetric family
- E. Peeling Lorentz spans off a stable submodule
- F. Mass weight four
- G. Mass weight six
- H. The classification below mass weight eight

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The symbols on the standard basis of the gauge algebra

The gauge algebra is finite dimensional, so a covector on it is the combination of the
coordinates of the standard basis with its own values on that basis. A field-strength
symbol evaluated on an arbitrary covector is therefore a combination of the twelve
symbols evaluated on those coordinates.

## B. Sums over tuples of covector indices

A Lorentz family is indexed by a tuple of covector indices, while the transformation law
of `IsGaugeSector` presents its sums one index at a time. These two lemmas, with
`Lorentz.sum_pi_fin_two` for two indices, turn a sum over tuples into an iterated sum and
back.

## C. The field-strength symbols as Lorentz families

An underived field-strength symbol carries two covector indices and nothing else, and a
once-derived one carries three, its derivative slot included. Read as families indexed by
those indices they are a bi-Lorentz and a triple Lorentz tensor, the transformation law
of `IsGaugeSector` moving every index by the Lorentz matrix of the `SL(2,ℂ)` element.

## D. The vanishing of the metric trace of an antisymmetric family

Two covector indices admit a single invariant contraction, the metric trace, and the
metric is diagonal, so that trace is the sum of the components on the diagonal. A family
antisymmetric in its two indices has every diagonal component equal to its own negative,
hence zero, and the trace vanishes with them.

## E. Peeling Lorentz spans off a stable submodule

Both classifications come in a form relative to a Lorentz-stable submodule `S`: an
invariant of the span of a family together with `S` is a contraction of the family up to
a remainder in `S`. When the contraction vanishes, or when there is none, the span of the
family reduces to `⊥`, and the invariant lies in `S` outright. The spans themselves are
Lorentz stable, so `ReducesInvariantsTo.biSup` combines these reductions over a finite
join of them.

## F. Mass weight four

Mass weight four is the underived field strength. At each of the twelve directions of the
standard basis of the gauge algebra it is a bi-Lorentz family, whose metric trace vanishes
by the antisymmetry of the field strength in its two covector indices, so section E peels
the twelve spans off and leaves nothing behind. No gauge hypothesis enters: the vanishing
holds at the colour and isospin directions just as at the hypercharge one.

## G. Mass weight six

Mass weight six is the once-derived field strength, a triple Lorentz family at each
direction of the standard basis. Three covector indices carry no invariant contraction at
all, so the rank-three classification needs no antisymmetry and no gauge input either: the
twelve spans peel off and the invariant is left in `S`.

## H. The classification below mass weight eight

The seven weights between zero and eight are now settled: weights one, two, three, five
and seven are trivial submodules, weight four is section F and weight six section G. So
between weight zero and weight eight there is no invariant beyond what `S` already
supplies, and the equivalence records it.

The lower bound `0 < w` cannot be dropped. Weight zero contains the scalars by
`one_le_massWeightSubmodule_zero`, and `1` is fixed by both groups, the two
representations being multiplicative, without lying in any given `S`.

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.F_mem_iSup_span_coord
declarations.doc:
A field-strength symbol lies in the span of the twelve symbols evaluated on the
coordinates of the standard basis of the gauge algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma F_mem_iSup_span_coord {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) :
    F l μ ν φ ∈ ⨆ c : Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1,
      ℂ ∙ F l μ ν (GaugeAlgebra.stdBasis.coord c)

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.sum_cov_one
declarations.doc: A sum over families of one covector index is a single sum.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_cov_one {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (f : (Fin 1 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M) :
    ∑ d : Fin 1 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, f d = ∑ x : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, f ![x]

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.sum_cov_three
declarations.doc: A sum over families of three covector indices is a triple sum.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_cov_three {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (f : (Fin 3 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → M) :
    ∑ d : Fin 3 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, f d
      = ∑ x : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, ∑ y : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, ∑ z : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3, f ![x, y, z]

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.isLorentzCovariant_F_underived
declarations.doc:
An underived field-strength symbol, viewed as a family indexed by its two covector
indices, is a bi-Lorentz tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma isLorentzCovariant_F_underived (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) :
    IsLorentzCovariant 2 B repLorentz
      (ofComponents fun d : Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 => F ![] (d 0) (d 1) φ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.isLorentzCovariant_F_deriv_one
declarations.doc:
A once-derived field-strength symbol, viewed as a family indexed by its derivative
slot and its two covector indices, is a triple Lorentz tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma isLorentzCovariant_F_deriv_one (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) :
    IsLorentzCovariant 3 B repLorentz
      (ofComponents fun d : Fin 3 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 => F ![d 0] (d 1) (d 2) φ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.ofComponents_metric_eq_zero_of_antisymm
declarations.doc:
The metric trace of a bi-Lorentz family antisymmetric in its two indices vanishes:
the metric is diagonal, and the diagonal components of such a family are zero.

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_biSup_rankTwo_span
declarations.doc:
A finite join of the spans of bi-Lorentz families with vanishing metric traces carries
no Lorentz invariant modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule: a Lorentz invariant of the join
together with `S` lies in `S`. Each span reduces to the line through its metric
contraction, which is zero, and `ReducesInvariantsTo.biSup` combines the reductions.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_biSup_rankTwo_span {ι : Type} [DecidableEq ι]
    {T : ι → (Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B}
    (hT : ∀ i, IsLorentzCovariant 2 B repLorentz (ofComponents (T i)))
    (hzero : ∀ i, ofComponents (T i) RankTwo.metric = 0) (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hS : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (s : Finset ι) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ (⨆ i ∈ s, Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (T i))) ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_biSup_rankThree_span
declarations.doc:
A finite join of the spans of triple Lorentz families carries no Lorentz invariant
modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule: three covector indices carry no invariant contraction
at all, so each span reduces to `⊥`, and `ReducesInvariantsTo.biSup` combines the
reductions.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_biSup_rankThree_span {ι : Type} [DecidableEq ι]
    {T : ι → (Fin 3 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B}
    (hT : ∀ i, IsLorentzCovariant 3 B repLorentz (ofComponents (T i)))
    (S : Submodule ℂ B) (hS : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (s : Finset ι)
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ (⨆ i ∈ s, Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range (T i))) ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.iSup_eq_biSup_univ
declarations.doc: A join over a finite index type is the join over its universal finite set.
declarations.statement:
lemma iSup_eq_biSup_univ {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (f : ι → Submodule ℂ B) :
    ⨆ i, f i = ⨆ i ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset ι), f i

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.ofComponents_F_underived_metric_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
The metric trace of the underived field-strength symbols at a fixed direction of the
gauge algebra vanishes, the symbol being antisymmetric in its two covector indices.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofComponents_F_underived_metric_eq_zero (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra) :
    ofComponents (fun d : Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 => F ![] (d 0) (d 1) φ) RankTwo.metric = 0

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.derivSubmodule_zero_le_iSup_span
declarations.doc:
The underived field strengths lie in the join, over the twelve directions of the
standard basis of the gauge algebra, of the spans of the bi-Lorentz families they
form.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_zero_le_iSup_span :
    h.derivSubmodule 0 ≤ ⨆ c : Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1,
      Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun d : Fin 2 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 =>
        F ![] (d 0) (d 1) (GaugeAlgebra.stdBasis.coord c))

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_massWeightSubmodule_four_sup
declarations.doc:
Mass weight four carries no Lorentz invariant modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule: a
Lorentz invariant of `massWeightSubmodule 4 ⊔ S` lies in `S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_massWeightSubmodule_four_sup (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule 4 ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.etaExpand_cov_one
declarations.doc: A family of one covector index is the tuple of its own entry.
declarations.statement: lemma etaExpand_cov_one (l : Fin 1 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : ![l 0] = l

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.derivSubmodule_one_le_iSup_span
declarations.doc:
The once-derived field strengths lie in the join, over the twelve directions of the
standard basis of the gauge algebra, of the spans of the triple Lorentz families they
form.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivSubmodule_one_le_iSup_span :
    h.derivSubmodule 1 ≤ ⨆ c : Fin 8 ⊕ Fin 3 ⊕ Fin 1,
      Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun d : Fin 3 → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3 =>
        F ![d 0] (d 1) (d 2) (GaugeAlgebra.stdBasis.coord c))

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_massWeightSubmodule_six_sup
declarations.doc:
Mass weight six carries no Lorentz invariant modulo a Lorentz-stable submodule: a
Lorentz invariant of `massWeightSubmodule 6 ⊔ S` lies in `S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_massWeightSubmodule_six_sup (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule 6 ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.mem_of_lorentz_invariant_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup
declarations.doc:
Between mass weight zero and mass weight eight there is no Lorentz invariant: a
Lorentz invariant of `massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S` for `0 < w < 8` lies in `S`. The five
odd or small weights are trivial submodules, and weights four and six are sections F
and G.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_lorentz_invariant_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup (w : ℕ) (hw0 : 0 < w)
    (hw : w < 8) (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) {x : B}
    (hx : x ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff
declarations.doc:
The classification below mass weight eight as an equivalence, in the shape of
`mem_massWeightSubmodule_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff`: an element of
`massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S` for `0 < w < 8` is fixed by both groups exactly when it is
itself an element of `S` fixed by both groups. The span of invariants that the weight
eight statement leaves over is here the trivial one, so `x - y` lies in it exactly when
`x = y`. Gauge stability of `S` is not needed, and neither is gauge invariance of `x`:
the forward direction is
`mem_of_lorentz_invariant_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup`, which uses the Lorentz
group alone.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff (w : ℕ)
    (hw0 : 0 < w) (hw : w < 8) (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g y = y)
          ∧ (∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g y = y)
          ∧ x = y

declarations.name: StandardModel.IsGaugeSector.mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem
declarations.doc:
The same classification without the existential: below mass weight eight an element
of `massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S` fixed by both groups is an element of `S` fixed by both
groups, and conversely.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_lt_eight_sup_and_gauge_lorentz_invariant_iff_mem (w : ℕ)
    (hw0 : 0 < w) (hw : w < 8) (S : Submodule ℂ B)
    (hSL : ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentz g y ∈ S) (x : B) :
    (x ∈ h.massWeightSubmodule w ⊔ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
        ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)
      ↔ (x ∈ S ∧ (∀ g : GaugeGroupI, repGauge g x = x)
          ∧ ∀ g : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentz g x = x)

modules.title: The jet algebra of the Standard Model is a Standard Model
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The abstract theory of `AlgebraRealization` asks an algebra for an equivariant algebra map out
of the jet algebra of the Standard Model. The jet algebra therefore carries one for free —
the identity — and `AlgebraRealization.id` records it, in `AlgebraRealization.Basic`. The
four compatibility laws are definitional; the two multiplicativity laws are the ones the
jet gauge action and the Lorentz action were shown to satisfy when they were built.

Once the instance exists, two things follow that make it worth having. The field algebra it
generates is the whole algebra — the fields of the
Standard Model generate the algebra in which its Lagrangian lives, since nothing else is
available to write down — so the mass-weight submodules stop being intersections with the
field algebra and become the honest eigenspaces of `massWeightPoly` on the whole of
`JetAlgebra`, and are worth defining on `JetAlgebra` directly.

And then the classification of invariants of mass dimension at most four applies to *every*
element of the algebra of that dimension, with no side condition left to check. That is
the result this whole chain of files exists for, and section B states it: for an arbitrary
`x : JetAlgebra` of mass weight at most eight,

`x` is fixed by the jet gauge group and by the Lorentz group
  ↔ `x` is a combination of the constant term, the Higgs mass term `H† H`, and the
    dimension-four Standard Model Lagrangian.

Nothing is assumed of `x` beyond its mass weight: not membership of a subalgebra, not
covariance, not a bound of the form `0 < w`. Every hypothesis of the abstract statement has
discharged against the concrete algebra. The `⊔ S` form, which sets aside a submodule of
higher-dimension operators, follows as a generalization for a reader who wants one.

## ii. Key results

- `JetAlgebra.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_and_invariant_iff_lagrangian` : the theorem
  the chain exists for. For every element of the jet algebra of mass weight at most eight
  — with no other hypothesis of any kind — invariance under the jet gauge group and the
  Lorentz group holds exactly when the element is a combination of the constant term, the
  Higgs mass term `H† H`, and the dimension-four Standard Model Lagrangian.
- `JetAlgebra.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_sup_and_invariant_iff_lagrangian` : the same
  classification modulo a submodule of higher-dimension operators set aside.
- `AlgebraRealization.id` (see `AlgebraRealization.Basic`) : the jet algebra of the
  Standard Model is a Standard Model.
- `JetAlgebra.algebraRealization_fieldAlgebra_eq_top` : its field algebra is everything.
- `JetAlgebra.massWeightSubmodule`, `JetAlgebra.massWeightSubmoduleLE` : the mass-weight
  grading and its filtration, on the jet algebra itself.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The field algebra is everything
  - A.1. The field algebra
  - A.2. The collapse of the graded pieces
  - A.3. The mass-weight filtration of the jet algebra
- B. The Standard Model Lagrangian

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The field algebra is everything

The field algebra of an `AlgebraRealization` is the algebra generated by the thirteen families
of derivative symbols. On the jet algebra it is everything: a Standard Model Lagrangian
lives in an algebra in which there is nothing to write down but the fields and their
derivatives.

The consequence is that the mass-weight filtration simplifies. The graded piece
`AlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmodule n` is by definition the intersection of the field
algebra with the kernel of `massWeightPoly - X ^ n`; with the field algebra the whole
algebra the intersection is idle, and what is left is the honest weight-`n` eigenspace of
`massWeightPoly` on the whole algebra. That collapse is section A.2, stated for an
arbitrary `AlgebraRealization` whose field algebra is everything.

The weight pieces and the filtration are therefore worth having on `JetAlgebra` directly,
with no mention of an `AlgebraRealization` instance, and section A.3 gives them: a reader of
the classification of section B should not have to know that an instance exists. They are
defined by the eigenvalue equation rather than as a kernel because `Polynomial JetAlgebra`
carries no synthesizable `Ring` instance — the search does not close at this concrete
type — so the subtraction `massWeightPoly - X ^ n` can only be written at an abstract type.
The bridges of section A.3 identify the two.
### A.1. The field algebra
### A.2. The collapse of the graded pieces
### A.3. The mass-weight filtration of the jet algebra

## B. The Standard Model Lagrangian

This is what the chain was built for, and the first theorem below is the headline. Take
any element `x` of the jet algebra of mass weight at most eight — that is, of mass
dimension at most four; by section A that is a condition on `x` alone, and it is the only
hypothesis there is. Then `x` is invariant under the jet gauge group and under the Lorentz
group if and only if it is a combination of

* the constant term, of mass dimension zero;
* the Higgs mass term `H† H`, of mass dimension two;
* and the dimension-four span — the four Lorentz contractions of the three `F·F` trace
  families and of the twice-derived hypercharge field strength, among them the gauge
  kinetic and theta terms, the Higgs kinetic term, its quartic potential and its two box
  terms, the kinetic terms of the ten fermion species over the nine family pairs, and the
  six Yukawa couplings over the nine family pairs —

and nothing else. This is a statement about formal expressions: the listed terms span, but
they are not shown to be independent or nonzero, and nothing is identified modulo total
derivatives or the equations of motion.

The second theorem is the same classification with a submodule `S` set aside — the
operators of mass dimension above four, for a reader who wants to work modulo them. It is
strictly more general and strictly less readable, which is why it comes second. It keeps its
hypothesis `hScov : S ≤ covAlgebra.toSubmodule`, and that is not an oversight of the
simplification of section A. The field algebra is everything, but the covariant subalgebra
is not: a covariant element is fixed by the pure gauge jets, while the gauge potential
picks up the Maurer–Cartan shift and so is not. `covAlgebra` therefore stays a proper
subalgebra of `JetAlgebra`, and a set-aside `S` still has to be written in the covariant
towers for the classification to say anything about it.

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetAlgebra.algebraRealization_fieldAlgebra_eq_top
declarations.doc:
The fields of the Standard Model generate its jet algebra: the field algebra of the
instance is the whole of `JetAlgebra`.
declarations.statement: lemma algebraRealization_fieldAlgebra_eq_top : AlgebraRealization.id.fieldAlgebra = ⊤

declarations.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmodule_eq_ker
declarations.doc:
When the field algebra is everything the graded piece of mass weight `n` is the
weight-`n` eigenspace of `massWeightPoly` on the whole algebra: the intersection with the
field algebra in the definition of `massWeightSubmodule` cuts nothing away.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eq_ker (htop : h.fieldAlgebra = ⊤) (n : ℕ) :
    h.massWeightSubmodule n
      = LinearMap.ker (massWeightPoly.toLinearMap
        - (Polynomial.monomial n : B →ₗ[B] Polynomial B).restrictScalars ℂ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.massWeightSubmoduleLE_eq_iSup_ker
declarations.doc:
When the field algebra is everything the filtration by mass weight at most `w` is the
join of the eigenspaces of `massWeightPoly` of weight `0` through `w`, taken over the
whole algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmoduleLE_eq_iSup_ker (htop : h.fieldAlgebra = ⊤) (w : ℕ) :
    h.massWeightSubmoduleLE w
      = ⨆ k ∈ Finset.range (w + 1), LinearMap.ker (massWeightPoly.toLinearMap
          - (Polynomial.monomial k : B →ₗ[B] Polynomial B).restrictScalars ℂ)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetAlgebra.massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
The weight-`n` piece of the jet algebra, defined on the algebra itself: the eigenspace
on which `massWeightPoly` is the monomial `X ^ n`. Nothing about `AlgebraRealization` enters
the definition; that it agrees with the instance's graded piece is
`algebraRealization_massWeightSubmodule`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def massWeightSubmodule (n : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ JetAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetAlgebra.mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: Membership of the weight-`n` piece is the eigenvalue equation.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule {n : ℕ} {x : JetAlgebra} :
    x ∈ massWeightSubmodule n ↔ massWeightPoly x = Polynomial.monomial n x

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetAlgebra.massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight filtration of the jet algebra, defined on the algebra itself: the join
of the weight pieces of weight at most `w`. An element lies in it exactly when it is a
sum of eigenvectors of `massWeightPoly` of weight at most `w`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def massWeightSubmoduleLE (w : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ JetAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetAlgebra.algebraRealization_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
The graded piece defined on the jet algebra is the graded piece of the instance: the
two differ only by the intersection with the field algebra, which is everything.
declarations.statement:
lemma algebraRealization_massWeightSubmodule (n : ℕ) :
    AlgebraRealization.id.massWeightSubmodule n = massWeightSubmodule n

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetAlgebra.algebraRealization_massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.doc: The filtration defined on the jet algebra is the filtration of the instance.
declarations.statement:
lemma algebraRealization_massWeightSubmoduleLE (w : ℕ) :
    AlgebraRealization.id.massWeightSubmoduleLE w = massWeightSubmoduleLE w

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetAlgebra.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_and_invariant_iff_lagrangian
declarations.doc:
The invariant content of the Standard Model up to mass dimension four, on the jet
algebra of the Standard Model itself, with nothing set aside. An element of mass weight
at most eight is fixed by the jet gauge group and by the Lorentz group exactly when it is
a combination of the constant term, the Higgs mass term `H† H`, and the dimension-four
span: the Lorentz contractions of the gauge sector, among them the gauge kinetic and theta
terms (`IsGaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan`), the Higgs kinetic term, quartic potential
and box terms (`HiggsAlgebraCovRealization.lorentzContractionEightSpan`),
  the fermion kinetic terms
(`IsFermionSector.kineticSpan`) and the Yukawa couplings (`yukawaSpan`) — and nothing
else.

There are no other hypotheses. The mass-weight condition is a condition on `x` alone: by
`mem_massWeightSubmodule` it says that `x` is a sum of eigenvectors of `massWeightPoly`
of weight at most eight, with no demand that `x` lie in any subalgebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_and_invariant_iff_lagrangian (x : JetAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ massWeightSubmoduleLE 8
        ∧ (∀ U : JetGaugeGroupI, repJetGaugeGroupI U x = x)
        ∧ ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup Λ x = x)
      ↔ x ∈ 1
        ⊔ (AlgebraRealization.id.toCovAlgebraRealization.isHiggsSector.dotSpan 0 0
          ⊔ (AlgebraRealization.id.toCovAlgebraRealization.isGaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
           ⊔ AlgebraRealization.id.toCovAlgebraRealization.isHiggsSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
            ⊔ (AlgebraRealization.id.toCovAlgebraRealization.isFermionSector.kineticSpan
              ⊔ AlgebraRealization.id.toCovAlgebraRealization.yukawaSpan)))

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetAlgebra.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_sup_and_invariant_iff_lagrangian
declarations.doc:
The same classification as
`mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_and_invariant_iff_lagrangian`, with a submodule `S` set
aside — the operators of mass dimension above four, say. An element of
`massWeightSubmoduleLE 8 ⊔ S` is fixed by the jet gauge group and the Lorentz group
exactly when it is the Standard Model Lagrangian, the Higgs mass term and a constant, up
to a remainder in `S` fixed by both groups.

The hypothesis `hScov` does not disappear when the field algebra becomes everything: the
covariant subalgebra `covAlgebra` remains a proper subalgebra, because a covariant
element is fixed by the pure gauge jets whereas the gauge potential picks up the
Maurer–Cartan shift. A set-aside `S` therefore still has to be written in the covariant
towers, which is the case of interest — higher-dimension operators are built from
covariant derivatives and the field strength.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_eight_sup_and_invariant_iff_lagrangian
    (S : Submodule ℂ JetAlgebra)
    (hS : ∀ U : JetGaugeGroupI, ∀ y ∈ S, repJetGaugeGroupI U y ∈ S)
    (hSL : ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), ∀ y ∈ S, repLorentzGroup Λ y ∈ S)
    (hScov : S ≤ AlgebraRealization.id.covAlgebra.toSubmodule) (x : JetAlgebra) :
    (x ∈ massWeightSubmoduleLE 8 ⊔ S
        ∧ (∀ U : JetGaugeGroupI, repJetGaugeGroupI U x = x)
        ∧ ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup Λ x = x)
      ↔ ∃ y ∈ S, (∀ U : JetGaugeGroupI, repJetGaugeGroupI U y = y)
          ∧ (∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), repLorentzGroup Λ y = y)
          ∧ x - y ∈ 1
          ⊔ (AlgebraRealization.id.toCovAlgebraRealization.isHiggsSector.dotSpan 0 0
          ⊔ (AlgebraRealization.id.toCovAlgebraRealization.isGaugeSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
           ⊔ AlgebraRealization.id.toCovAlgebraRealization.isHiggsSector.lorentzContractionEightSpan
            ⊔ (AlgebraRealization.id.toCovAlgebraRealization.isFermionSector.kineticSpan
              ⊔ AlgebraRealization.id.toCovAlgebraRealization.yukawaSpan)))

modules.title: The jet algebra of the Standard Model
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The full jet algebra of the Standard Model — the algebra in which a Standard Model
Lagrangian lives — is the local field algebra of its field datum,
`StandardModel.fieldData.LocalFieldAlgebra`: the exterior algebra on the fermionic
generators of the datum, tensored with the symmetric algebra on its bosonic generators,
tensored with the complexified symmetric algebra on the connection generators. The bosonic
factors commute with everything, so the ordinary tensor product is correct; the
anticommutativity of the fermions lives entirely inside the fermionic factor, where all
fifteen species share one exterior algebra.

The three sector inclusions keep their old names and their old sources — the sector
algebras `FermionJetAlgebra`, `HiggsJetAlgebra` and `LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra GaugeAlgebra` — so
that every downstream family of field symbols is unchanged. The two matter inclusions
factor through the sector equivalences of
`PhyslibAlpha.Particles.StandardModel.JetAlgebra.SectorEquiv.Basic`; the connection sector needs
no equivalence, the two presentations of it being the same type.

This file defines the algebra and its three sector inclusions, and proves that the gauge
sector is central. The Lorentz action, the jet gauge action, the formal total derivative
and the mass-dimension scaling are assembled factorwise in the sibling files.

## ii. Key results

- `JetAlgebra` : the jet algebra of the Standard Model.
- `JetAlgebra.includeFermion`, `includeHiggs`, `includeGauge` : the sector inclusions.
- `JetAlgebra.includeGauge_commute` : the gauge sector is central.
- `JetAlgebra.includeFermion_ι`, `JetAlgebra.includeHiggs_ι`,
  `JetAlgebra.includeGauge_one_tmul_ι` : the included degree-one elements of the three
  sectors are the generic generators of the field datum.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The jet algebra of the Standard Model
  - A.1. The sector inclusions
  - A.2. Centrality of the gauge sector

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.doc:

declarations.statement: noncomputable def includeFermion : FermionJetAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] JetAlgebra

declarations.statement: noncomputable def includeHiggs : HiggsJetAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] JetAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetAlgebra.includeGauge
declarations.doc:
The inclusion of the gauge sector. The Standard Model gauge bosons are the generic
ones at `GaugeAlgebra`, so this is the connection inclusion of the datum itself.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def includeGauge :
    (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra GaugeAlgebra)) →ₐ[ℂ] JetAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetAlgebra.includeGauge_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma includeGauge_apply (y : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra GaugeAlgebra)) :
    includeGauge y = ((1 : fieldData.MatterAlgebra) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] y : JetAlgebra)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetAlgebra.includeFermion_apply_equiv
declarations.doc:
The fermionic sector inclusion factors through the sector equivalence and the generic
fermionic factor inclusion.
declarations.statement:
lemma includeFermion_apply_equiv (a : FermionJetAlgebra) :
    includeFermion a = fieldData.includeFermion (fermionAlgebraEquiv a)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetAlgebra.includeHiggs_apply_equiv
declarations.doc:
The Higgs sector inclusion factors through the sector equivalence and the generic
bosonic factor inclusion.
declarations.statement:
lemma includeHiggs_apply_equiv (h : HiggsJetAlgebra) :
    includeHiggs h = fieldData.includeBoson (higgsAlgebraEquiv h)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetAlgebra.includeGauge_eq_includeConnection
declarations.doc: The gauge sector inclusion is the generic connection factor inclusion.
declarations.statement:
lemma includeGauge_eq_includeConnection :
    includeGauge = fieldData.includeConnection

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetAlgebra.includeFermion_ι
declarations.doc:
A degree-one element of the fermionic sector, included, is a total fermionic generator
of the field datum, read through the fermionic generator identification.
declarations.statement:
lemma includeFermion_ι (v : JetComponentSpace fermionMatterField) :
    includeFermion (ExteriorAlgebra.ι ℂ v)
      = fieldData.ιFermionTotal (fermionGeneratorsEquiv.symm v)

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetAlgebra.includeHiggs_ι
declarations.doc:
A degree-one element of the Higgs sector, included, is the generator of the one bosonic
species of the field datum.
declarations.statement:
lemma includeHiggs_ι (v : JetComponentSpace HiggsVec.matterField) :
    includeHiggs (SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℂ (JetComponentSpace HiggsVec.matterField) v)
      = fieldData.ιBoson () v

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetAlgebra.includeGauge_one_tmul_ι
declarations.doc:
A real degree-one element of the gauge sector, included, is a connection generator of
the field datum: the connection factors of the two presentations are the same type, and
the complexification is the scalar one.
declarations.statement:
lemma includeGauge_one_tmul_ι (v : GaugeBoson.JetComponentSpace GaugeAlgebra) :
    includeGauge ((1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ]
        SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℝ (GaugeBoson.JetComponentSpace GaugeAlgebra) v)
      = fieldData.ιConnection v

declarations.name: StandardModel.JetAlgebra.includeGauge_commute
declarations.doc:
The image of the gauge sector is central: gauge-boson symbols commute with
everything, as bosons must.
declarations.statement:
lemma includeGauge_commute (y : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra GaugeAlgebra)) (x : JetAlgebra) :
    x * includeGauge y = includeGauge y * x

modules.title: The covariant jet algebra
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

`AlgebraRealization.covAlgebra` is the subalgebra of an algebra with a Standard Model
generated by the covariant towers — the covariant derivatives of the field strength and of
the twelve matter species. Section A records that each covariant tower lies in it.

Sections B and C make that subalgebra an algebra in its own right. The global gauge action,
the Lorentz action and the mass-weight polynomial each carry a covariant tower to a
combination of covariant towers and each is multiplicative, so each preserves the
subalgebra; restricting them gives the subalgebra a gauge action, a Lorentz action and a
mass-weight grading. The mass-weight polynomial needs the most care, since its target is
the polynomials over the subalgebra rather than the subalgebra itself.

Section D takes the case that matters. The covariant subalgebra of the *jet* algebra of
the Standard Model — that is, of `AlgebraRealization.id` — is `CovJetAlgebra`, the algebra
in which every covariant expression of the Standard Model lives and nothing else. It comes
with the global gauge action, the Lorentz action, the mass-weight polynomial and the
thirteen covariant towers, and is the covariant counterpart of `JetAlgebra`: what
`JetAlgebra` is to `AlgebraRealization`, `CovJetAlgebra` is to `CovAlgebraRealization`.

That it is itself a covariant Standard Model is
[`Sectors.lean`](Sectors.lean).

## ii. Key results

- `StandardModel.CovJetAlgebra` : the covariant jet algebra of the Standard Model.
- `StandardModel.CovJetAlgebra.repGaugeGroupI`,
  `StandardModel.CovJetAlgebra.repLorentzGroup`,
  `StandardModel.CovJetAlgebra.massWeightPoly` : its gauge action, Lorentz action and
  mass-weight polynomial.
- `StandardModel.CovJetAlgebra.fieldStrength`, `StandardModel.CovJetAlgebra.higgsField`
  and their companions : its thirteen covariant towers.
- `AlgebraRealization.repGlobal_mem_covAlgebra`,
  `AlgebraRealization.repLorentz_mem_covAlgebra`,
  `AlgebraRealization.massWeightPoly_mem_range_mapAlgHom` : the three closure facts.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The covariant towers lie in the covariant subalgebra
- B. The covariant subalgebra is closed under the actions
  - B.1. The global gauge action
  - B.2. The Lorentz action
  - B.3. The mass-weight polynomial
- C. The covariant subalgebra as an algebra in its own right
  - C.1. Corestricting a family of symbols
- D. The covariant jet algebra
- E. Transporting a law to the covariant jet algebra

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The covariant towers lie in the covariant subalgebra

## B. The covariant subalgebra is closed under the actions

The global gauge action, the Lorentz action and the mass-weight polynomial all carry a
covariant tower to a combination of covariant towers, and each is multiplicative, so each
carries the whole covariant subalgebra into itself. Those three closure facts are what let
the covariant subalgebra be regarded as an algebra with a gauge action, a Lorentz action
and a mass-weight grading of its own.
### B.1. The global gauge action
### B.2. The Lorentz action
### B.3. The mass-weight polynomial

## C. The covariant subalgebra as an algebra in its own right

The three closure facts of section B let the covariant subalgebra carry a gauge action, a
Lorentz action and a mass-weight polynomial of its own: each is the ambient one restricted,
and each is recorded here together with the lemma identifying it with the ambient one on
underlying elements. The mass-weight polynomial takes a little more care than the two
actions, because its target is the polynomials over the subalgebra rather than the
subalgebra itself; the identification is through the injection
`Polynomial.mapAlgHom h.covAlgebra.val`.
### C.1. Corestricting a family of symbols

## D. The covariant jet algebra

The covariant field algebra of the jet algebra of the Standard Model — equivalently, by
section A, its covariant subalgebra — is the algebra in which every covariant expression of
the Standard Model lives, and nothing else. It carries a global gauge action, a Lorentz
action, a mass-weight polynomial and the thirteen covariant towers, all of them the jet
algebra's own restricted to it. It is the universal object of the covariant theory in the
sense that `JetAlgebra` is the universal object of the theory in the bare symbols.

## E. Transporting a law to the covariant jet algebra

A law of the covariant jet algebra is an equation between elements of a subalgebra of the
jet algebra, so it is the jet algebra's own law under `Subtype.ext`. Three shapes need more
than that: the multiplicativity of the two actions, which is the ambient multiplicativity;
a mass-weight eigenvalue equation, whose target is the polynomials over the subalgebra; and
a Lorentz law, whose right-hand side is a sum of scalar multiples that the coercion has to
be pushed through.

declarations.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.covGenerators_induction
declarations.doc:
A property that holds of every covariant tower holds of every covariant generator:
the case analysis of the generating set, done once.
declarations.statement:
lemma covGenerators_induction {P : B → Prop}
    (hF : ∀ {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
      (φ : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra), P (h.covF l μ ν φ))
    (hH : ∀ {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ HiggsVec),
      P (h.covDerivH l φ))
    (hBarH : ∀ {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule HiggsVec)),
      P (h.covDerivBarH l φ))
    (hD : ∀ (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ DownSinglet), P (h.covDerivD i l φ))
    (hBarD : ∀ (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule DownSinglet)), P (h.covDerivBarD i l φ))
    (hU : ∀ (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ UpSinglet), P (h.covDerivU i l φ))
    (hBarU : ∀ (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule UpSinglet)), P (h.covDerivBarU i l φ))
    (hQ : ∀ (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ QuarkDoublet), P (h.covDerivQ i l φ))
    (hBarQ : ∀ (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule QuarkDoublet)), P (h.covDerivBarQ i l φ))
    (hL : ∀ (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ LeptonDoubletV), P (h.covDerivL i l φ))
    (hBarL : ∀ (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule LeptonDoubletV)), P (h.covDerivBarL i l φ))
    (hE : ∀ (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ LeptonSinglet), P (h.covDerivE i l φ))
    (hBarE : ∀ (i : Fin 3) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule LeptonSinglet)), P (h.covDerivBarE i l φ)) :
    ∀ x ∈ h.covGenerators, P x

declarations.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.mapsTo_covAlgebra
declarations.doc:
A unital multiplicative endomorphism of the algebra that carries the covariant
generators into the covariant subalgebra carries the whole subalgebra into itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma mapsTo_covAlgebra {f : B →ₗ[ℂ] B} (hone : f 1 = 1)
    (hmul : ∀ b₁ b₂ : B, f (b₁ * b₂) = f b₁ * f b₂)
    (hgen : ∀ x ∈ h.covGenerators, f x ∈ h.covAlgebra) {x : B} (hx : x ∈ h.covAlgebra) :
    f x ∈ h.covAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.repGlobal_one

declarations.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.repGlobal_mem_covAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The global gauge action preserves the covariant subalgebra: it carries each covariant
tower to a tower of the same shape at a rotated value index, and it is multiplicative.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGlobal_mem_covAlgebra (g : GaugeGroupI) {x : B} (hx : x ∈ h.covAlgebra) :
    repGlobal repJet g x ∈ h.covAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.massWeightPoly_mem_range_mapAlgHom
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight polynomial carries the covariant subalgebra into the polynomials with
coefficients in it: each covariant tower is an eigenvector whose eigenvector is the tower
itself, and the mass-weight polynomial is an algebra map.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightPoly_mem_range_mapAlgHom {x : B} (hx : x ∈ h.covAlgebra) :
    massWeightPoly x ∈ (Polynomial.mapAlgHom h.covAlgebra.val).range

declarations.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.covRepGauge

The global gauge action on the covariant subalgebra: the ambient global gauge action,
which section B shows preserves it.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def covRepGauge : Representation ℂ GaugeGroupI ↥h.covAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.coe_covRepGauge
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_covRepGauge (g : GaugeGroupI) (x : ↥h.covAlgebra) :

declarations.statement:
lemma coe_covRepLorentz (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x : ↥h.covAlgebra) :

declarations.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.mapAlgHom_val_injective

declarations.statement:

    Function.Injective (Polynomial.mapAlgHom h.covAlgebra.val)

declarations.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.covMassWeightPoly
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight polynomial of the covariant subalgebra: the ambient mass-weight
polynomial, whose value on the subalgebra has all of its coefficients in the subalgebra
by section B.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def covMassWeightPoly : ↥h.covAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] Polynomial ↥h.covAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.mapAlgHom_covMassWeightPoly
declarations.statement:
lemma mapAlgHom_covMassWeightPoly (x : ↥h.covAlgebra) :
    Polynomial.mapAlgHom h.covAlgebra.val (h.covMassWeightPoly x) = massWeightPoly (x : B)

declarations.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.covMassWeightPoly_eq_monomial_iff
declarations.doc: A mass-weight eigenvalue equation in the covariant subalgebra is the ambient one.
declarations.statement:
lemma covMassWeightPoly_eq_monomial_iff {n : ℕ} (x : ↥h.covAlgebra) :
    h.covMassWeightPoly x = Polynomial.monomial n x
      ↔ massWeightPoly (x : B) = Polynomial.monomial n (x : B)

declarations.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.corestrict
declarations.doc:
A family of symbols whose values lie in the covariant subalgebra, read as a family
valued in that subalgebra.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def corestrict {V : Type} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (G : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) (hG : ∀ φ, G φ ∈ h.covAlgebra) :
    Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] ↥h.covAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.coe_corestrict
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_corestrict {V : Type} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    (G : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) (hG : ∀ φ, G φ ∈ h.covAlgebra) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    (h.corestrict G hG φ : B) = G φ

declarations.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.corestrictReal
declarations.doc: The real-linear analogue of `corestrict`, for the gauge-algebra valued family.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def corestrictReal (G : Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (hG : ∀ φ, G φ ∈ h.covAlgebra) :
    Module.Dual ℝ GaugeAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] ↥h.covAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.AlgebraRealization.coe_corestrictReal

    (h.corestrictReal G hG φ : B) = G φ

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovJetAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The covariant jet algebra of the Standard Model: the covariant field algebra of the
jet algebra. Its elements are exactly the polynomial expressions in the covariant
derivatives of the field strength and of the twelve matter towers.
declarations.statement: abbrev CovJetAlgebra : Type

declarations.doc:
The covariant jet algebra is a ring: it is a subalgebra of the jet algebra. The
instance is given explicitly because the generic `Subalgebra.toRing` is not found by
instance search at this concrete algebra.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance : Ring CovJetAlgebra

declarations.doc:
The covariant jet algebra is a complex algebra, stated at the ring instance just
given.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance : Algebra ℂ CovJetAlgebra

declarations.name: StandardModel.CovJetAlgebra.repGaugeGroupI_mul

declarations.statement:

    repGaugeGroupI g (x * y) = repGaugeGroupI g x * repGaugeGroupI g y
